3.4.s:
3.16
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
kāvye ye'bhihitā doṣāḥ kaiścittebhyaḥ prahelikā ..
kartavyāśca tathaivānyāstāsāṃ vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam .. 1 ..
3.4.d:
3.16
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
काव्ये येऽभिहिता दोषाः कैश्चित्तेभ्यः प्रहेलिका ॥
कर्तव्याश्च तथैवान्यास्तासां वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥ 1 ॥
3.4.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Those flaws which have been mentioned in poetry by some—from them riddles / should be composed, and other kinds as well; I shall explain their characteristics.

3.4.s:
ślokenaikena vā dvābhyāṃ kartavyā tu narottama ..
na kartavyāśca tā rājanbahuślokanibandhanāḥ .. 2 ..
3.4.d:
श्लोकेनैकेन वा द्वाभ्यां कर्तव्या तु नरोत्तम ॥
न कर्तव्याश्च ता राजन्बहुश्लोकनिबन्धनाः ॥ 2 ॥
3.4.m: It should be composed in one verse or two, O best of men; / they should not be composed with an arrangement of many verses, O king.

3.4.s:
tasyāṃ mātrāvaśādartho gopyate sā samāgatā ..
paryāyavacanādyasyāṃ vanditā sā prakīrtitā .. 3 ..
3.4.d:
तस्यां मात्रावशादर्थो गोप्यते सा समागता ॥
पर्यायवचनाद्यस्यां वन्दिता सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 3 ॥
3.4.m: That [riddle] in which the meaning is concealed by virtue of morae is [called] Samāgatā; / that in which [the meaning is concealed] through synonyms is proclaimed as Vanditā.

3.4.s:
vṛttāntagopikāntāyā padairvyavahitairbhavet ..
aprasiddhaistu paryāyairduḥkhitā nāma sā smṛtā .. 4 ..
3.4.d:
वृत्तान्तगोपिकान्ताया पदैर्व्यवहितैर्भवेत् ॥
अप्रसिद्धैस्तु पर्यायैर्दुःखिता नाम सा स्मृता ॥ 4 ॥
3.4.m: That which conceals the story by words that are separated [is known as Vṛttāntagopikā]; / while that which [does so] through unfamiliar synonyms is remembered as Duḥkhitā.

3.4.s:
kalpanāgopitārthāttu kathitā parihāsikā ..
samānarūpatulyārtho śabdairanyaiḥ prakīrtitā .. 5 ..
3.4.d:
कल्पनागोपितार्थात्तु कथिता परिहासिका ॥
समानरूपतुल्यार्थो शब्दैरन्यैः प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 5 ॥
3.4.m: That whose meaning is concealed by imagination is declared to be Parihāsikā; / that which has a similar form and identical meaning expressed by other words is proclaimed [as Samānarūpā].

3.4.s:
durbodhākṣarabandhā ca paruṣā nāmataḥ smṛtā..
saṃkhyāmātrasamānatvātsaṃkhyātākhyā tathocyate .. 6 ..
3.4.d:
दुर्बोधाक्षरबन्धा च परुषा नामतः स्मृता॥
संख्यामात्रसमानत्वात्संख्याताख्या तथोच्यते ॥ 6 ॥
3.4.m: That which has a composition of obscure syllables is remembered by the name Paruṣā; / that which is called Saṃkhyātā is spoken of thus on account of identity in mere number.

3.4.s:
arthāntarānkalpanayā kalpitā ca tathocyate ..
anyasya saṃjñāyāmohānnamāntaritasaṃjñitā ..7..
3.4.d:
अर्थान्तरान्कल्पनया कल्पिता च तथोच्यते ॥
अन्यस्य संज्ञायामोहान्नमान्तरितसंज्ञिता ॥7॥
3.4.m: That formed through the imagining of another meaning is spoken of as [Kalpitā]; / because of confusion regarding the name of another, [a riddle] is designated Nāmāntaritā.

3.4.s:
arthavyāmohataḥ proktā nibhṛtā ca mahānṛpa ..
samānaśabdā kathitā tulyaśabdanibandhanā ..8..
3.4.d:
अर्थव्यामोहतः प्रोक्ता निभृता च महानृप ॥
समानशब्दा कथिता तुल्यशब्दनिबन्धना ॥8॥
3.4.m: From confusion of meaning, O great king, [a riddle] is said to be Nibhṛtā; / that which is constructed with identical words is declared to be Samānaśabdā.

3.4.s:
arthānulomadurbodhā vyāmūḍheti tathocyate ..
gucchākhyā kathitā vṛtte nānābandhani bandhanā .. 9 ..
3.4.d:
अर्थानुलोमदुर्बोधा व्यामूढेति तथोच्यते ॥
गुच्छाख्या कथिता वृत्ते नानाबन्धनि बन्धना ॥ 9 ॥
3.4.m: That which is hard to understand even though the meaning runs naturally is spoken of as Vyāmūḍhā; / that constructed with various meters in a stanza is declared to be named Gucchā.

3.4.s:
ekobhayabahucchanne yathārthaparigopite ..
saṃkīrṇā sambhavopetā yā tadarthakarī bhavet .. 3.16.10 ..
3.4.d:
एकोभयबहुच्छन्ने यथार्थपरिगोपिते ॥
संकीर्णा सम्भवोपेता या तदर्थकरी भवेत् ॥ 3.16.10 ॥
3.4.m: When one, both, or many [meanings] are concealed, properly hidden in their real sense, / [a riddle] that possesses plausibility and conveys that meaning is Saṃkīrṇā.

3.4.s:
tadarthakārī yatrārtho jñāyate'nyārthakāmukaḥ ..
rājañśabdavaśātsā ca kathitā vyabhicāriṇī .. 11 ..
3.4.d:
तदर्थकारी यत्रार्थो ज्ञायतेऽन्यार्थकामुकः ॥
राजञ्शब्दवशात्सा च कथिता व्यभिचारिणी ॥ 11 ॥
3.4.m: Where an expression conveying its own sense is understood as desiring another meaning / through the power of words, O king, that is declared to be Vyabhicāriṇī.

3.4.s:
ukterthe vṛttabandhena mātrābhiḥ sthāpitā tathā ..
naṣṭārthā vā ca sā proktā vṛttabandhanidarśitā .. 12 ..
3.4.d:
उक्तेर्थे वृत्तबन्धेन मात्राभिः स्थापिता तथा ॥
नष्टार्था वा च सा प्रोक्ता वृत्तबन्धनिदर्शिता ॥ 12 ॥
3.4.m: When the stated meaning is fixed by metrical form and by morae, / that is declared to be Naṣṭārthā, illustrated through metrical composition.

3.4.s:
naṣṭākṣarā tu kathitā vinaikena tadārthadā ..
anyārthatā tathaivoktā varṇabhraṣṭā nareśvara .. 13 ..
3.4.d:
नष्टाक्षरा तु कथिता विनैकेन तदार्थदा ॥
अन्यार्थता तथैवोक्ता वर्णभ्रष्टा नरेश्वर ॥ 13 ॥
3.4.m: That which yields its meaning when deprived of one syllable is called Naṣṭākṣarā; / that which likewise yields another meaning is said to be Varṇabhraṣṭā, O lord of men.

3.4.s:
kālasya rūparūpāṇāṃ vyākhyānena tadārthadā ..
bījamātreṇa leśākhyā bhūmipāla prakīrtitā .. 14 ..
3.4.d:
कालस्य रूपरूपाणां व्याख्यानेन तदार्थदा ॥
बीजमात्रेण लेशाख्या भूमिपाल प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 14 ॥
3.4.m: That which yields its meaning through explanation of time and various forms, / [or] by a mere hint, O protector of the earth, is proclaimed as named Leśā.

3.4.s:
aślīlametāsvapi naiva kāryaṃ tadvarjyamāhuḥ kavayo narendra ..
udvejanīyaṃ tu satāṃ taduktamaślīlabandhaṃ sukhadaṃ na kāvyam .. 15 ..
3.17
.. vajra uvāca .. ..
mantrāḥ sabrāhmaṇāḥ proktāstadarthaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ smṛtam ..
kalpanā ca tathā kalpaḥ kalpaśca brāhmaṇastathā .. 1 ..
kathitāni tathārthāni purāṇaṃ ca tathā dvija ..
prakriyā prathamaḥ pādaḥ kathāvastuparigrahaḥ .. 2 ..
upodghātānuṣaṅgau ca tathā saṃhāra eva ca ..
catuṣpādaṃ hi kathitaṃ purāṇaṃ bhṛgunandana .. 3 ..
sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca ..
vaṃśānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam .. 4 ..
tatra vā viditaṃ sarvaṃ tatroktaṃ gītalakṣaṇam ..
vṛttasya lakṣaṇaṃ caiva nāṭakākhyānalakṣaṇam .. 5 ..
tasmādahaṃ tvāṃ pṛcchāmi dvija nāṭyasya lakṣaṇam ..
sabhedaṃ tanmamācakṣva sarvajño'si yataḥ prabho..6..
3.4.d:
अश्लीलमेतास्वपि नैव कार्यं तद्वर्ज्यमाहुः कवयो नरेन्द्र ॥
उद्वेजनीयं तु सतां तदुक्तमश्लीलबन्धं सुखदं न काव्यम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.17
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥ ॥
मन्त्राः सब्राह्मणाः प्रोक्तास्तदर्थं ब्राह्मणं स्मृतम् ॥
कल्पना च तथा कल्पः कल्पश्च ब्राह्मणस्तथा ॥ 1 ॥
कथितानि तथार्थानि पुराणं च तथा द्विज ॥
प्रक्रिया प्रथमः पादः कथावस्तुपरिग्रहः ॥ 2 ॥
उपोद्घातानुषङ्गौ च तथा संहार एव च ॥
चतुष्पादं हि कथितं पुराणं भृगुनन्दन ॥ 3 ॥
सर्गश्च प्रतिसर्गश्च वंशो मन्वन्तराणि च ॥
वंशानुचरितं चैव पुराणं पञ्चलक्षणम् ॥ 4 ॥
तत्र वा विदितं सर्वं तत्रोक्तं गीतलक्षणम् ॥
वृत्तस्य लक्षणं चैव नाटकाख्यानलक्षणम् ॥ 5 ॥
तस्मादहं त्वां पृच्छामि द्विज नाट्यस्य लक्षणम् ॥
सभेदं तन्ममाचक्ष्व सर्वज्ञोऽसि यतः प्रभो॥6॥
3.4.m:
Even in these, vulgarity must never be introduced; poets say that is to be avoided, O ruler of men. / For that which is distressing to the virtuous is said to be [vulgar]; a poem with vulgar composition brings no pleasure.
Vajra said: / Mantras along with Brāhmaṇas have been spoken of, and the Brāhmaṇa is considered to explain their meaning; / so also ritual arrangement and the Kalpa, and the Kalpa is like the Brāhmaṇa.
Likewise, their meanings and the Purāṇa have been told, O twice-born one. / The first quarter is Prakriyā, the adoption of the narrative subject matter;
and Upodghāta, Anuṣaṅga, and likewise Saṃhāra— / indeed, the Purāṇa is declared to have four quarters, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Creation, secondary creation, genealogy, the Manvantaras, / and the history of dynasties—the Purāṇa has these five characteristics.
All that is known therein; therein the definition of song was stated, / as well as the definition of meter, and the definition of dramatic narratives.
Therefore I ask you, O twice-born one, about the characteristics of drama; / explain that to me along with its divisions, since you are omniscient, O lord.

3.4.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
itihāsānusāreṇa purāṇānāṃ samīkṣitam ..
caritaṃ tridaśānāṃ vā nāṭakaṃ tatra kīrtitam..7..
ekanāyakasaṃyuktaṃ nāyakapratināyakaiḥ.
saṃyuktamathavā kāryaḥ kāvye vai tatra nāyakaḥ ..8..
sarvāstu vṛttayastatra tatra sarve tathā rasāḥ ..
kālaprayogaṃ ca tathā yuktyā saṃdarśayennṛpa ..9..
pañcāvarāṅkaṃ tatproktaṃ tathādaśaparaṃ śubham ..
ekadaivatikaṃ vṛttamaṅke rājanpradarśayeta .. 3.17.10 ..
tadante sarvapātrāṇāṃ niṣkramaśca vidhīyate ..
yuktyupanyāsasaṃyuktaṃ tathā niṣkamaṇaṃ matam ..11..
maraṇaṃ rājyavibhraṃśo nagarasyoparodhanam ..
etāni darśayennāṃke tathā yuddhaṃ ca pārthiva .. 12 ..
praveśakena kartavyaṃ teṣāmākhyānakaṃ budhaiḥ ..
pātradvayena kartavyaṃ tathā nityaṃ praveśakam .. 13 ..
3.4.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इतिहासानुसारेण पुराणानां समीक्षितम् ॥
चरितं त्रिदशानां वा नाटकं तत्र कीर्तितम्॥7॥
एकनायकसंयुक्तं नायकप्रतिनायकैः।
संयुक्तमथवा कार्यः काव्ये वै तत्र नायकः ॥8॥
सर्वास्तु वृत्तयस्तत्र तत्र सर्वे तथा रसाः ॥
कालप्रयोगं च तथा युक्त्या संदर्शयेन्नृप ॥9॥
पञ्चावराङ्कं तत्प्रोक्तं तथादशपरं शुभम् ॥
एकदैवतिकं वृत्तमङ्के राजन्प्रदर्शयेत ॥ 3.17.10 ॥
तदन्ते सर्वपात्राणां निष्क्रमश्च विधीयते ॥
युक्त्युपन्याससंयुक्तं तथा निष्कमणं मतम् ॥11॥
मरणं राज्यविभ्रंशो नगरस्योपरोधनम् ॥
एतानि दर्शयेन्नांके तथा युद्धं च पार्थिव ॥ 12 ॥
प्रवेशकेन कर्तव्यं तेषामाख्यानकं बुधैः ॥
पात्रद्वयेन कर्तव्यं तथा नित्यं प्रवेशकम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.4.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Drama is proclaimed therein as that which examines the deeds of the gods / or [human heroes] in accordance with Itihāsa and the Purāṇas.
It may be provided with a single hero, or provided with a hero and a rival hero; / the hero should be made [prominent] in that poetic work.
All dramatic styles are to be employed therein, likewise all rasas therein; / and one should appropriately demonstrate the passage of time, O king.
It is stated to have a minimum of five acts, and auspiciously a maximum of ten; / in an act, O king, one should show an incident concerning a single principal deity.
At the end of it, the exit of all characters is prescribed; / their exit is considered proper when connected with an appropriate dramatic pretext.
Death, loss of a kingdom, the siege of a city, / and likewise battle—these one should not show in an act, O king.
The wise should present the narrative of these through an introductory scene; / an introductory scene should always be performed by two characters.

3.4.s:
pātre parijane tatra kartavyaṃ nāyakena tu ..
bhinnaṃ pātradvayaṃ yatra tatra viṣkambhakaṃ smṛtam ..14..
tayorante tu kartavyā tathā raṅgasya śūnyatā ..
aṅgānte ca tathā kāryā na kāryā sānyathā bhavet .. 15 ..
3.4.d:
पात्रे परिजने तत्र कर्तव्यं नायकेन तु ॥
भिन्नं पात्रद्वयं यत्र तत्र विष्कम्भकं स्मृतम् ॥14॥
तयोरन्ते तु कर्तव्या तथा रङ्गस्य शून्यता ॥
अङ्गान्ते च तथा कार्या न कार्या सान्यथा भवेत् ॥ 15 ॥
3.4.m:
There it should be performed by [minor] characters or attendants of the hero; / where two different characters [of intermediate rank] are used, that is remembered as a Viṣkambhaka.
At the conclusion of both, the stage should be left empty; / likewise it should be made [empty] at the end of an act; it should not be otherwise.

3.4.s:
bahudaivatikaṃ vṛttaṃ kartavyaṃ tu praveśakam ..
saṃkṣapoktiśca kartavyā kartavyo nahi vistaraḥ .. 16 ..
3.4.d:
बहुदैवतिकं वृत्तं कर्तव्यं तु प्रवेशकम् ॥
संक्षपोक्तिश्च कर्तव्या कर्तव्यो नहि विस्तरः ॥ 16 ॥
3.4.m: An introductory scene, however, should treat an action involving many deities; / it should be composed with concise speech; extensive detail must not be made.

3.4.s:
prakhyātanāyakavadhaṃ na ca tatra praveśayet..
tasya prakāśanaṃ kāryamaṅkepyeva narādhipa .. 17 ..
3.4.d:
प्रख्यातनायकवधं न च तत्र प्रवेशयेत्॥
तस्य प्रकाशनं कार्यमङ्केप्येव नराधिप ॥ 17 ॥
3.4.m: And one should not introduce therein the slaying of a celebrated hero; / its revelation should be made only in an act, O ruler of men.

3.4.s:
nāyakābhyudayaḥ kāryo nāṭakānte tathaiva ca ..
bahvyo'pi nāyikā yatra tāsāmapi tathā bhavet .. 18 ..
3.4.d:
नायकाभ्युदयः कार्यो नाटकान्ते तथैव च ॥
बह्व्योऽपि नायिका यत्र तासामपि तथा भवेत् ॥ 18 ॥
3.4.m: Likewise, the prosperity of the hero should be brought about at the end of the drama; / where there are many heroines, the same should also happen for them.

3.4.s:
evaṃvidhā saśṛṅgārā caturaṅkāḥ tu nāṭikā ..
kṛtaṃ prakaraṇaṃ tadvatsvayamutpādya vastunā .. 19 ..
3.4.d:
एवंविधा सशृङ्गारा चतुरङ्काः तु नाटिका ॥
कृतं प्रकरणं तद्वत्स्वयमुत्पाद्य वस्तुना ॥ 19 ॥
3.4.m: A nāṭikā of this kind has four acts and is accompanied by the erotic sentiment. / Likewise, a prakaraṇa is composed with its plot invented by the poet himself.

3.4.s:
brāhmaṇo nāyakastatra vaṇikca nṛpasattama ..
evaṃ prakaraṇī kāryā caturaṅkāpi sā bhavet .. 3.17.20 ..
3.4.d:
ब्राह्मणो नायकस्तत्र वणिक्च नृपसत्तम ॥
एवं प्रकरणी कार्या चतुरङ्कापि सा भवेत् ॥ 3.17.20 ॥
3.4.m: A brahmin or a merchant is the hero in that, O best of kings. / In this way a prakaraṇī should be made, and it too should have four acts.

3.4.s:
itihāsānubandho vā svayamutpādya vā kṛtaḥ ..
bhāratīkaruṇaprāyo nivṛttaṃ samanantaram .. 21 ..
3.4.d:
इतिहासानुबन्धो वा स्वयमुत्पाद्य वा कृतः ॥
भारतीकरुणप्रायो निवृत्तं समनन्तरम् ॥ 21 ॥
3.4.m: Whether connected to traditional history or invented by the author himself, / consisting predominantly of the verbal style and pathos, whose action ceases immediately thereafter,

3.4.s:
catuṣṭayāṅkaḥ kartavyo divyanāyakavartitaḥ ..
itihāsānusāreṇa prāṇaścaikāhikaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 22 ..
3.4.d:
चतुष्टयाङ्कः कर्तव्यो दिव्यनायकवर्तितः ॥
इतिहासानुसारेण प्राणश्चैकाहिकः स्मृतः ॥ 22 ॥
3.4.m: it should be made in four acts, enacted by a divine hero. / Based on traditional history, its duration is taught to be limited to a single day.

3.4.s:
ekāṃko yuddhabahulasvātmaśaṃsāparastathā ..
ākāśakathanairyuktastvekapātrakṛtakriyaḥ .. 23 ..
3.4.d:
एकांको युद्धबहुलस्वात्मशंसापरस्तथा ॥
आकाशकथनैर्युक्तस्त्वेकपात्रकृतक्रियः ॥ 23 ॥
3.4.m: Consisting of a single act, full of fighting, devoted to self-praise, / joined with aerial discourses, its action performed by a single character—

3.4.s:
proktaḥ samavatārākhyastridaśāsuranāyakaḥ ..
triśṛṅgārastrikapaṭastathā dvādaśanāyakaḥ .. 24 ..
3.4.d:
प्रोक्तः समवताराख्यस्त्रिदशासुरनायकः ॥
त्रिशृङ्गारस्त्रिकपटस्तथा द्वादशनायकः ॥ 24 ॥
3.4.m: [this] is called the samavakāra, having gods and demons as its heroes, / having three varieties of the erotic sentiment, three deceptions, and twelve heroes.

3.4.s:
īhāmṛgo'tha bahvaṅkastathā gandharvanāyakaḥ ..
śṛṅgārabahulaḥ kāryo'tṛpta yonirasāśrayaḥ .. 25 ..
3.4.d:
ईहामृगोऽथ बह्वङ्कस्तथा गन्धर्वनायकः ॥
शृङ्गारबहुलः कार्योऽतृप्त योनिरसाश्रयः ॥ 25 ॥
3.4.m: Then the īhāmṛga has many acts and has a gandharva as its hero; / it should be filled with the erotic sentiment, resting on an unsatisfied, divine source of aesthetic experience.

3.4.s:
aikāhiko dṛptaraso vyāyogaścaikanāyakaḥ ..
vīthī trayodaśāṅkā syāttathā nāyakavarjitā ..26 ..
3.4.d:
ऐकाहिको दृप्तरसो व्यायोगश्चैकनायकः ॥
वीथी त्रयोदशाङ्का स्यात्तथा नायकवर्जिता ॥26 ॥
3.4.m: The vyāyoga lasts a single day, has an arrogant aesthetic tone, and has a single hero; / the vīthī should have thirteen divisions and is destitute of a [major] hero.

3.4.s:
ḍimākhyaśca tathā prokto rasastu suranāyakaḥ ..
tathā raudrarasaprāyaḥ prakhyastaviṣayānvitaḥ .. 27 ..
3.4.d:
डिमाख्यश्च तथा प्रोक्तो रसस्तु सुरनायकः ॥
तथा रौद्ररसप्रायः प्रख्यस्तविषयान्वितः ॥ 27 ॥
3.4.m: And that which is called a ḍima is declared to have gods as its heroes; / likewise, it is predominantly filled with the furious sentiment and is endowed with an illustrious subject matter.

3.4.s:
ekāṅko hāsyabahulastathaivodāttanāyakaḥ ..
kāryaḥ prahasanākhyastu veśyāviṭasamanvitaḥ .. 28 ..
3.4.d:
एकाङ्को हास्यबहुलस्तथैवोदात्तनायकः ॥
कार्यः प्रहसनाख्यस्तु वेश्याविटसमन्वितः ॥ 28 ॥
3.4.m: Consisting of a single act, abundant in comedy, and with an exalted hero— / that drama called prahasana should be made, joined with courtesans and rogues.

3.4.s:
sūtradhārasya vākyena kāvyavastunibandhanam ..
sarvaṃ prakāśayedādau sarveṣveteṣu vastu yat .. 29 ..
3.4.d:
सूत्रधारस्य वाक्येन काव्यवस्तुनिबन्धनम् ॥
सर्वं प्रकाशयेदादौ सर्वेष्वेतेषु वस्तु यत् ॥ 29 ॥
3.4.m: Through the words of the stage-manager, the composition of the poetic plot— / he should illuminate at the beginning whatever entire plot exists in all of these.

3.4.s:
saṃskataṃ nāyakavaco liṅgiśrotriyabhūbhujām ..
dvijanmanāṃ surāṇāṃ ca daityagandharvabhoginām .. 3.17.30 ..
3.4.d:
संस्कतं नायकवचो लिङ्गिश्रोत्रियभूभुजाम् ॥
द्विजन्मनां सुराणां च दैत्यगन्धर्वभोगिनाम् ॥ 3.17.30 ॥
3.4.m: Sanskrit is the speech of heroes, ascetics, Vedic scholars, and kings, / of twice-born men, of gods, and of serpent-demons and gandharvas.

3.4.s:
nāyikādevarāmāṇāṃ vyājaliṅgavatāṃ tathā ..
vidūṣakāṇāṃ ca bhavetprākṛtaṃ vacanaṃ nṛpa .. 31 ..
3.4.d:
नायिकादेवरामाणां व्याजलिङ्गवतां तथा ॥
विदूषकाणां च भवेत्प्राकृतं वचनं नृप ॥ 31 ॥
3.4.m: The speech of heroines, of younger brothers-in-law, and of women, / as well as of hypocritical ascetics and jesters, should be Prakrit, O king.

3.4.s:
bālastrīnīcaṣaṇḍānāṃ ye cānye nānukīrtitāḥ ..
teṣāṃ vākyamapabhraṣṭaṃ tacca jñātvā prayojayet .. 32 ..
3.4.d:
बालस्त्रीनीचषण्डानां ये चान्ये नानुकीर्तिताः ॥
तेषां वाक्यमपभ्रष्टं तच्च ज्ञात्वा प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 32 ॥
3.4.m: Of children, women, the low-born, eunuchs, and whoever else have not been mentioned— / their speech is corrupt [vernacular]; knowing that, one should employ it.

3.4.s:
svayamutpāditānāṃ me nānātvaṃ śṛṇu lakṣaṇam ..
śarma varmadhanānyante varṇānāṃ dāsavattathā .. 33 ..
3.4.d:
स्वयमुत्पादितानां मे नानात्वं शृणु लक्षणम् ॥
शर्म वर्मधनान्यन्ते वर्णानां दासवत्तथा ॥ 33 ॥
3.4.m: Listen from me to the distinctive characteristics of names invented by oneself: / [the names] of the castes should end in -śarman, -varman, -dhana, and like -dāsa.

3.4.s:
rājñāṃ vikramasaṃyuktamamātyānāṃ tathā bhavet ..
strīṇāṃ sukhodyamakrūraṃ nāyikānāṃ manoharam .. 34 ..
3.4.d:
राज्ञां विक्रमसंयुक्तममात्यानां तथा भवेत् ॥
स्त्रीणां सुखोद्यमक्रूरं नायिकानां मनोहरम् ॥ 34 ॥
3.4.m: [The names] of kings should be connected with valor; those of ministers should be likewise. / For women, they should be easy to pronounce and unharsh; for heroines, delightful.

3.4.s:
rājñīparijanastrīṇāṃ kalākauśalasaṃyutam ..
rājñaḥ parijanastrīṇāṃ vijayottaramiṣyate .. 35 ..
3.4.d:
राज्ञीपरिजनस्त्रीणां कलाकौशलसंयुतम् ॥
राज्ञः परिजनस्त्रीणां विजयोत्तरमिष्यते ॥ 35 ॥
3.4.m: For the female attendants of the queen, they should be connected with skill in arts; / for the female attendants of the king, [a name] ending in victory is desired.

3.4.s:
sāṃvatsarāṇāṃ māṅgalyaṃ śāntiprāyaṃ purodhasām ..
śūraprāyamamātyānāmāyupyaṃ bhiṣajāmapi .. 36 ..
3.4.d:
सांवत्सराणां माङ्गल्यं शान्तिप्रायं पुरोधसाम् ॥
शूरप्रायममात्यानामायुप्यं भिषजामपि ॥ 36 ॥
3.4.m: For astrologers, [a name] denoting auspiciousness; for royal priests, mostly denoting peace; / for ministers, mostly denoting heroism; and for physicians, denoting longevity.

3.4.s:
viṭānāṃ bhūṣaṇaprāyaṃ dāsīnāṃ kusumādikam ..
ṛṣigotradharau kāryau kañcukīyavidūṣakau .. 37 ..
3.4.d:
विटानां भूषणप्रायं दासीनां कुसुमादिकम् ॥
ऋषिगोत्रधरौ कार्यौ कञ्चुकीयविदूषकौ ॥ 37 ॥
3.4.m: For gallants, mostly denoting ornaments; for female servants, flowers and the like. / The chamberlain and the jester should be made to bear the gotra of a sage.

3.4.s:
dattā mitrā tathā senā vaiśyā nāma tato bhavet ..
adhikārānurūpāṇi tathā caivādhikāriṇām .. 38 ..
3.4.d:
दत्ता मित्रा तथा सेना वैश्या नाम ततो भवेत् ॥
अधिकारानुरूपाणि तथा चैवाधिकारिणाम् ॥ 38 ॥
3.4.m: -dattā, -mitrā, and likewise -senā may then be the name of a vaiśya woman. / And [the names] of officials should be in accordance with their office.

3.4.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yena vācyastu yo yathā ..
deveti rājā vaktavyo bhṛtyaiḥ prakṛtibhistathā .. 39 ..
3.4.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि येन वाच्यस्तु यो यथा ॥
देवेति राजा वक्तव्यो भृत्यैः प्रकृतिभिस्तथा ॥ 39 ॥
3.4.m: Hereafter I shall declare by whom who should be addressed and in what manner: / A king should be addressed as 'Lord' by servants and by subjects;

3.4.s:
rājeti viprairvaktavyo ṛṣibhirnāmagotrataḥ ..
apatyapratyayāddevairvayasyeti samo janaḥ .. 3.17.40 ..
3.4.d:
राजेति विप्रैर्वक्तव्यो ऋषिभिर्नामगोत्रतः ॥
अपत्यप्रत्ययाद्देवैर्वयस्येति समो जनः ॥ 3.17.40 ॥
3.4.m: as 'King' by brahmins; by sages by name and gotra; / by gods with reference to his lineage; and an equal person with 'Friend'.

3.4.s:
vidūṣako'pi vaktavyo vayasya iti nāyakaiḥ ..
āyuṣmāniti sūtena rathī vācyastathā bhavet ..41 ..
3.4.d:
विदूषकोऽपि वक्तव्यो वयस्य इति नायकैः ॥
आयुष्मानिति सूतेन रथी वाच्यस्तथा भवेत् ॥41 ॥
3.4.m: The jester also should be addressed as 'Friend' by heroes. / The warrior in the chariot should be addressed as 'Long-lived one' by the charioteer.

3.4.s:
bhagavanniti vaktavyā ṛṣayo guravaḥ surāḥ ..
putra vatseti śiṣyasya tathā vā nāmagotrataḥ .. 42 ..
3.4.d:
भगवन्निति वक्तव्या ऋषयो गुरवः सुराः ॥
पुत्र वत्सेति शिष्यस्य तथा वा नामगोत्रतः ॥ 42 ॥
3.4.m: Sages, teachers, and gods should be addressed as 'Reverend Sir'. / A student should be addressed as 'Son', 'Child', or by name and gotra.

3.4.s:
āryaputreti vaktavyaḥ striyā bhartā narādhipa ..
nāmnā bhāryā tu vaktavyā rājñī devīti nāyikā .. 43 ..
3.4.d:
आर्यपुत्रेति वक्तव्यः स्त्रिया भर्ता नराधिप ॥
नाम्ना भार्या तु वक्तव्या राज्ञी देवीति नायिका ॥ 43 ॥
3.4.m: A husband should be addressed by his wife as 'Son of an Aryan', O ruler of men. / A wife, however, should be addressed by name; a queen and a heroine as 'My Lady'.

3.4.s:
pitā tātastathā vācyo mātuścaivāryakaḥ pitā ..
yuvarājaḥ kumāraḥ syānmānyo bhāvaḥ samīritaḥ .. 44 ..
3.4.d:
पिता तातस्तथा वाच्यो मातुश्चैवार्यकः पिता ॥
युवराजः कुमारः स्यान्मान्यो भावः समीरितः ॥ 44 ॥
3.4.m: A father should be addressed as 'Dear Father', and a mother's father as 'Respected Elder'. / A crown prince should be 'Prince'; an honorable man is addressed as 'Noble Sir'.

3.4.s:
mānyamānastathā bhāmo bhartṛdāraḥ kumārakaḥ ..
haleti tu samānā strī vaktavyā samayā tathā .. 45 ..
3.4.d:
मान्यमानस्तथा भामो भर्तृदारः कुमारकः ॥
हलेति तु समाना स्त्री वक्तव्या समया तथा ॥ 45 ॥
3.4.m: An esteemed person is likewise 'Noble Sir', and a master's son is 'Prince'. / An equal woman should be addressed by an equal as 'Friend' (halā).

3.4.s:
hañjetyāmantrayennārī haṇḍe parijane svake ..
svaseti bhaginī vācyā liṅgasthā vratinī tathā .. 46 ..
3.4.d:
हञ्जेत्यामन्त्रयेन्नारी हण्डे परिजने स्वके ॥
स्वसेति भगिनी वाच्या लिङ्गस्था व्रतिनी तथा ॥ 46 ॥
3.4.m: One should address a [maid]servant as 'hañje', and one's own servant girl as 'haṇḍe'. / A sister should be addressed as 'Sister', and an ascetic woman as 'Lady of Vows'.

3.4.s:
āryeti brāhmaṇī vācyā śeṣā liṅgārthatastathā ..
antaḥpuracaro yastu strībhogaparivarjitaḥ .. 47 ..
3.4.d:
आर्येति ब्राह्मणी वाच्या शेषा लिङ्गार्थतस्तथा ॥
अन्तःपुरचरो यस्तु स्त्रीभोगपरिवर्जितः ॥ 47 ॥
3.4.m: A brahmin woman should be addressed as 'Noble Lady', and others according to the sense of their sectarian attire. / But he who walks within the inner apartments, devoid of the enjoyment of women,

3.4.s:
sa tu varṣadharo jñeyastadadhyakṣastu kañcukiḥ ..
brāhmaṇaḥ sa bhaved vṛddho mānyaśca vasudhādhipaiḥ .. 48 ..
3.4.d:
स तु वर्षधरो ज्ञेयस्तदध्यक्षस्तु कञ्चुकिः ॥
ब्राह्मणः स भवेद् वृद्धो मान्यश्च वसुधाधिपैः ॥ 48 ॥
3.4.m: he should be known as an eunuch, and their supervisor is the chamberlain; / he should be an elderly brahmin and honored by rulers of the earth.

3.4.s:
vidūṣako brāhmaṇaḥ syānnāyakasya rahasyavit ..
naṭaḥ pradhānaḥ sa bhavetsūtradhāro narādhipa .. 49 ..
3.4.d:
विदूषको ब्राह्मणः स्यान्नायकस्य रहस्यवित् ॥
नटः प्रधानः स भवेत्सूत्रधारो नराधिप ॥ 49 ॥
3.4.m: The jester should be a brahmin who knows the secrets of the hero. / The foremost actor is the stage-manager, O ruler of men.

3.4.s:
jñeyā bījasamutpattirmukhaṃ nānā rasodbhavaḥ ..
mukhotthabījodghaṭanaṃ tathā pratimukhaṃ smṛtam .. 3.17.50 ..
3.4.d:
ज्ञेया बीजसमुत्पत्तिर्मुखं नाना रसोद्भवः ॥
मुखोत्थबीजोद्घटनं तथा प्रतिमुखं स्मृतम् ॥ 3.17.50 ॥
3.4.m: The origin of the seed is to be known as the opening (mukha), from which various sentiments arise. / The unfolding of the seed that arose in the opening is taught as the progression (pratimukha).

3.4.s:
prāpyāprātiyuto garbhastasyaivodbhedasaṃjñitaḥ ..
tadevodbhinnabījārtho visargo vyasanānvitaḥ .. 51 ..
3.4.d:
प्राप्याप्रातियुतो गर्भस्तस्यैवोद्भेदसंज्ञितः ॥
तदेवोद्भिन्नबीजार्थो विसर्गो व्यसनान्वितः ॥ 51 ॥
3.4.m: Joined with attainment and non-attainment, the development (garbha) is designated as its burgeoning. / The pause (avamarśa/visarga) is connected with calamity, when the purpose of the sprouted seed [is endangered].

3.4.s:
mukhādīnāṃ nirvahaṇaṃ tathā nirvahataṃ bhavet ..
nāṭake saprakaraṇe kartavyāḥ pātrasandhayaḥ .. 52 ..
3.4.d:
मुखादीनां निर्वहणं तथा निर्वहतं भवेत् ॥
नाटके सप्रकरणे कर्तव्याः पात्रसन्धयः ॥ 52 ॥
3.4.m: The conclusion (nirvahaṇa) of the opening and the other [junctures] is the denouement. / In a nāṭaka along with a prakaraṇa, the dramatic junctures must be constructed with suitable characters.

3.4.s:
ḍime samavakāre ca visargaṃ naiva kārayet ..
vyāyogehāmṛgau kāryo tathā garbhavivarjitau .. 53 ..
3.4.d:
डिमे समवकारे च विसर्गं नैव कारयेत् ॥
व्यायोगेहामृगौ कार्यो तथा गर्भविवर्जितौ ॥ 53 ॥
3.4.m: In a ḍima and a samavakāra, one should never employ the pause. / The vyāyoga and īhāmṛga should be constructed without the development.

3.4.s:
utsṛṣṭāṅka prahasanaṃ vīthī bhāṇakameva ca ..
eteṣāṃ nāvakartavyaṃ tathā pratimukhaṃ nṛpa .. 54 ..
3.4.d:
उत्सृष्टाङ्क प्रहसनं वीथी भाणकमेव च ॥
एतेषां नावकर्तव्यं तथा प्रतिमुखं नृप ॥ 54 ॥
3.4.m: In the utsṛṣṭikāṅka, the prahasana, the vīthī, and the bhāṇa, / the progression (pratimukha) should not be made for these, O king.

3.4.s:
audāryasatpathaṃ śauryaṃ nāyakastu na saṃtyajet ..
nāyikāpi tathā rājanyajedvā pratināyakaḥ .. 55 ..
3.4.d:
औदार्यसत्पथं शौर्यं नायकस्तु न संत्यजेत् ॥
नायिकापि तथा राजन्यजेद्वा प्रतिनायकः ॥ 55 ॥
3.4.m: The hero must not abandon nobility, the virtuous path, or heroism; / nor should the heroine, O king, or the antagonist may abandon them.

3.4.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi nāyikāṣṭakalakṣaṇam ..
nijāparādhātsvagṛhe vāsasajjā tu nāyikā .. 56 ..
3.4.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि नायिकाष्टकलक्षणम् ॥
निजापराधात्स्वगृहे वाससज्जा तु नायिका ॥ 56 ॥
3.4.m: Hereafter I shall state the definitions of the eight types of heroine: / She who is dressed and waiting in her own house owing to her own fault is the vāsakasajjā heroine;

3.4.s:
virahotkaṇṭhitā saiva yā tvanāgatanāyikā ..
svādhīna bhartṛkā proktā yā syātsvādhīnabhartṛkā .. 57 ..
3.4.d:
विरहोत्कण्ठिता सैव या त्वनागतनायिका ॥
स्वाधीन भर्तृका प्रोक्ता या स्यात्स्वाधीनभर्तृका ॥ 57 ॥
3.4.m: she whose hero has not arrived is the virahotkaṇṭhitā; / she who has her husband under her control is proclaimed the svādhīnabhartṛkā;

3.4.s:
kalahāntaritā proktā kalahāhatanāyakā ..
khaṇḍitā yā ca nakharairyutameti pragopatim .. 58 ..
3.4.d:
कलहान्तरिता प्रोक्ता कलहाहतनायका ॥
खण्डिता या च नखरैर्युतमेति प्रगोपतिम् ॥ 58 ॥
3.4.m: she whose hero is repulsed in a quarrel is called the kalahāntaritā; / she who meets her lord while he is marked with nail-scratches is the khaṇḍitā;

3.4.s:
vipralabdhā tu sā jñeyā saṃkete kāntavarjitā ..

3.4.m: she who is without her beloved at the rendezvous is to be known as the vipralabdhā; / and she whose beloved has gone on a journey is the proṣitabhartṛkā.

3.4.m: A dense composition with suitable expressions and graceful movements of these [heroines] / should be made in all twelve types of dramatic forms, beginning with the nāṭaka.

3.4.s:
śṛṅgārahāsyakaruṇavīraraudrabhayānakāḥ ..
bībhatsādbhutaśāntākhyā nava nāṭyarasāḥ smṛtāḥ ..61..
3.4.d:
शृङ्गारहास्यकरुणवीररौद्रभयानकाः ॥
बीभत्साद्भुतशान्ताख्या नव नाट्यरसाः स्मृताः ॥61॥
3.4.m: The erotic, the comic, the pathetic, the heroic, the furious, the terrifying, / the loathsome, the marvelous, and that called the peaceful are taught as the nine dramatic sentiments.

3.4.s:
bandho rasānugaḥ kāryaḥ sarveṣveteṣu yatnataḥ ..
rasapradhānamevaitatsarvanāṭyaṃ narādhipaḥ .. 62 ..
3.4.d:
बन्धो रसानुगः कार्यः सर्वेष्वेतेषु यत्नतः ॥
रसप्रधानमेवैतत्सर्वनाट्यं नराधिपः ॥ 62 ॥
3.4.m: The composition in all of these should be carefully made to follow the sentiments. / All dramatic performance is primarily based on sentiment, O ruler of men.

3.4.s:

3.4.d:
एते कलाकौशलशीलयुक्ताः कार्यास्तथा लोक विधानयुक्ताः ॥
धर्मार्वकामाद्युपदेशगाश्च हिताय लोकस्य नरेन्द्रचन्द्र ॥ 63 ॥
3.4.m: Endowed with skill in arts and good character, and endowed with the ways of worldly conduct, / these should convey instructions on dharma, wealth, pleasure, and the rest, for the welfare of the world, O moon among kings.

3.18
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
अथ गीतलक्षणं भवति तस्य त्रीणि स्थानानि उरः कण्ठः शिरश्च, तेभ्यो मन्द्रमध्यतारोत्पत्तिः ।
त्रयो ग्रामाः । षड्जमध्यमगान्धाराः ।
सप्तस्वरा । षड्जर्षभ गान्धारमध्यमपञ्चमनिषादधैवताः
एकविंशतिमूर्च्छनाः सप्त सप्त प्रतिग्रामाश्रिताः ।
तद्यथासां नामानि सौवीरी हारिणाश्वा कलोपनता शुद्धमध्यमा मार्गी पौरवी ऋष्यका चेति ॥
एताः सप्त मध्यमग्रामिण्यः उत्तरासंज्ञाः ।
प्राञ्चिनी उत्तरायता शुद्धषड्जमत्सरीकृता अश्वक्रान्ता उद्गता च एताः सप्त षड्जग्रामिकाः ।
आलापी कुन्तिमा श्रद्धा उत्तरा षड्जा पञ्चायता॥॥॥एताः सप्त गान्धारग्रामिकाः ।
अथैकोनपञ्चाशत्तानाः । अग्निष्टोमिकः अत्यग्निष्टोमिकः पौण्डरिकः आश्वमेधिकः राजसूयिकः वहुसुवर्णिकः गोसविकः महाव्रतिकः ब्रह्म तानः प्राजापत्यः नगाश्रयः यज्ञाश्रयः गोदानिकः हयक्रान्तः अजक्रान्तः विष्णुक्रान्तः अरण्यः मत्तकोकिलः उज्जीविकश्चेति एते विंशतिर्मध्यमग्रामिकाः ।
प्रस्वापनं पैशाचः जीवनः सावित्रः अर्धसावित्रः सर्वतोभद्रः सुवर्णः विष्णुः जिष्णुर्विष्णुवरः शारदः विजयः हंसः ज्येष्ठ इति एते चतुर्दशषड्जग्रामिकाः । तुम्बुरुप्रियः महालक्ष्मणः गन्धर्वानुमतः अलम्बुसप्रियः नारदप्रियः भीमसेनप्रियः वितानः मातङ्गः भार्गवप्रियः अभिरामः संश्राव्यः किन्नरप्रियः पुण्यः मनोहरः कल्याणकरश्चेति एते पञ्चदश गान्धारमाश्रिताः
एतच्चतुर्विधं स्वरपदलयावधानयोगात् ।
मूर्च्छनास्वादिमध्यान्ते वादिसंवाद्यन्त्यवादिसंज्ञास्तिस्रो वृत्तयः॥
पूर्वोक्ताश्च नवरसाः तत्र हास्यशृङ्गारयोर्मध्यमपञ्चमौ।
वीररौद्राद्भुतेषु षड्जपञ्चमौ । करुणे निषादगान्धारौ ।
बीभत्सभयानकयोर्धैवतम् ।
शान्ते मध्यमम् ।
तथा लयाः हास्यशृङ्गारयोर्मध्यमाः ।
बीभत्सभयानकयोर्विलम्बितः ।
वीररौद्राद्भुतेषु द्रुतः ।
चोक्षाप्रयोगः स्वरोराधने रूपकेषु प्रकरणानुगतः मन्युव्यपदेशेन ते भवन्ति॥
भवन्ति चात्र श्लोकाः ॥
ग्रहांशस्तारमन्द्रे च न्यासोपन्यास एव च॥
अल्पत्वं च बहुत्वं च षाडवोडविते तथा॥
एवमेव बुधैर्ज्ञेया जातयो दशलक्षणाः॥
अलङ्काराश्च चत्वारो भवन्ति वसुधाधिप ॥
प्रसन्नादिः प्रसन्नान्तः प्रसन्नाद्यन्त एव च ॥
प्रसन्नमध्यश्च तथा क्रमेणैवं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
अपरान्तकमुल्लोप्यं मन्द्रकः मकरी तथा ॥
उवेणकं सरो बिन्दुमुत्तमं गीतकानि तु॥
ऋग्गाथा पाणिका दक्षविहिता ब्रह्मगीतिका॥
गीतमेतत्तदाभ्यासः कारणाच्चोक्षसंज्ञः ॥
संक्षेपेण मया प्रोक्तं सुराराधन कारणात् ॥
गीतज्ञो यदि गीतेन नाप्नोति परमं पदम् ॥
देवस्यानुचरो भूत्वा तेनैव सह मोदते ॥
3.4.m:
3.18
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now comes the definition of vocal music: it has three registers: the chest, the throat, and the head; from these arises the low, middle, and high.
There are three scales: the ṣaḍja, madhyama, and gāndhāra.
There are seven notes: ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, madhyama, pañcama, niṣāda, and dhaivata.
There are twenty-one modal shifts, seven belonging to each scale.
Their names are as follows: Sauvīrī, Hāriṇāśvā, Kalopanatā, Śuddhamadhyamā, Mārgī, Pauravī, and Ṛṣyakā;
these seven belong to the madhyama scale and are called Uttarā.
Prāñcinī, Uttarāyatā, Śuddhaṣaḍjā, Matsarīkṛtā, Aśvakrāntā, and Udgatā—these seven belong to the ṣaḍja scale.
Ālāpī, Kuntimā, Śraddhā, Uttarā, Ṣaḍjā, Pañcāyatā [...] these seven belong to the gāndhāra scale.
Now, the forty-nine melodic patterns: Āgniṣṭomika, Atyagniṣṭomika, Pauṇḍarīka, Āśvamedhika, Rājasūyika, Bahusuvarṇika, Gosavika, Mahāvratika, Brahmatāna, Prājāpatya, Nagāśraya, Yajñāśraya, Godānika, Hayakrānta, Ajakrānta, Viṣṇukrānta, Araṇya, Mattakokila, and Ujjīvika—these twenty belong to the madhyama scale.
Prasvāpana, Paiśāca, Jīvana, Sāvitra, Ardhasāvitra, Sarvatobhadra, Suvarṇa, Viṣṇu, Jiṣṇu, Viṣṇuvara, Śārada, Vijaya, Haṃsa, and Jyeṣṭha—these fourteen belong to the ṣaḍja scale.
Tumburupriya, Mahālakṣmaṇa, Gandharvānumata, Alambusapriya, Nāradapriya, Bhīmasenapriya, Vitāna, Mātaṅga, Bhārgavapriya, Abhirāma, Saṃśrāvya, Kinnarapriya, Puṇya, Manohara, and Kalyāṇakara—these fifteen belong to the gāndhāra scale.
This is fourfold through the application of notes, words, tempo, and attentiveness.
In the modal shifts, at the beginning, middle, and end, there are three modes designated as sonant, consonant, and final consonant.
And the previously mentioned nine aesthetic sentiments: there, in the comic and the erotic, are the madhyama and pañcama notes;
in the heroic, furious, and marvellous, the ṣaḍja and pañcama;
in the pathetic, the niṣāda and gāndhāra;
in the odious and terrible, the dhaivata;
in the peaceful, the madhyama.
Likewise, the tempos: in the comic and the erotic, the moderate tempo;
in the odious and terrible, the slow tempo;
in the heroic, furious, and marvellous, the fast tempo.
The clean performance of notes in worship in the dramas conforms to the context; they occur under the designation of passionate expression.
And here are verses:
The initial note, the predominant note, the high and the low registers, the final note, and the penultimate note,
the paucity and the abundance, as well as the hexatonic and pentatonic forms—
thus indeed the melodic types should be known by the wise to have ten characteristics.
And there are four melodic ornaments, O lord of the earth:
that which begins clearly, that which ends clearly, that which begins and ends clearly,
and that which is clear in the middle; thus should one specify in order.
The Aparāntaka, the Ullopya, the Mandraka, and the Makarī,
the Uveṇaka, the Sarobindu, and the Uttama are the song forms.
The Ṛg-song, the Gāthā, the Pāṇikā, the Brahmagītikā arranged by Dakṣa—
this is vocal music, and its practice, on account of its purpose, is called pure.
It has been declared by me in brief for the sake of worshipping the gods.
If one who knows vocal music does not attain the supreme state through song,
he becomes an attendant of the god and rejoices with him.

3.19
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अथातोद्यविधानम् ॥
चतुर्विधमातोद्यं ततं सुषिरं घनमवनद्धं च ।
ततं वीणादि, शुषिरं वंशादि घनं तालादि अवनद्धं मुरजादि तत्र स्वरास्तुल्याः शारीरा वैणवाश्च।
तद्वद्वंशा किन्तु यथा शरीराणामा रोहावरोहणे तथा वैणवानां वंशानां विपर्ययात् तालः कालप्रयोज्यः ।
पञ्चलघ्वक्षरोच्चारणकलामात्रास्तिस्रो वृत्तयः ।
चित्रा वृत्तिर्दक्षिणा द्विधा ।
मात्राकलाचित्रे चतुर्मात्रावृत्तौ अष्टमात्रा दक्षिणाया ।
अष्टमात्रादक्षिणे अवया निष्क्रयो विक्षेपः प्रवेशः शम्पातालः संनिपातभेदः ।
कलासमूहो युक्तः ।

3.19
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now the rule for musical instruments:
Musical instruments are fourfold: stringed, wind, solid, and covered with hide.
The stringed is the vīṇā and the like; the wind is the flute and the like; the solid is the cymbals and the like; the covered with hide is the drum and the like. There, the notes of the human throat and of the vīṇā are equal.
Likewise the flute; however, as the ascent and descent are for the human voice, so they are the opposite for flutes of reed. Rhythm is determined by time.
A measure is the time of uttering five short syllables; there are three modes of execution:
the varied, the intermediate, and the southern, which are twofold.
In the varied, a measure is one time-unit; in the intermediate, four time-units; in the southern, eight time-units.
In the southern, of eight time-units, the limbs are the silent beat, the throwing out, the entry, the clapping beat, and the striking down.
The collection of time-units is connected.
In the even time-measure, the uneven time-measure ending with a protracted note, the five-beat measure is the empty beat, situated according to the syllables.
There, the tempos are fast, moderate, and slow.
Rhythm is possessed of tempo.
The section is twofold: the collective and the divided.
Now, the covered instrument: there, like the puṣkara drum, it is endowed with resonance and pathos.
There, the sixteen syllables are: ka, kha, ga, gha, ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ṇa, ta, tha, da, dha, ya, ra, la, va. There, the syllables beginning with ka, ṭa, ra, tha, and ga are on the right face; gha, dha, and ma on the left; ga and da on the top; ṭa, ṇa, la, and ha on the encompassing face; a, ā, i, u, e, o, ai, and au, appropriately; the combination of kha, ga, and dha is with the letter r;
of ka, ha, bha, and da, with ṇa, la, tha, and va.
By the stroke of the flat hand, by the movement of the fingers on the upper and left sides, by the stroke of the flat hand with the index finger, likewise is the combination of the ḍa-la syllables: with the level hand, the half-hand, the non-elongated hand, the single hand, struck with the two hands and the index finger; struck with the flat hand for the auxiliary syllables gha, tha, ga, ḍa, and ra; on the hand-and-a-half, the syllables ka and tha;
on the hand-and-a-half, ṭha, ṇa, la, and ha; struck with the flat hand and index finger of both hands. The tuning paths are Addhita, Vitasta, Ālipta, and Gomukhī: Addhita is in the erotic and comic sentiments;
in the heroic, furious, and marvellous, Vitasta; in the pathetic and peaceful, Ālipta;
in the odious and terrible, Gomukha; the dardura and paṇava drums follow the mṛdaṅga drum.
And here are verses:
Facing the stage in alignment with the door of the tiring-room,
the drums should be behind them, and likewise the plastering.
To the south of that, the dardura and paṇava are to be known.
Facing north should be the singer, and thus to his south,
to his left the clay-drummer, and to his right two flute players;
the positioning of the singers is directly facing the main singer.

3.4.m:
Dramatic performance is stated by those learned in theatre to be the imitation of another, O king. / Dance serves as its embellishment, enhancing its beauty.
Dance is declared to be of two kinds, always based on dramatic performance and lyrical dance. / Each of these two kinds is again twofold, O ruler of men:
the internal and the external; the external is devoid of rules, / while the internal possesses rules and is auspicious through its proper execution.
Lyrical dance may be performed freely, either in a playhouse or outside. / Dramatic performance should be held only in a playhouse; the playhouse is of two kinds:
rectangular and square, measured at thirty-two cubits. / The square should not be made [longer], while the rectangular is twice as long.
It should not be made deficient or excessive, as it bestows visible and invisible auspicious results. / In a deficient [theatre] there is crowding, and in one too spacious, the drama and song
fail to achieve distinct clarity; therefore, one should avoid both of those. / At the very beginning, worship of the gods must be performed,

Then follows the entrance of each character with the tossing aside of the curtain. / Entrances and exits should be executed having indicated the dramatic business.
An offering of folded hands with flowers must be made, and at the end of the drama, worship of the site. / Devoted to the recitation and song, the movement across the stage corresponds to the character.
It consists of four kalās for heroes, three kalās for middling characters, / and two kalās for low characters in the intermediate action of a king.
One [kalā] more or less should be applied for all according to the demands of the dramatic action. / Gods are to be known as heroic and fierce; Dānavas and others are fierce;
kings are firm and playful; their attendants are firm; / sages are tranquil and firm; their disciples are tranquil;
brahmins are firm and noble; merchants are regarded as noble. / Such varieties are explained through the combination of these very traits.
Costume and makeup, internal psychological states, vocal expression, and bodily movement— / fourfold is the representation to be employed in dramatic action.

3.4.m:
Costume and makeup is said to be the altered dress consisting of headdresses, masks, and the like. / For the firm and fierce, the dress should not be exceedingly ostentatious;
it should be fierce for the fierce, and for kings it is desired to be charming. / The dress of the antagonist should likewise be made fierce.
For others, the dress should be appropriate, conforming to their region and profession. / Horses and the like should be constructed to resemble [real ones] using hide, wood, and other materials.
Next, I shall explain to you the representation through internal psychological states: / shedding of tears, horripilation, sweating, trembling,
and likewise changes of complexion constitute the representation through internal states. / Vocal representation is declared to be through speech; bodily representation I shall describe in what follows.
Dramatic dance should always be performed extensively in scenes of joy; / in scenes of sorrow it should not be performed, or only a little should be executed thereafter.
The recaka movement is stated to be fourfold, based on the waist, feet, shanks, and [hands]. / The cārī movement is regarded as twofold: the cārī and the other, the mahācārī.
The cārī consists of delicate limbs, speech, and gestures, O descendant of Yadu; / enhanced by these [energetic movements], it is to be recognized as the mahācārī, O lord of men.

3.4.m:
Its circular movements born from the combination of cārīs are indeed ten: / atikrānta, vicitra, lalitasañcara,
sūcīviddha, daṇḍapāda, the two named vikṛta and alāta, / vāmabaddha, salalita, and krānta—these are aerial movements.
Hear of the ten other circular movements that are earthly, O earth-ruler: / bhramara and āskandita, and after that mārdava,
samā, what they call saritā, along with eḍakākrīḍita, / aḍḍita, the one named śakaṭa, and that remembered as āhārya,
piṣṭakubja is to be known, and likewise apagata. / Now I shall describe the aṅgahāras; learn them from me by name:
the aṅgahāra sthirahasta, and likewise ākṣiptaka is remembered; / udghāṭita is the third, and another is aparājita;
mattākrīḍa, then viṣkambha, likewise svastikarecita, / vṛścikāpasṛta, talamandā, and sarpita;

3.4.d:
मतल्लीस्खलितश्चैव भ्रमरः पार्श्वस्वस्तिकः ॥
मदाद्विलसितश्चैव विक्षिप्तो गतिमण्डलः ॥ 31 ॥
वैशाखरेचितश्चैव परिवृत्तकरेचितः ॥
उद्वर्तकः परिच्छिन्नो रेचकोऽथ बलाहकः ॥ 32 ॥
सम्भ्रान्तो वाङ्गिकश्चैव इति क्रीडो ह्यलातकः ॥
विद्युद्भ्रान्तः परावृत्तः पार्श्वच्छेदसमन्वितः ॥ 33 ॥
आक्षिप्तो रेचितश्चैव सौम्योऽथ करितस्तथा ॥
सूचीविद्धोऽपविद्धश्च विलापोवनिकुट्टितः ॥ 34 ॥
षट्त्रिंशदेते संप्रोक्ता ह्यङ्गहारा यदूत्तम ॥
एतेषां संप्रवक्ष्यामि कारणानि यथाक्रमम् ॥
हस्तपाद प्रचारश्च यथा योज्यः प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥ 35 ॥
सर्वेषामङ्गहाराणां निष्पत्तिः कारणं भवेत् ॥
तान्यहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि नामभिः कर्मभिस्तथा ॥ 36 ॥
हस्तपादसमायुक्तो नृत्तस्य करणं भवेत ॥
द्वे नृत्यकरणे चैव भवेतां नृप मातृका ॥ 37 ॥

त्रिभिः कलापकश्चैव चतुर्भिः खण्डकः स्मृतः ॥
पञ्चैव करणानि स्युः संज्ञाघात इति स्मृतः ॥ 38 ॥
षङ्भिर्वा सप्तभिर्वापि अष्टभिर्नवभिस्तथा ॥
करणैरिह संयुक्ता अङ्गहारा इति स्मृताः ॥ 39 ॥
एतेषां चैव वक्ष्यामि नामान्यहमतः परम् ॥
तालपुष्पापविद्धे द्वे लीनस्वस्तिकरेचितम् ॥ 3.20.40 ॥
मण्डलं स्वस्तिकं चैव ऊरु वृत्तं निकुण्डकम् ॥
सूचीविद्धं कटिच्छिन्नमर्धरेचितमेव च ॥ 41 ॥
वक्षः स्वस्तिकमुत्पन्नं स्वस्तिकं पृष्ठगं पुनः ॥
दिक्स्वन्तिकमलाताख्यमर्धसूचीकटीसमम्॥42॥
आक्षिप्तरेचितं क्षिप्रमर्धस्वस्तिकसञ्चितम्॥
भुजङ्गवासितं चैव ऊर्ध्वजानु निकुञ्चितम्॥43॥
मतल्ली त्वर्धमतल्ली स्याद्रेचकनिकुण्टकम् ॥
पारविद्धं तडिद्धान्तं वलितं चूर्णितं तथा ॥44॥
3.4.m:
With three it is remembered as a kalāpaka, and with four as a khaṇḍaka; / when there are five karaṇas, it is remembered by the term saṃghāta.
Combined with six, seven, eight, or nine / karaṇas here, they are remembered as aṅgahāras.
And after this I shall speak their names: / tālapuṣpa and apaviddha, the two; līnasvastikarecita,
maṇḍalasvastika, ūruvṛtta, nikuñcita, / sūcīviddha, kaṭicchinna, and ardharecita,
vakṣaḥsvastika, unmatta, svastika, and pṛṣṭhaga, / diksvastika, that named alāta, ardhasūcī, kaṭīsama,
ākṣiptarecita, kṣipra, ardhasvastikasañcita, / bhujaṅgatrāsita, ūrdhvajānu, nikuñcita,
matallī and ardhamatallī, recakanikuñcita, / parāviddha, vidyudbhrānta, valita, and cūrṇita.

3.4.d:
ललितं दण्डपक्षं च भुजङ्गत्रस्तरेचितम्॥
नूपुरं रेचितं चैव भ्रमरं चतुरं तथा॥45॥
भुजङ्गाञ्चितमन्यत्स्याच्छिन्नं वृश्चिकरेचितम् ॥
लतावृश्चिकमन्यत्स्याच्छिन्नं वृश्चिकरेचितम् ॥46॥
वृश्चिकं व्यंसितं चैव सूचीविद्धकमेव च ॥
ललाटतिलकं चैव कुण्डलं चक्रमंडलम् ॥47॥
तरोर्मण्डलमाक्षिप्तं लतालसितमार्गलम ॥
विक्षिप्तं भ्रमितं चैव विलासं वानरप्लुतम्॥48॥
परिवृत्तं निवृत्तं च पार्श्वाक्रान्तं निकुञ्चितम् ॥
अतिक्रान्तमवक्रान्तं दोलापादविवर्जितम् ॥49॥
नागप्रक्रीडितं चैव विप्लुतं गरुडप्लुतम् ॥
गण्डसूची परिक्षिप्तं पार्श्वजानुकमेव च ॥ 3.20.50 ॥
गृहावलीनकं लीनं विष्णुक्रान्तमजप्लुतम् ॥
आक्रान्तं मण्डितं चैव मयूरलसितं नसम् ॥ 51 ॥
सर्पितं चोलपादं च हरिणप्लुतमेव च ॥
प्रेङ्खालितं नितम्बं च स्खलितं परिहस्तकम् ॥ 52 ॥

असर्पिततलं चैव सिंहविक्रीडितं तथा ॥
वृषभ क्रीडितं चैव गङ्गावतरणं तथा ॥ 53 ॥
अष्टोत्तरशतं चैव करणानां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
सुकुमारं तथा विद्धं वृत्तं द्विविधमुच्यते ॥54 ॥।
उद्धृतं पुरुषप्रायं स्त्रीप्रायं सुकुमारकम् ॥
देवचिह्नकृताकारा पिण्डी भवति पर्थिव ॥ 55॥
भारती सात्त्वती चैव कौशिक्यारभटी तथा ॥
चतस्रो वृत्तयः प्रोक्ता वाक्प्रधाना तु भारती ॥ 56 ॥
तथा वीररसप्राया विज्ञेया सात्त्वती नृप ॥
तथा रौद्रप्रचारा च भवत्यारभटी सदा ॥ 57 ॥।
शृङ्गारहास्यबहुला तथा भवति कौशिकी ॥
आवन्ती दाक्षिणात्या च तथा चैवात्र मागधी ॥ 58 ॥
पञ्चाली मध्यमा चेति वृत्तिः सा तु चतुर्विधा ॥
वेषभाषानुकरणं तथाचारप्रवर्तनम् ॥ 59 ॥
प्रवृत्तिरिति विख्याता वृत्तीनामाश्रयास्तु ताः॥
नाट्यलोकाश्रया धर्मि धर्माश्च द्विविधा मता ॥ 3.20.60 ॥
3.4.m:
asarpitatala, and siṃhavikrīḍita, / vṛṣabhakrīḍita, and gaṅgāvataraṇa.
One hundred and eight karaṇas have thus been proclaimed. / Dramatic practice is said to be of two kinds: delicate and forceful.
The elevated consists mostly of men, whereas the delicate consists mostly of women. / The piṇḍī-formation assumes the shape of the emblem of a deity, O king.
Four styles of dramatic performance are proclaimed: bhāratī, sāttvatī, / kauśikī, and ārabhaṭī. The bhāratī style has speech as its principal element;
likewise, O king, sāttvatī should be understood as abounding in the heroic sentiment, / and ārabhaṭī is always characterised by furious conduct;
kauśikī abounds in the erotic and comic sentiments. / Then there are the regional modes here: āvantī, dākṣiṇātyā, māgadhī,
pañcālī, and madhyamā; thus regional mode is fourfold. / The imitation of dress and speech, as well as the adoption of conduct,
is known as local usage, and these [usages] depend upon the dramatic styles. / Practice is considered two-fold, based on theatrical convention and worldly convention.

3.4.m:
Success in drama is of two kinds: divine and human. / Among these, the human arises from practice, and the divine arises from the grace of the gods.
Dance endowed with sentiment and emotional state, conforming to the rhythm, conforming to the sentiment of the poetic text, / and following the vocal song, is declared blessed, bestowing happiness, and augmenting dharma.

pārśvaṃ nataṃ tathā kāryaṃ sthānaṃ mandālasaṃ tu tat ..
cintāyāṃ tu tathautsukye nirvede virahe tathā .. 4 ..
viṣādeṣu sadā deyaṃ sthānametatprayoktṛbhiḥ ..
cibukāpāśritau hastau bāhuśīrṣācitaṃ śiraḥ .. 5 ..
sarvābhinayanaṃ caiva vijñeyaṃ klāntanāyakam ..
balinā nigrahītasya ripuṇā khaṇḍitasya ca .. 6 ..
3.5.d:
तस्या यदेतत्प्रसृतं तु जंघे स्त्रस्तौ करौ तं नतमुद्दिशन्ति ।
आलस्यखेदश्रममोक्षणेषु कार्यस्तु तस्याभिनयप्रयोगः ॥ 7 ॥
3.22
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
स्वस्थमन्दालसक्रान्तं प्रस्थालसमथापि च ॥
विष्कम्भितं तत्कटुकं मुक्तजानु तथा समम् ॥ 1 ॥
जानूगतं विमुक्तं च स्थानकान्युपवेशने ॥
विष्कुम्भिताञ्चितौ पादौ वक्षः किञ्चित्समुन्नतम् ॥ 2 ॥
हस्तौ कट्यूरुविन्यस्तौ स्वस्थौ स्वस्थोपवेशने ॥
एकः प्रसारितः पादस्त्वन्यश्चैवासनाश्रितः ॥ 3 ॥
पार्श्वं नतं तथा कार्यं स्थानं मन्दालसं तु तत् ॥
चिन्तायां तु तथौत्सुक्ये निर्वेदे विरहे तथा ॥ 4 ॥
विषादेषु सदा देयं स्थानमेतत्प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥
चिबुकापाश्रितौ हस्तौ बाहुशीर्षाचितं शिरः ॥ 5 ॥
सर्वाभिनयनं चैव विज्ञेयं क्लान्तनायकम् ॥
बलिना निग्रहीतस्य रिपुणा खण्डितस्य च ॥ 6 ॥
3.5.m:
When her shanks are extended and her two hands hang loose, they call that bent down; / its dramatic performance should be applied in expressing indolence, distress, and weariness.
3.22
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Svastha, mandālasa, ākrānta, prasthālasa, and also / viṣkambhita, tatkaṭuka, muktajānu, and sama,
jānugata, and vimukta are the postures in sitting. / The two feet crossed and bent, the chest slightly raised,
the two hands placed comfortably on the waist and thighs—this is comfortable sitting. / One foot is stretched out, and the other rests upon the seat,
and the side of the body should be bent: that is the mandālasa posture. / In anxiety, longing, dejection, and separation,
as well as in despair, this posture should always be assigned by performers. / The two hands resting upon the chin, the head inclined towards the upper arm,
and all dramatic acting are to be known as showing an exhausted hero. / For one restrained by a powerful enemy, or broken by a foe,

3.5.s:
śokamlānasya ca tathā sthānametadvinirdiśet ..
grahau hastau vimuktaṃ ca śarīramalasaṃ tathā .. 7 ..
3.5.d:
शोकम्लानस्य च तथा स्थानमेतद्विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
ग्रहौ हस्तौ विमुक्तं च शरीरमलसं तथा ॥ 7 ॥
3.5.m: or withered by sorrow, one should designate this posture. / The two hands loosely held, the body languid,

3.5.s:
khedālasaṃ tathā cakṣuryatra svasthālasaṃ tu tat ..
śrame glānau made caiva mūrcchāyā vyathite tathā..8..
3.5.d:
खेदालसं तथा चक्षुर्यत्र स्वस्थालसं तु तत् ॥
श्रमे ग्लानौ मदे चैव मूर्च्छाया व्यथिते तथा॥8॥
3.5.m: and the eyes dull with fatigue: where this is, that is svasthālasa. / In weariness, languor, intoxication, fainting, suffering,

3.5.s:
mohe prāṇabhaye caiva sthānametatprayojayet ..
viṣkumbhitāñcitau pādau kuru viṣkumbhitau bhujau .. 9 ..
3.5.d:
मोहे प्राणभये चैव स्थानमेतत्प्रयोजयेत् ॥
विष्कुम्भिताञ्चितौ पादौ कुरु विष्कुम्भितौ भुजौ ॥ 9 ॥
3.5.m: infatuation, and fear of death, one should employ this posture. / Make the two feet crossed and arched, and the arms firmly braced;

3.5.s:
nimīlitaṃ tathā cakṣuḥ sthāne viṣkumbhitā sati ..
svavakṣogatayā dṛṣṭyā yoge dhyāne vidhīyate .. 3.22.10 ..
3.5.d:
निमीलितं तथा चक्षुः स्थाने विष्कुम्भिता सति ॥
स्ववक्षोगतया दृष्ट्या योगे ध्याने विधीयते ॥ 3.22.10 ॥
3.5.m: and the eyes half-closed in the viṣkambhita posture, / with the gaze directed towards one's own chest, is prescribed in yoga and meditation.

3.5.s:
svabhāvasaṃsthayā caiva sabhyānāmupaveśane ..
samau pādau samādhāya samaṃ yadupadiśyate .. 11 ..
3.5.d:
स्वभावसंस्थया चैव सभ्यानामुपवेशने ॥
समौ पादौ समाधाय समं यदुपदिश्यते ॥ 11 ॥
3.5.m: When sitting naturally, suitable for members of an assembly, / placing the two feet evenly, it is taught as the even posture.

3.5.s:
aspaṣṭabhūtalaṃ caiva jñeyaṃ mukuṭakāsanam ..
pitrye samādhau japye ca homādikaraṇeṣu ca .. 12 ..
3.5.d:
अस्पष्टभूतलं चैव ज्ञेयं मुकुटकासनम् ॥
पित्र्ये समाधौ जप्ये च होमादिकरणेषु च ॥ 12 ॥
3.5.m: When the surface of the ground is untouched, it should be known as the mukuṭaka seat. / In rites for the ancestors, deep absorption, recitation of prayers, and performing oblations into fire,

3.5.s:
etatsthānaṃ vidhātavyaṃ yathāgamanakarmaṇi ..
ekaṃ jānu yadāsye ca mahīpṛṣṭhe vidhīyate .. 13 ..
3.5.d:
एतत्स्थानं विधातव्यं यथागमनकर्मणि ॥
एकं जानु यदास्ये च महीपृष्ठे विधीयते ॥ 13 ॥
3.5.m: this posture is to be adopted, as also in rituals of invocation. / When one knee is positioned in front upon the surface of the earth,

3.5.s:
jñātavyaṃ bhūmipaśreṣṭha muktajānukamāsanam ..
etatkṛtavyalīkānāṃ priyāṇāṃ samprasādane .. 14 ..

ज्ञातव्यं भूमिपश्रेष्ठ मुक्तजानुकमासनम् ॥
एतत्कृतव्यलीकानां प्रियाणां सम्प्रसादने ॥ 14 ॥
3.5.m: it should be recognized, O best of kings, as the muktajānu seat. / This is used in appeasing beloved women who have experienced offenses,

3.5.s:
majjane kuṭilānāṃ ca tathā bhūmyanulepane ..
mahīgatābhyāṃ jānubhyāṃ sthānaṃ jānugataṃ bhaveta .. 15 ..
3.5.d:
मज्जने कुटिलानां च तथा भूम्यनुलेपने ॥
महीगताभ्यां जानुभ्यां स्थानं जानुगतं भवेत ॥ 15 ॥
3.5.m: in bathing for deceitful people, and in smearing the ground. / With both knees resting on the earth, the posture becomes jānugata.

3.5.s:
rājñāṃ vijñāpane kāryaṃ surāṇāṃ caiva pūjane ..
bhūmau yadūrdhvaṃ patanaṃ tadvimuktamiti smṛtam .. 16 ..
3.5.d:
राज्ञां विज्ञापने कार्यं सुराणां चैव पूजने ॥
भूमौ यदूर्ध्वं पतनं तद्विमुक्तमिति स्मृतम् ॥ 16 ॥
3.5.m: It should be performed in making a petition to kings and in the worship of the gods. / Falling down backwards upon the ground is remembered as vimukta.

3.5.s:
prahārataḥ prayoktavyamāveśe krandane tathā ..
bhadrāsanaṃ tu devānāṃ rājñāṃ siṃhāsanaṃ bhaveta .. 17 ..
3.5.d:
प्रहारतः प्रयोक्तव्यमावेशे क्रन्दने तथा ॥
भद्रासनं तु देवानां राज्ञां सिंहासनं भवेत ॥ 17 ॥
3.5.m: It should be employed in [representing] a blow, in possession, and likewise in weeping. / A bhadrāsana [is suitable] for gods, and a lion-throne for kings;

3.5.s:
rūpyāsanaṃ tu dātavyaṃ sāṃvatsarapurodhasoḥ ..
vetrāsanamamātyānāṃ mantriṇāṃ tu tathā bhaveta .. 18 ..

रूप्यासनं तु दातव्यं सांवत्सरपुरोधसोः ॥
वेत्रासनममात्यानां मन्त्रिणां तु तथा भवेत ॥ 18 ॥
3.5.m: a silver seat should be given to the astrologer and the royal priest; / a cane seat should belong to ministers and counselors;

3.5.s:
mandāsanaṃ tu dātavyaṃ senānīyuvarājayoḥ ..
munīnāṃ ca dvijānāṃ ca tathā sabrahmacāriṇām .. 19 ..

मन्दासनं तु दातव्यं सेनानीयुवराजयोः ॥
मुनीनां च द्विजानां च तथा सब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥ 19 ॥
3.5.m: a low seat should be given to the general and the crown prince. / For sages, twice-born men, and likewise for fellow students,

3.5.s:

sthānīyāḥ puruṣā ye ca mukhyāḥ paurāśca ye tathā .. 3.22.20 ..

बृसी देया महाराज ये चान्ये नियमे स्थिताः ॥
स्थानीयाः पुरुषा ये च मुख्याः पौराश्च ये तथा ॥ 3.22.20 ॥

3.5.s:

veśastrīṇāṃ kumārāṇāṃ tathā bhṛtyajanasya ca .. 21 ..

siṃhāsanaṃ vinā rājangṛhe svacchandamānasam .. 22 ..

3.5.s:
naikāsanaṃ syādguruṇā tu rājanrathe gaje vāpi śilātale ca ..

3.23
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
वैष्णवं समपादं च वैशाखं मण्डलं तथा ॥
प्रत्यालीढमथालीढं षट् पुसां स्थानकानि तु ॥ 1 ॥
स्वभावसंश्रितः पादस्त्र्यंशः पक्षगतोऽपरः ॥
किञ्चिदञ्चितजंघश्च वैष्णवं स्थानमुच्यते ॥ 2 ॥
स्थाने नानेन कर्तव्ये संलापस्तु स्वभावतः ॥
समपादं तु विज्ञेयं समैस्तालान्तरैः पदैः ॥ 3 ॥
स्वस्वभासौष्ठवोपेतं रुद्रब्रह्मादिदैवतम् ॥
अनेन कार्यं स्थानेन विप्रमण्डलकारणम् ॥ 4 ॥
बलानां पक्षिणां चैव वरकौतुकमेव च ॥
स्वस्थानं स्यन्दनस्थानां विमानस्थायिनामपि ॥ 5 ॥
लिङ्गस्थानां व्रतस्थानां स्थानमेतत्प्रयोजयेत् ॥
द्वौ तालावर्धतालं च पादयोरंतरं भवेत् ॥ 6 ॥
3.5.m:
One should not share a single seat with one's guru, O king, [except] on a chariot, an elephant, or a rock slab; / nor is there any fault with a guru on a single seat if it is always a very long wooden plank.
3.23 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Vaiṣṇava, samapāda, vaiśākha, and maṇḍala, / as well as pratyālīḍha and ālīḍha: these are the six standing postures for men.
One foot in its natural [position], the other placed obliquely at three aṅgulas, / and with the shank slightly curved: this is called the vaiṣṇava posture.
In this posture, natural conversation is to be represented. / The samapāda is to be known by the feet being even, at a distance of one tāla apart,
endowed with the elegance of their respective nature, [appropriate for] deities such as Rudra and Brahmā. / In this posture, the gathering of brahmins is to be represented,
as well as [the movements] of troops and birds, and the eagerness of the bridegroom; / it is the proper posture for those standing on chariots and on celestial vehicles;
one should employ this posture for those who stand before a liṅga or observe vows. / When the distance between the two feet is two and a half tālas,

अञ्चितं यत्र जंघे तु पदौ पक्षस्थितो तथा ॥
वैशाखं नाम तत्स्थानं स्कन्दश्चैवात्र देवता ॥ 7 ॥
स्थानेनानेन कर्तव्यमश्वानां वाहनं बुधैः ॥
व्यायामो निर्गमश्चैव प्रवेशो धनुषस्तथा ॥ 8 ॥।
अतः परं मण्डलं स्यात्त्रींस्तालान्तरमेव च ॥
कटी जानुसमा यत्र पादौ पक्षस्थितौ यथा ॥ 9॥
धनुर्वज्रप्रहरणं मण्डलेन प्रयोजयेत् ॥
वाहनं कुञ्जराणां तु नृत्ते चोद्वहनक्रिया ॥ 3.23.1 0॥
आदौ च दक्षिणं पादं पञ्चतालं प्रसारयेत् ॥
आलीढं नाम तत्स्थानं रुद्रकाल्यत्र दैवतम् ॥11॥
अनेन कार्या स्थानेन सर्वत्रोद्धरणक्रिया ॥
रौद्रपादप्रचारस्तु संग्रामस्य निरूपणम् ॥ 12 ॥
सिंहाद्यभिनयं चैव शक्तसन्धानमेव च ॥
खड्गयुद्धे नियुद्धे च मण्डलभ्रमणे तथा ॥ 13 ॥
3.5.m:
where the shanks are curved and the feet are placed obliquely, / that is the posture named vaiśākha, and Skanda is its presiding deity.
With this posture the wise should represent the riding of horses, / exercise, departure, and the stringing of a bow.
Next is the maṇḍala [posture], with a distance of three tālas [between the feet], / where the waist is on a level with the knees, and the feet are placed obliquely.
Striking with a bow or a thunderbolt should be performed in the maṇḍala [posture], / as well as the riding of elephants and the lifting movement in dance.
First, one should stretch out the right foot by five tālas; / that is the posture named ālīḍha, and Rudrakālī is its presiding deity.
With this posture, the act of drawing [a weapon] should everywhere be represented, / as well as the gait of the furious sentiment and the depiction of battle,
the imitation of lions and the like, the fitting of the arrow to the string, / sword-fights, close combat, and wheeling in a circle,

uttarottarasaṃjalpe roṣāmarṣasamudbhave ..

उत्तरोत्तरसंजल्पे रोषामर्षसमुद्भवे ॥

तथाभिद्रवणं चैव शास्त्राणां च विमोक्षणम् ॥
अञ्चितं दक्षिणं कृत्वा वामं पादं प्रसार्य च ॥ 15 ॥
आलीढं परिवर्तन्ते प्रत्यालीढमिति स्मृतम् ॥।
प्रत्यालीढं तु विज्ञेयं स्थानं च नवदैवतम् ॥ 16 ॥
आलीढेनोदितं शस्तं प्रत्यालीढं न मोचयेत् ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि स्त्रीणां स्थानत्रयं नृप ॥ 17 ॥
आयतं वावहित्थं च हयक्रान्तमथापि च ॥
एकश्चानुयुतो यत्र पादौ विरचितः समः ॥ 18 ॥
तालमात्रान्तरन्यस्तः त्र्यक्षः पक्षगतोऽपरः ॥
प्रसन्नमाननमुरः समं यत्र समुन्नतम् ॥ 19 ॥
लतानितम्बगौ हस्तौ स्थानं ज्ञेयं तदायतम् ॥
रङ्गावतरणे ह्येतत्तथा पुष्पाञ्जलौ भवेत् ॥ 3.23.20 ॥
3.5.m:
retorts and mutual banter, the arising of rage and intolerance, / the collision of wrestlers, and the observation of enemies,
as well as charging forward and the discharging of weapons. / Making the right [leg] curved and stretching out the left foot,
they reverse the ālīḍha; this is known as pratyālīḍha. / The pratyālīḍha posture is to be known as having nine deities.
Whatever has been praised as indicated by ālīḍha should [also] not be released from pratyālīḍha. / Beyond this, I shall describe the three postures for women, O king:
āyata, avahittha, and hayakrānta. / Where one foot is in place, arranged even,
placed at an interval of just one tāla, and the other is placed obliquely in three parts, / where the face is serene and the chest is even and raised,
and the two hands rest on the hip like a creeper, that posture is to be known as āyata. / It is used in descending onto the stage and in offering a handful of flowers.

उच्छ्राये दर्शने गर्वे तत्तथोर्ध्वनिरीक्षणे ॥।

सन्देहालापसंज्ञासु तत्तथा वाहनादिषु ॥
किञ्चित्पार्श्वनतग्रीवं शिरो विज्ञेयमञ्चितम् ॥ 8 ॥
मूर्च्छिते व्यथिते चैव सञ्चिते दुःखिते भवेत् ॥
( उत्क्षिप्तबाहुशिखरं तथाचितशिरोधरम् ॥ 9 ॥
निकुञ्चितं च तद्गर्वे विलासे च प्रयोजयेत् ॥
परावृत्तपरावृत्तं कार्यं पृष्ठनिरीक्षणे ॥ 3.24.10 ॥)
उत्क्षिप्तं चापि विज्ञेयमुन्मुखावस्थितं शिरः ॥
आशु दिव्यार्थयोगे च कार्यं तच्च प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥ 11 ॥
अधोमुखस्थितं चापि बुधाः प्राहुरधोगतम् ॥
लज्जायां च प्रमाणे च दुःखे तच्च प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 12 ॥
सर्वतो लोलनाच्चैव परिलोलितमुच्यते ॥
व्याधिते मूर्च्छिते मत्ते भवेत्तु परिलोलितम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.5.m:
it occurs in looking up at height, seeing, pride, and gazing upward. / When it is thrown down just once, bent downwards,
in doubt, conversation, signaling, and likewise on vehicles and the like; / with the neck slightly bent to one side, the head is to be known as añcita;
it occurs in one who is faint, distressed, collected, or sorrowful. / When the top of the arm is raised and the neck is curved,
And one should employ [the head called] nikuñcita in arrogance and playful grace; / parāvṛtta should be performed when looking behind.
And the head held facing upward should be known as utkṣipta; / that should be executed swiftly by performers in connection with celestial matters.
And the wise call [the head] held facing downward adhogata; / and one should employ that in shame, in measurement, and in grief.
And because of rolling in every direction, it is called parilolita; / parilolita should occur when sick, swooning, and intoxicated.

3.5.d:
एतत्तु शिरसः कर्म कथितं ते नराधिप ॥
अञ्चितं रेचितं मुक्तं विवृतं चतुरं तथा ॥ 14 ॥
प्रसारितं तथा स्तब्धं ग्रीवाकर्मणि निर्दिशेत् ॥
अञ्चितं किञ्चिदेकांशं लोलनाद्रेचितं तु तत् ॥ 15 ॥
रेचितं भ्रमणान्मुक्तं विवृतं चलितं च तत् ॥
मधुरं चतुरं प्रोक्तमायतं स्यात्प्रसारितम् ॥ 16 ॥
स्तब्धं स्तब्धं तथा प्रोक्तं शिरःकर्मानुगामि च ॥
अञ्चितं स्याद्विलासादौ रेचितं मण्डलेक्षणे ॥ 17 ॥
मुक्तं मूर्च्छादियोगेषु विवृत्तं ललितादिषु ॥
सौम्यभावे तु चतुरं दृष्टौ कार्यं प्रसारितम् ॥ 18 ॥
स्तब्धं शीतेऽथ वा व्याधावविकारि स्वभावतः ॥
विबुद्धं विनिवृत्तं च निर्भुग्नं भुग्नमेव च ॥ 19 ॥
विवृत्तं च तथैवर्जुकर्मण्यस्य विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
व्यावृत्तं स्याद्विबुद्धाख्यं निवृत्तं पिहितं भवेत् ॥3.24.20॥

3.5.s:
prasāraṇādubhayataḥ pārśvayoḥ syātprasāritam ..
parivartanāttrikasyāpi vivartitamiheṣyate .. 33 ..
3.5.d:
प्रसारणादुभयतः पार्श्वयोः स्यात्प्रसारितम् ॥
परिवर्तनात्त्रिकस्यापि विवर्तितमिहेष्यते ॥ 33 ॥
3.5.m: from extending on both sides, it becomes prasārita in the sides; / and from turning of the sacrum, it is here deemed vivartita;

3.5.s:
asya caivopagamanādbhavedapasṛtaṃ punaḥ ..
nataṃ tvapasṛte kāryaṃ connataṃ tūpasarpite .. 34 ..
3.5.d:
अस्य चैवोपगमनाद्भवेदपसृतं पुनः ॥
नतं त्वपसृते कार्यं चोन्नतं तूपसर्पिते ॥ 34 ॥
3.5.m: and from its moving forward, it becomes apasṛta again; / nata should be performed when stepping back, and unnata when advancing;

3.5.s:
prasārite praharṣādau trāse cāpasṛte punaḥ ..
vivartitaṃ vivarte ca kāraṇaṃ pārśvamucyate .. 35 ..
3.5.d:
प्रसारिते प्रहर्षादौ त्रासे चापसृते पुनः ॥
विवर्तितं विवर्ते च कारणं पार्श्वमुच्यते ॥ 35 ॥
3.5.m: in prasārita during intense joy and the like, and in apasṛta during terror; / and vivartita is used in turning: this is declared the purpose of the side.

3.5.s:
kṣāmaṃ nimnaṃ ca pūrṇaṃ ca saṃproktamudaraṃ tridhā ..
kṣāmaṃ tu hasite kāryaṃ tathā caiva vijṛmbhite .. 36 ..
3.5.d:
क्षामं निम्नं च पूर्णं च संप्रोक्तमुदरं त्रिधा ॥
क्षामं तु हसिते कार्यं तथा चैव विजृम्भिते ॥ 36 ॥
3.5.m: Kṣāma, nimna, and pūrṇa: the belly is declared threefold. / Kṣāma should be performed in laughter, and likewise in yawning;

3.5.s:
vyādhite tapasi śrānte kṣudhārte nimnameva ca ..
pūrṇaṃ niḥśvasite caiva hyārogye lalitaṃ tathā .. 37 ..
3.5.d:
व्याधिते तपसि श्रान्ते क्षुधार्ते निम्नमेव च ॥
पूर्णं निःश्वसिते चैव ह्यारोग्ये ललितं तथा ॥ 37 ॥
3.5.m: in disease, austerity, fatigue, and hunger, it should be nimna; / and pūrṇa in sighing, and likewise gracefully in good health;

3.5.s:
prakampitā ca cchinnā ca nivṛttā recitā tathā ..
udvāhitā caiva kaṭirnṛtte pañcavidhā smṛtā .. 38 ..
3.5.d:
प्रकम्पिता च च्छिन्ना च निवृत्ता रेचिता तथा ॥
उद्वाहिता चैव कटिर्नृत्ते पञ्चविधा स्मृता ॥ 38 ॥
3.5.m: Tremulous, severed, turned away, emptied, / and raised up—the waist in dance is traditionally declared to be of five kinds.

3.5.s:
tiryaggatā gatā kṣipraṃ vijñeyā vaprakampitā ..
madhyasthabalanāccaiva cchinnā saṃparikīrtitā .. 39 ..
3.5.d:
तिर्यग्गता गता क्षिप्रं विज्ञेया वप्रकम्पिता ॥
मध्यस्थबलनाच्चैव च्छिन्ना संपरिकीर्तिता ॥ 39 ॥
3.5.m: Moving sideways and moving quickly, it should be known as tremulous; / and from turning while staying in the middle, it is proclaimed to be severed.

3.5.s:
parāṅmukhasyābhimukhī nivṛttā parikīrtitā ..
sarvatobhramaṇāccaiva recitetyabhidhīyate .. 3.24.40...
3.5.d:
पराङ्मुखस्याभिमुखी निवृत्ता परिकीर्तिता ॥
सर्वतोभ्रमणाच्चैव रेचितेत्यभिधीयते ॥ 3.24.40॥।
3.5.m: Facing toward what is turned away, it is proclaimed to be turned away; / and from rotating in all directions, it is designated as emptied.

3.5.s:
niścitodvāhanāccaiva tathaivodvāhitā matā ..
nīca vāmanakubjānāṃ gatau kāryā prakampitā .. 41 ..
3.5.d:
निश्चितोद्वाहनाच्चैव तथैवोद्वाहिता मता ॥
नीच वामनकुब्जानां गतौ कार्या प्रकम्पिता ॥ 41 ॥
3.5.m: And from a distinct raising, it is likewise considered raised up. / The tremulous [waist] should be performed in the gait of base people, dwarfs, and hunchbacks.

3.5.s:
vyāyāme tvatha saṃprāpte vyāvṛttaprekṣiteṣu ca ..
chinnā kāryā kaṭistajjñairnivṛttā vartiteṣu ca .. 42 ..
3.5.d:
व्यायामे त्वथ संप्राप्ते व्यावृत्तप्रेक्षितेषु च ॥
छिन्ना कार्या कटिस्तज्ज्ञैर्निवृत्ता वर्तितेषु च ॥ 42 ॥
3.5.m: When physical exercise occurs, and in glances cast looking backward, / the severed waist should be performed by experts, and the turned away in turned [movements].

3.5.s:
recitā recite kāryā anyā līlāgate tridhā ..
kampanaṃ valanaṃ caiva stambhanodvartane tathā ..43 ..
3.5.d:
रेचिता रेचिते कार्या अन्या लीलागते त्रिधा ॥
कम्पनं वलनं चैव स्तम्भनोद्वर्तने तथा ॥43 ॥
3.5.m: The emptied [waist] should be performed in the emptied [movement]; the other, in graceful gait, is threefold. / Shaking, turning, rigidifying, uplifting,

3.5.s:
vivartanaṃ ca pañcaiva ūrvoḥ karmāṇi nirdiśet ..
namanonnamane pārantyormahīpṛṣṭhedbhute yadā .. 44 ..
3.5.d:
विवर्तनं च पञ्चैव ऊर्वोः कर्माणि निर्दिशेत् ॥
नमनोन्नमने पारन्त्योर्महीपृष्ठेद्भुते यदा ॥ 44 ॥
3.5.m: and rolling over—one should indicate these as the five actions of the thighs. / When bending and raising [...] on the surface of the earth,

3.5.s:
sthitā pādatalāgreṇa kampitaṃ tattadiṣyate ..
gacchedabhyantaraṃ jānu śanairyadvalitaṃ tu tat .. 45 ..
3.5.d:
स्थिता पादतलाग्रेण कम्पितं तत्तदिष्यते ॥
गच्छेदभ्यन्तरं जानु शनैर्यद्वलितं तु तत् ॥ 45 ॥
3.5.m: standing on the tip of the sole of the foot, that is regarded as shaken. / When the knee slowly goes inward, that is turned.

3.5.s:
stambhanaṃ cāpi vijñeyamapavṛttakriyākulam ..
valitāviddhabhāvaṃ syādudvartanamathāpi ca .. 46 ..
3.5.d:
स्तम्भनं चापि विज्ञेयमपवृत्तक्रियाकुलम् ॥
वलिताविद्धभावं स्यादुद्वर्तनमथापि च ॥ 46 ॥
3.5.m: Rigidifying should also be understood as free from actions of turning away. / Uplifting would be having a state that is turned and cast about.

3.5.s:
pārṣṇirabhyantaraṃ gacchedyatra tatra nivartitam ..
gatiṣvadhamapātrāṇāṃ kampitaṃ saṃprayojayet .. 47 ..
3.5.d:
पार्ष्णिरभ्यन्तरं गच्छेद्यत्र तत्र निवर्तितम् ॥
गतिष्वधमपात्राणां कम्पितं संप्रयोजयेत् ॥ 47 ॥
3.5.m: Where the heel goes inward, there it is rolled over. / One should employ the shaken in the movements of base characters.

3.5.s:
valanaṃ caiva kartavyaṃ strīṇāṃ svairaparikrame ..
bhīmordhasaviṣādeṣu stambhanaṃ saṃprayojayet .. 48 ..
3.5.d:
वलनं चैव कर्तव्यं स्त्रीणां स्वैरपरिक्रमे ॥
भीमोर्धसविषादेषु स्तम्भनं संप्रयोजयेत् ॥ 48 ॥
3.5.m: And turning should be performed in the leisurely pacing of women. / In terror, [...] and dejection, one should employ rigidifying.

3.5.s:
vyāyāme tāṇḍave caiva kāryamudvartanaṃ tathā ..
vivartanaṃ ca kartavyaṃ saṃkramādiparikrame .. 49 ..
3.5.d:
व्यायामे ताण्डवे चैव कार्यमुद्वर्तनं तथा ॥
विवर्तनं च कर्तव्यं संक्रमादिपरिक्रमे ॥ 49 ॥
3.5.m: In physical exercise and in tāṇḍava dance, uplifting should likewise be performed; / and rolling over should be performed in pacing across, and the like.

3.5.s:
āvartitaṃ nataṃ kṣiptaṃ codvāhitamathāpi ca ..
parivṛttaṃ tathā pañca jaṅghākarmāṇi nirdiśet .. 3.24.50 ..
3.5.d:
आवर्तितं नतं क्षिप्तं चोद्वाहितमथापि च ॥
परिवृत्तं तथा पञ्च जङ्घाकर्माणि निर्दिशेत् ॥ 3.24.50 ॥
3.5.m: Whirled, bent, thrown, and also raised up, / as well as turned round—thus one should indicate the five actions of the shanks.

3.5.s:
āvartitaṃ tu vyatyāsādvāmadakṣiṇajaṅghayoḥ ..
jānvorākuñjanāccaiva nataṃ jñeyaṃ prayoktṛbhiḥ..51..
3.5.d:
आवर्तितं तु व्यत्यासाद्वामदक्षिणजङ्घयोः ॥
जान्वोराकुञ्जनाच्चैव नतं ज्ञेयं प्रयोक्तृभिः॥51॥
3.5.m: The whirled is from the crossing of the left and right shanks; / and from the bending of the knees, the bent should be known by performers.

3.5.s:
vikṣepāccaiva jaṃghāyāḥ kṣiptamityabhidhīyate ..
udvāhitaṃ tu vijñeyamūrūdvāhanakarmaṇā .. 52 ..
3.5.d:
विक्षेपाच्चैव जंघायाः क्षिप्तमित्यभिधीयते ॥
उद्वाहितं तु विज्ञेयमूरूद्वाहनकर्मणा ॥ 52 ॥
3.5.m: From the casting forth of the shank, it is termed thrown; / and raised up should be known by the action of raising the thigh.

3.5.s:
pratīpanayanaṃ yatra parivṛttaṃ tadiṣyate ..
āvartanaṃ prayoktavyaṃ vidūṣakaparikrame .. 53 ..
3.5.d:
प्रतीपनयनं यत्र परिवृत्तं तदिष्यते ॥
आवर्तनं प्रयोक्तव्यं विदूषकपरिक्रमे ॥ 53 ॥
3.5.m: Where there is bringing backward, that is regarded as turned round. / The whirling should be employed in the pacing of the jester.

3.5.s:
nataṃ cāpi hi kartavyaṃ sthānāsanagatādiṣu ..
kṣiptaṃ vyāyāmayogeṣu tāṇḍaveṣu prayojayet .. 54 ..
3.5.d:
नतं चापि हि कर्तव्यं स्थानासनगतादिषु ॥
क्षिप्तं व्यायामयोगेषु ताण्डवेषु प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 54 ॥
3.5.m: And the bent should be performed in postures, sittings, gaits, and the like. / One should employ the thrown in exercises and in tāṇḍava dances.

3.5.s:
tathā codvāhitaṃ kāryamāviddhagamanādiṣu ..
tāṇḍavādau prayoktavyaṃ parivṛttaṃ prayoktṛbhiḥ .. 55 ..
3.5.d:
तथा चोद्वाहितं कार्यमाविद्धगमनादिषु ॥
ताण्डवादौ प्रयोक्तव्यं परिवृत्तं प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥ 55 ॥
3.5.m: Likewise, the raised up should be performed in sweeping movements and the like. / The turned round should be employed by performers in tāṇḍava and other [dances].

3.5.s:
udghāṭitasamaścaiva......,.saṃcaraḥ ..
añcitaḥ kuñcitaścaiva pādaḥ pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 56 ..
3.5.d:
उद्घाटितसमश्चैव॥॥॥,.संचरः ॥
अञ्चितः कुञ्चितश्चैव पादः पञ्चविधः स्मृतः ॥ 56 ॥
3.5.m: Striking the ground, flat, [...] moving, / arched, and contracted—the foot is traditionally said to be of five kinds.

3.5.s:
sthitvā pādatalāgreṇa pārṣṇirbhūmau nipātyate ..
yasya pādasya karaṇātsa taddhaṭita ucyate.. .. 57 ..
3.5.d:
स्थित्वा पादतलाग्रेण पार्ष्णिर्भूमौ निपात्यते ॥
यस्य पादस्य करणात्स तद्धटित उच्यते॥ ॥ 57 ॥
3.5.m: Having stood on the tip of the sole of the foot, the heel is brought down on the ground: / by the performance of which foot that is done, it is called striking the ground.

3.5.s:
kāryo'nuraktakaraṇe (caiva) pracāre lalite tathā ..
( svabhāvaracito bhūmau samasthānaḥ samaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 58 ..
3.5.d:
कार्योऽनुरक्तकरणे (चैव) प्रचारे ललिते तथा ॥
( स्वभावरचितो भूमौ समस्थानः समः स्मृतः ॥ 58 ॥
3.5.m: it should be performed in an impassioned action, and likewise in graceful gait. / Natural upon the ground, in an even position, it is known as sama;

3.5.s:
eṣa kāryaḥ sadā pādaḥ svabhāvābhinayāśrayaḥ ..
utkṣiptā tu bhavetpārṣṇiḥ pāde'gratalasaṃcare .. 59 ..
3.5.d:
एष कार्यः सदा पादः स्वभावाभिनयाश्रयः ॥
उत्क्षिप्ता तु भवेत्पार्ष्णिः पादेऽग्रतलसंचरे ॥ 59 ॥
3.5.m: this foot should always be performed relying on natural representation. / But the heel is raised in the foot moving on its tip;

3.5.s:
nikṣiptarecite bhrānte pāde yastāḍito bhavet ..
lalitaścāyameva syātpādo recitasaṃjñitaḥ .. 3.24.60 ..
3.5.d:
निक्षिप्तरेचिते भ्रान्ते पादे यस्ताडितो भवेत् ॥
ललितश्चायमेव स्यात्पादो रेचितसंज्ञितः ॥ 3.24.60 ॥
3.5.m: when the foot placed, emptied, and turned is struck, / this graceful foot is called recita.

3.5.s:
eṣa pradānasaṃcāre lalitodvahitaṃ bhavet ..
ukṣiptāgratalaḥ pādaḥ kathitastu tathāñcitaḥ .. 61 ..
3.5.d:
एष प्रदानसंचारे ललितोद्वहितं भवेत् ॥
उक्षिप्ताग्रतलः पादः कथितस्तु तथाञ्चितः ॥ 61 ॥
3.5.m: This should be a graceful lifting in the movement of offering gifts. / But the foot with the tip of the sole raised is declared añcita;

3.5.s:
nānābhramaṇakāleṣu kāryaḥ pādo'yamañcitaḥ ..
pādaḥ kuñcitamadhyo'yaṃ bhavetkuñcitasaṃjñitaḥ .. 62 ..
3.5.d:
नानाभ्रमणकालेषु कार्यः पादोऽयमञ्चितः ॥
पादः कुञ्चितमध्योऽयं भवेत्कुञ्चितसंज्ञितः ॥ 62 ॥
3.5.m: this añcita foot should be performed at times of various whirlings. / This foot with a bent middle is called kuñcita;

3.5.s:
atikrāntābhigamane pādametatprayojayet ..
ekapādapracāro yaḥ sa cārītyeva saṃjñitaḥ .. 63 ..
3.5.d:
अतिक्रान्ताभिगमने पादमेतत्प्रयोजयेत् ॥
एकपादप्रचारो यः स चारीत्येव संज्ञितः ॥ 63 ॥
3.5.m: one should employ this foot in stepping forward. / That movement of a single foot is named cārī;

3.5.s:
dvipādakramaṇaṃ yatra karaṇaṃ nāma tadbhavet ..
karaṇānāṃ samāyogaḥ khaṇḍa ityabhidhīyate .. 64 ..
3.5.d:
द्विपादक्रमणं यत्र करणं नाम तद्भवेत् ॥
करणानां समायोगः खण्ड इत्यभिधीयते ॥ 64 ॥
3.5.m: where there is movement of both feet, that becomes a karaṇa; / a combination of karaṇas is termed a khaṇḍa;

3.5.s:
dvābhyāṃ tribhirvā yadi vā caturbhiryuktaṃ bhavenmaṇḍalameva nāmnā ..
ityaṅgakarmābhihitaṃ bravīmi nibodha rājaṃstvamupāṅgakarma .. 65 .. ..
3.25
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
kṣāntā bhayānakā hāsyā karuṇā hyadbhutā tathā ..
raudrā vīrā ca bībhatsā vijñeyā rasadṛṣṭayaḥ .. 1..
snigdhā hṛṣṭā ca jihmā ca kruddhā bhītā ca lajjitā ..
tṛptātha vismitā saumyā sthāyibhāveṣu dṛṣṭayaḥ .. 2 ..
malinā kekarā śrāntā cābhitaptātha viplutā .. ... 3 ..
viṣaṇṇā śaṅkitā caiva trastā śokā nimīlitā ..
vibhrāntā kuñcitā śūnyā muktalā ca vitarkitā ..
madirā lalitā mlānā ityevaṃ dṛṣṭisaṃgrahaḥ .. 4 ..
ṣaḍtriṃśaddṛṣṭayo hyetā nāmato'bhihitā mayā ..
sabhrūkṣepakaṭākṣā tu kāntā jñeyā samañjasī .. 5 ..
udavṛttapuṭapakṣmāgrā calattārā bhayānakā ..
kiñcidākuñcitapuṭā hāsyavibhrāntatārakā .. 6 ..
3.5.d:
द्वाभ्यां त्रिभिर्वा यदि वा चतुर्भिर्युक्तं भवेन्मण्डलमेव नाम्ना ॥
इत्यङ्गकर्माभिहितं ब्रवीमि निबोध राजंस्त्वमुपाङ्गकर्म ॥ 65 ॥ ॥
3.25
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
क्षान्ता भयानका हास्या करुणा ह्यद्भुता तथा ॥
रौद्रा वीरा च बीभत्सा विज्ञेया रसदृष्टयः ॥ 1॥
स्निग्धा हृष्टा च जिह्मा च क्रुद्धा भीता च लज्जिता ॥
तृप्ताथ विस्मिता सौम्या स्थायिभावेषु दृष्टयः ॥ 2 ॥
मलिना केकरा श्रान्ता चाभितप्ताथ विप्लुता ॥ ॥। 3 ॥
विषण्णा शङ्किता चैव त्रस्ता शोका निमीलिता ॥
विभ्रान्ता कुञ्चिता शून्या मुक्तला च वितर्किता ॥
मदिरा ललिता म्लाना इत्येवं दृष्टिसंग्रहः ॥ 4 ॥
षड्त्रिंशद्दृष्टयो ह्येता नामतोऽभिहिता मया ॥
सभ्रूक्षेपकटाक्षा तु कान्ता ज्ञेया समञ्जसी ॥ 5 ॥
उदवृत्तपुटपक्ष्माग्रा चलत्तारा भयानका ॥
किञ्चिदाकुञ्चितपुटा हास्यविभ्रान्ततारका ॥ 6 ॥
3.5.m:
when combined with two, three, or four, it is by name a maṇḍala. / Thus the action of the major limbs has been declared; listen now, O king, to the action of the minor limbs.
3.25
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Kāntā, bhayānakā, hāsyā, karuṇā, and adbhutā, / raudrā, vīrā, and bībhatsā are to be known as the glances of the sentiments.
Snigdhā, hṛṣṭā, jihmā, kruddhā, bhītā, lajjitā, / tṛptā, then vismitā, and saumyā are the glances in the permanent emotional states.
Malinā, kekarā, śrāntā, abhitaptā, and viplutā, […]
viṣaṇṇā, śaṅkitā, trastā, śokā, nimīlitā, / vibhrāntā, kuñcitā, śūnyā, muktalā, and vitarkitā, / madirā, lalitā, and mlānā: such is the summary of glances.
These thirty-six glances have indeed been declared by me by name. / With a play of brows and sidelong glance, kāntā is to be known as charming;
bhayānakā has inverted eyelids and eyelash-tips, with trembling pupil; / hāsyā has slightly contracted lids and a wandering pupil.

पतितोर्ध्वपुटा सास्रा करुणा नष्टतारका ॥
किञ्चित्कुञ्चितपक्ष्माग्रा किञ्चिदुद्वृत्ततारका ॥ 7 ॥
समा विकसिता चैव साद्भुता दृष्टिरिष्यते ॥
उद्भूता कथिता रौद्रा भ्रुकुटी कुटिला तथा ॥ 8 ॥
उत्फुल्लमध्या वीरा तु कथिता समतारका ॥
बीभत्सा कथिता दृष्टिरपाङ्गाक्षिप्ततारका ॥9॥
ध्यानादनिमिषा शान्ता ह्यधोमार्गविचारिणी ॥
व्याकोशमध्या मधुरा स्निग्धा प्रहसिता मता ॥ 3.25.10 ॥
उत्फुल्लमध्या प्रचला हृष्टा पर्यन्तवीक्षिणी ॥
जिह्माधोगततारा च गूढा मग्ना निरीक्षिणी ॥ 11 ॥
भ्रुकुटीकुटिला क्रुद्धा तथा निष्टब्धतारका ॥
आकुंचिता लज्जिता स्यात्तथा निश्चलतारका ॥ 12 ॥
सत्त्वमद्भिरतीवेष्टा दृप्ता विकसिता भवेत ॥
समा विकसितापाङ्गा विस्मिता सा निगद्यते ॥ 13 ॥
समा सौम्या विनिर्दिष्टा तथा च समतारका ॥
आकुञ्चितपुटा भीता रूक्षा व्यावृत्ततारका ॥ 14 ॥

आकुञ्चितपुटा या तु दृष्टिराकेकरा भवेत् ॥ 15 ॥
किञ्चिदुन्नामितपुटा शान्ता सा तु विधीयते ॥
अभितप्ता तथा मन्दा मन्दतारापुटा तु या ॥ 16 ॥
विप्लुताविप्लुता प्रोक्ता स्रस्ता विस्फुरिता च या ॥
किञ्चिन्निष्टब्धतारा तु विषण्णा दृष्टिरुच्यते ॥ 17 ॥
अनवस्थिततारा च शङ्किता परिकीर्तिता ॥
रूक्षा ललित तारा च प्रताख्या सभया भवेत् ॥ 18 ॥
उत्फुल्ला तु विशोकाख्या तथा च निमिषेक्षणा ॥
अनवस्थितनेत्रा च विभ्रान्ता भ्रान्ततारका ॥ 19 ॥
कुंचिता कुंचिता दृष्टिः किञ्चिदञ्चिततारका ॥
स्थिततारापुटा शून्या संक्षुब्धा समदर्शना ॥ 3.25.20 ॥
प्रस्पन्दमानपक्ष्याग्रा मुकुला मुक्तला भवेत् ॥
उद्वृत्तपुटपक्ष्मा तु वितर्का स्तब्धतारका ॥ 21 ॥
उत्फुल्ला मदिरा नाम तथा वलिततारका ॥
फुल्लितान्ता सलावण्या सस्मिता ललिता मता ॥ 22 ॥

3.5.d:
प्रलूनपक्ष्मा सा साग्रा ग्लानाख्या मुकुलीकृता ॥
कान्ता दृष्टिः कटाक्षे तु घातने तु भयानका ॥ 23 ॥
हास्या हास्ये च विज्ञेया करुणा करुणे रसे ॥
स्वद्भुते चाद्भुता कार्या रौद्री रौद्रे विधीयते ॥ 24 ॥
वीरा वीरे च कर्तव्या बीभत्सा च जुगुप्सिते ॥
शान्ता शान्ते तु निर्दिष्टा स्निग्धा स्निग्धावलोकने ॥ 25 ॥
हृष्टा हृष्टे तु कर्तव्या जिह्मा कार्याभ्यसूयिते ॥
क्रुद्धा क्रुद्धे तु निर्दिष्टा भीता भीते तथा भवेत्॥ ॥ 26 ॥
लज्जिता लज्जिताख्या स्याद्दृप्तोत्साहगतेषु च ॥
विस्मिता विस्मये दृष्टिः सौम्या सौम्यावलोकने ॥ 27 ॥
मलिना विरहे कार्या सम्भोगे केकरा भवेत् ॥
श्रान्ता श्रान्तस्य कर्तव्या निर्वेदे त्वभितप्तका ॥ 28 ॥
विप्लुताख्या तु दैन्ये स्याद्विषादे तु विषण्णिका ॥
शंकिते शंकिता चैव त्रस्ते त्रस्ता विधीयते ॥ 29 ॥

ज्ञाने विशोका च तथा स्पर्शे कार्या निमीलिता ॥
विभ्रान्ता विभ्रमे कार्या कुंचिता सूक्ष्मदर्शने॥। 3.25.30 ॥
चिन्तान्वितस्य शून्या स्यान्मुक्तला घ्राणकर्मणि ॥
वितर्के तु वितर्का स्यान्मदे तु मदिरा भवेत् ॥ 31 ॥
स्त्रीणां हेलासु ललिता ग्लाने ग्लाना विधीयते ॥
उत्सेधश्च निमेषश्च प्रसारितविवर्तिते ॥ 32 ॥
आकुञ्चितं समं चैव स्फुरितं विहतं ततः ॥
ताडितं पुटयोः कर्म नवधा परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 33 ॥
समागमः पुटानां यः स निमेष इति स्मृतः ॥
विश्लेषश्चैव यस्ताभ्यां स उन्मेषः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 34 ॥
प्रसारितौ पुटौ यत्र भवेत्तद्धि विवर्तितम् ॥
आकुञ्चिताभ्यां ताभ्यां तु ज्ञेयमाकुञ्चितं बुधैः ॥ 35 ॥
स्वभावपुटसंस्थानं समं तद्धि प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
पुटौ प्रस्फुरितौ यत्र स्फुरितं तदिहोच्यते ॥ 36 ॥
3.5.m:
the sorrowless is in knowledge, and the closed should be used in touch. / The bewildered should be used in confusion, and the contracted in viewing subtle things;
the vacant is of one overcome by worry, and the released in the act of smelling. / In deliberation it is the reflective, and in intoxication it should be the intoxicated [gaze];
the graceful is prescribed in the playful dalliance of women, and the languid in exhaustion. / Elevation, closing, opening, rolling,
contracting, level, throbbing, striking, / and beating: the movement of the eyelids is proclaimed to be ninefold.
The coming together of the eyelids is known as closing, / and the separation between them is proclaimed as opening.
Where the two eyelids are widened, that is rolling; / when they are contracted, it should be known by the wise as contracting.
The natural position of the eyelids is proclaimed as level; / where the two eyelids quiver, it is here called throbbing.

स्रस्तमूलौ पुटौ यत्र तद्धि ताडितमुच्यते ॥ 37 ॥
गन्धस्पर्शे तथानिष्टे ज्ञेयमाकुञ्चितं बुधैः ॥
विस्मयार्थे तथा वीरे तच्च कार्यं प्रसाधितम् ॥ 38 ॥
शृङ्गारे तु समं कार्यमभिघातेऽवताडितम् ॥

क्रोधे विवर्तितं कार्यं निमेषोन्मेषयोः समम् ॥ ॥ 3.25.40 ॥
वलनं भ्रमणं चैव चलनं संप्रणाशनम् ॥

उद्वर्तः प्राकृतं चैव तारकाकर्म चेष्यते ॥
