3.5.d:
तथा चापाङ्गसंचारादुद्धर्षितमुदाहृतम् ॥
पातनं स्रस्तभावश्च निष्कामान्निष्क्रमं तथा ॥ 44 ॥
उद्वर्तनात्परावृत्तिः प्राकृतं तु स्वभावतः ॥
हास्ये तु वलनं कार्यं मदे भ्रमणमेव च ॥ 45 ॥
वीरे रसे स्याच्चलनं बीभत्से संप्रवेशनम् ॥
विवर्तितं तु शृङ्गारे पातनं करुणे रसे ॥ 46 ॥
भयानके निष्क्रमणं वीरे चोद्वर्तनं तथा ॥
प्राकृतं शेषभावे तु यथायोगं प्रयोजयेत्॥47॥
समं साचीकृतं च स्यादनुवृत्तमतः परम् ॥
आलोकितं चाल्लोकितमवलोकितमेव च ॥48॥
समतारं च सौम्यं च दृष्टिकर्म समं भवेत ॥
पक्ष्मान्तर्गततारं च साचीकृतमिहोच्यते ॥49॥
रूपनिर्वर्तनायुक्तमनुवृत्तमिति स्मृतम् ॥
सहसा दर्शनं यत्स्यात्तदालोकितमिष्यते॥3.25.50 ॥
ऊर्ध्वमुल्लोकितं ज्ञेयं सर्वतो लोकितं तथा ॥
विलोकितं तु पार्श्वाभ्यां पृष्ठतश्चावलोकितम् ॥51॥

3.5.s:
dṛṣṭīnāmanugaṃ caiva bhruvo karma prayojayet ..
yathā netraṃ prasarpeddhi nānābhāvarasāśrayam ..52..
netrasyānukrameṇaiva bhruvostu calanaṃ bhavet ..
utkṣepaḥ patanaṃ caiva bhrukuṭīcaturaṃ tathā .. 53 ..
nikuñcitaṃ kuñcitaṃ ca tathā svābhāvikaṃ bhavet ..
bhruvorudgamamutkṣepaḥ pātanaṃ patanaṃ bhavet .. 54 ..
dvayormūlordhavikṣepādbhrukuṭī parikīrtitā ..
caturaḥ kiñciducchvāsānmadhurāyatayā bhruvā .. 55 ..
ekasyā ubhayorvāpi syādudbhagnaṃ trikuñcitam ..
ekasyā lalitodyogādrecitaṃ nāma kīrtitam .. 56 ..
yathāsthite svabhāvasthe bhruvoḥ karma nibodha me ..
samutkṣepastu līlāyāḥ kāruṇyātpātanaṃ bhavet .. 57 ..
krodhe ca bhrukuṭī jñeyā śṛṅgāracaturaṃ tathā ..
kṣāmaṃ kṛśaṃ tu vijñeyaṃ phullaṃ vikasitaṃ bhavet .. 58 ..
3.5.d:
दृष्टीनामनुगं चैव भ्रुवो कर्म प्रयोजयेत् ॥
यथा नेत्रं प्रसर्पेद्धि नानाभावरसाश्रयम् ॥52॥
नेत्रस्यानुक्रमेणैव भ्रुवोस्तु चलनं भवेत् ॥
उत्क्षेपः पतनं चैव भ्रुकुटीचतुरं तथा ॥ 53 ॥
निकुञ्चितं कुञ्चितं च तथा स्वाभाविकं भवेत् ॥
भ्रुवोरुद्गममुत्क्षेपः पातनं पतनं भवेत् ॥ 54 ॥
द्वयोर्मूलोर्धविक्षेपाद्भ्रुकुटी परिकीर्तिता ॥
चतुरः किञ्चिदुच्छ्वासान्मधुरायतया भ्रुवा ॥ 55 ॥
एकस्या उभयोर्वापि स्यादुद्भग्नं त्रिकुञ्चितम् ॥
एकस्या ललितोद्योगाद्रेचितं नाम कीर्तितम् ॥ 56 ॥
यथास्थिते स्वभावस्थे भ्रुवोः कर्म निबोध मे ॥
समुत्क्षेपस्तु लीलायाः कारुण्यात्पातनं भवेत् ॥ 57 ॥
क्रोधे च भ्रुकुटी ज्ञेया शृङ्गारचतुरं तथा ॥
क्षामं कृशं तु विज्ञेयं फुल्लं विकसितं भवेत् ॥ 58 ॥

3.5.s:
sampūrṇaṃ pūrṇamityuktaṃ kampitaṃ paridhūnitam ..
śṛṅgabhinnaṃ kuñcitakaṃ saromāñcaṃ tathāvidham .. 59 ..
prākkṛtaṃ tu svabhāvasthaṃ mandaṃ proktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ ..
kṣāmaṃ duḥkhe tu kartavyaṃ phullaṃ harṣe prayojayet .. 3.25.60 ..
pūrṇaṃ tuṣṭe tu kartavyaṃ tathā roṣe ca kampitam ..
hāsye tvākuñcitaṃ sparśe saromāñcaṃ vidhīyate .. 61 ..
prākṛtaṃ tu svabhāvasthaṃ tvarthayogena yojayet ..
natā mandā vikṛṣṭā ca socchvāsā kūṇitānatā .. 62 ..
svābhāvike ca kartavyā prayoge nāsikā budhaiḥ ..
natānatā tu vijñeyā mandā natapuṭā bhavet .. 63 ..
vikṛṣṭā kuñcitā cordhvaṃ socchvāsā vāyupūritā ..
saṃkūṇanātkūṇitā syātsvabhāvasthā svanāsikā .. 64 ..
natā tu rucite kāryā mandā śoke vidhīyate ..
tīvragandhe vikṛṣṭā tu socchvāsā tu tathā priye .. 65 ..
3.5.d:
सम्पूर्णं पूर्णमित्युक्तं कम्पितं परिधूनितम् ॥
शृङ्गभिन्नं कुञ्चितकं सरोमाञ्चं तथाविधम् ॥ 59 ॥
प्राक्कृतं तु स्वभावस्थं मन्दं प्रोक्तं मनीषिभिः ॥
क्षामं दुःखे तु कर्तव्यं फुल्लं हर्षे प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 3.25.60 ॥
पूर्णं तुष्टे तु कर्तव्यं तथा रोषे च कम्पितम् ॥
हास्ये त्वाकुञ्चितं स्पर्शे सरोमाञ्चं विधीयते ॥ 61 ॥
प्राकृतं तु स्वभावस्थं त्वर्थयोगेन योजयेत् ॥
नता मन्दा विकृष्टा च सोच्छ्वासा कूणितानता ॥ 62 ॥
स्वाभाविके च कर्तव्या प्रयोगे नासिका बुधैः ॥
नतानता तु विज्ञेया मन्दा नतपुटा भवेत् ॥ 63 ॥
विकृष्टा कुञ्चिता चोर्ध्वं सोच्छ्वासा वायुपूरिता ॥
संकूणनात्कूणिता स्यात्स्वभावस्था स्वनासिका ॥ 64 ॥
नता तु रुचिते कार्या मन्दा शोके विधीयते ॥
तीव्रगन्धे विकृष्टा तु सोच्छ्वासा तु तथा प्रिये ॥ 65 ॥

3.5.s:
vikūṇitā jugupsāyāṃ śeṣā svābhāvikī matā ..
kūṇanaṃ khaṇḍanaṃ chinnaṃ mukitaṃ samatā tathā . 66 ..
3.5.d:
विकूणिता जुगुप्सायां शेषा स्वाभाविकी मता ॥
कूणनं खण्डनं छिन्नं मुकितं समता तथा । 66 ॥
3.5.m: wrinkled in disgust; the rest is regarded as natural. / Contracting, biting, severed, [shut], and also evenness:

3.5.s:
jihvādharoṣṭhamadaṃ ca dantakarmaṇi kārayeta ..
kuṭṭanaṃ bhaktavacchedaṃ khaṇḍanaṃ tu vighaṭṭanam .. 67 ..
3.5.d:
जिह्वाधरोष्ठमदं च दन्तकर्मणि कारयेत ॥
कुट्टनं भक्तवच्छेदं खण्डनं तु विघट्टनम् ॥ 67 ॥
3.5.m: these, with crushing by the tongue and lower lip, one should execute in actions of the teeth: / kuṭṭana (chattering) is the cutting of food, khaṇḍana (chewing) is rubbing together;

3.5.s:
chinnaṃ nikṛtameva syācchukktiṃ viddhameva ca ..
vyādhau tu kuṭṭanaṃ kāryamutsāhe khaṇḍanaṃ bhavet .. 68 ..
3.5.d:
छिन्नं निकृतमेव स्याच्छुक्क्तिं विद्धमेव च ॥
व्याधौ तु कुट्टनं कार्यमुत्साहे खण्डनं भवेत् ॥ 68 ॥
3.5.m: severed is cut off, and pierced is penetrated. / Chattering should be used in sickness, biting should occur in exertion;

3.5.s:
chinnaṃ krodhe paraṃ hāsye samaṃ śeṣeṣu kārayet ..
vivartanaṃ tathā kampo vimarśo'tha vigūhanam .. 69 ..
3.5.d:
छिन्नं क्रोधे परं हास्ये समं शेषेषु कारयेत् ॥
विवर्तनं तथा कम्पो विमर्शोऽथ विगूहनम् ॥ 69 ॥
3.5.m: severed in rage, another in laughter, and one should execute the even in the rest. / Turning around, trembling, deliberation, concealing,

3.5.s:
saṃdṛṣṭaśca samudraśca karmāṇyadharajāni ca ..
sṛkkā suvakrakaraṇaṃ vivartitamiti smṛtam .. 3.25.70 ..
3.5.d:
संदृष्टश्च समुद्रश्च कर्माण्यधरजानि च ॥
सृक्का सुवक्रकरणं विवर्तितमिति स्मृतम् ॥ 3.25.70 ॥
3.5.m: bitten, and pressed together are the actions of the lower lip. / The act of making the corner of the mouth very crooked is remembered as vivartita (turned around);

3.5.s:
vepanaṃ cāpi vijñeyamadharasya tu kampane ..
yo niṣkramo'dharasyātha sa visarga iti smṛtaḥ .. 71 ..
3.5.d:
वेपनं चापि विज्ञेयमधरस्य तु कम्पने ॥
यो निष्क्रमोऽधरस्याथ स विसर्ग इति स्मृतः ॥ 71 ॥
3.5.m: and shaking is to be known in kampana (trembling) of the lower lip; / and that which is the protruding of the lower lip is remembered as visarga (thrusting out);

3.5.s:
antaḥpraveśanaṃ caiva vinigūhitamucyate ..
dantoṣṭhapīḍanāccaiva saṃdaṣṭakamiti smṛtam .. 72 ..
3.5.d:
अन्तःप्रवेशनं चैव विनिगूहितमुच्यते ॥
दन्तोष्ठपीडनाच्चैव संदष्टकमिति स्मृतम् ॥ 72 ॥
3.5.m: and drawing inside is called vinigūhita (concealed); / and from the pressure of the teeth and lip it is remembered as saṃdaṣṭaka (bitten);

3.5.s:
piṇḍitābhyudgataścaiva samudgaka iti smṛtaḥ ..
vivartitamasūyāyāṃ roṣe kampitamiṣyate ..
bhayānake visargaśca karṣaṇe'tha nigūhanam .. 73 ..
3.5.d:
पिण्डिताभ्युद्गतश्चैव समुद्गक इति स्मृतः ॥
विवर्तितमसूयायां रोषे कम्पितमिष्यते ॥
भयानके विसर्गश्च कर्षणेऽथ निगूहनम् ॥ 73 ॥
3.5.m: and gathered and elevated is remembered as samudgaka (pursed). / Turned around is desired in envy, trembling in anger,

3.5.s:
tatonmādavikāreṣu sandaṣṭaṃ vīraraudrayoḥ ..
samudgamanakampāyāṃ śeṣe kāryaṃ svabhāvajam .. 74 ..
3.5.d:
ततोन्मादविकारेषु सन्दष्टं वीररौद्रयोः ॥
समुद्गमनकम्पायां शेषे कार्यं स्वभावजम् ॥ 74 ॥
3.5.m: thrusting out in the terrible [sentiment], and concealing in dragging; / then in the modifications of madness, bitten in the heroic and furious [sentiments], / samudgama (pursed) in trembling; in the rest the natural one should be used.

3.5.s:
upāṅgakarmābhihitaṃ tathaitaṃ mayā samāsena narendracandra ..
kāryaḥ prayatno'tra sadā budhena yasmādupāṅgāśrayameva nṛtyam .. 75 ..
3.5.d:
उपाङ्गकर्माभिहितं तथैतं मया समासेन नरेन्द्रचन्द्र ॥
कार्यः प्रयत्नोऽत्र सदा बुधेन यस्मादुपाङ्गाश्रयमेव नृत्यम् ॥ 75 ॥
3.5.m: Thus has this action of the minor limbs been declared by me in brief, O moon among kings; / an effort should always be made herein by the wise person, because dance rests entirely on the minor limbs.

3.6.s:
3.26
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
patākastripatākaśca tathā vaikartaremukhaḥ ..
ardhacandro hyaṭālaśca gurutuṇḍastathāparaḥ .. 1 ..
3.6.d:
3.26
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
पताकस्त्रिपताकश्च तथा वैकर्तरेमुखः ॥
अर्धचन्द्रो ह्यटालश्च गुरुतुण्डस्तथापरः ॥ 1 ॥
3.6.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Patāka (flag), tripatāka (three-fingered flag), and vaikartaremukha (kartarīmukha), / ardhacandra (crescent moon), arāla, and another, gurutuṇḍa (śukatuṇḍa);

3.6.s:
muṣṭiśca śikhirākhyaśca kapitthaḥ khaṭakāmukhaḥ ..
sūcyardhaḥ padmakośaśca mṛgaśīrṣo mṛgasya ca .. 2 ..
3.6.d:
मुष्टिश्च शिखिराख्यश्च कपित्थः खटकामुखः ॥
सूच्यर्धः पद्मकोशश्च मृगशीर्षो मृगस्य च ॥ 2 ॥
3.6.m: muṣṭi (fist), the one called śikhira (peak), kapittha (wood-apple), and khaṭakāmukha; / sūcyardha (half-needle), padmakośa (lotus-bud), mṛgaśīrṣa (deer-head) of the deer;

3.6.s:
lāṅgūlaḥ kālapadmaśca caturo bhramarastathā ..
haṃsāsyo haṃsapakṣaśca saṃdaṃśo mukulastathā .. 3 ..
3.6.d:
लाङ्गूलः कालपद्मश्च चतुरो भ्रमरस्तथा ॥
हंसास्यो हंसपक्षश्च संदंशो मुकुलस्तथा ॥ 3 ॥
3.6.m: lāṅgūla (tail), kālapadma (lotus), catura, and bhramara (bee); / haṃsāsya (swan-face), haṃsapakṣa (swan-wing), saṃdaṃśa (pincers), and mukula (bud)—

3.6.s:
asaṃyutāḥ karā hyete dvāviṃśatirudāhṛtāḥ ..
atha saṃyuktato hastāngadatastānnibodha me .. 4 ..
3.6.d:
असंयुताः करा ह्येते द्वाविंशतिरुदाहृताः ॥
अथ संयुक्ततो हस्तान्गदतस्तान्निबोध मे ॥ 4 ॥
3.6.m: these single-hand gestures are stated to be twenty-two. / Now learn from me the combined hand gestures as I declare them:

3.6.s:
aṃjaliśca kapotaśca karkaṭaḥ svastikastathā ..
khaṭako vardhamānaśca utsaṅgo niṣidhastathā .. 5 ..
3.6.d:
अंजलिश्च कपोतश्च कर्कटः स्वस्तिकस्तथा ॥
खटको वर्धमानश्च उत्सङ्गो निषिधस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
3.6.m: añjali, kapota (dove), karkaṭa (crab), and svastika; / khaṭaka, vardhamāna, utsaṅga, and niṣiddha;

3.6.s:
dolaḥ puṣpapuṭaścaiva tathā makara eva ca ..
gajadanto'vahitthaśca vardhamānastathaiva ca .. 6 ..
3.6.d:
दोलः पुष्पपुटश्चैव तथा मकर एव च ॥
गजदन्तोऽवहित्थश्च वर्धमानस्तथैव च ॥ 6 ॥
3.6.m: dola (swing), puṣpapuṭa (flower-casket), and likewise makara (sea-monster); / gajadanta (elephant-tusk), avahittha, and likewise vardhamāna—

3.6.s:
ete vai saṃyutā hastā mayā proktāstrayodaśa ..
nṛttahastāryupaścaiva bhūyo nāmni nibodhata .. 7 ..
3.6.d:
एते वै संयुता हस्ता मया प्रोक्तास्त्रयोदश ॥
नृत्तहस्तार्युपश्चैव भूयो नाम्नि निबोधत ॥ 7 ॥
3.6.m: these combined hands declared by me are thirteen. / Learn also further the names of the dance-hands:

3.6.s:
caturasrastathā vṛttastathā laghumukhau smṛtau ..
tathā caiva tu vijñeyau hyarālakhaṭakāmukhau .. 8 ..
3.6.d:
चतुरस्रस्तथा वृत्तस्तथा लघुमुखौ स्मृतौ ॥
तथा चैव तु विज्ञेयौ ह्यरालखटकामुखौ ॥ 8 ॥
3.6.m: caturasra (square), vṛtta (circular), and both are known as laghumukha; / and likewise to be known are arāla and khaṭakāmukha;

3.6.s:
āviddhavakrasaṃvyāsvau recitāvarddharecitau ..
avahitthaḥ pallavito nitambaḥ keśavardhanau .. 9 ..
3.6.d:
आविद्धवक्रसंव्यास्वौ रेचितावर्द्धरेचितौ ॥
अवहित्थः पल्लवितो नितम्बः केशवर्धनौ ॥ 9 ॥
3.6.m: āviddhavakra and saṃvyāsu, recita and ardharecita; / avahittha, pallavita, nitamba, and both keśavardhana;

3.6.s:
latākhyau karihastau ca pakṣodyotā'rthavardhitau ..
jñeyau garuḍapakṣau ca daṇḍapakṣau tathaiva ca ...3.26.10...
3.6.d:
लताख्यौ करिहस्तौ च पक्षोद्योताऽर्थवर्धितौ ॥
ज्ञेयौ गरुडपक्षौ च दण्डपक्षौ तथैव च ॥.3.26.10॥।
3.6.m: both called latā (creeper) and karihasta (elephant-trunk), pakṣodyota and arthavardhita; / and garuḍapakṣa and daṇḍapakṣa are to be known;

3.6.s:
ūrdhvamaṇḍalajau caiva pārśvamaṃḍalājāvapi ..
pārśvārdhamaṇḍalau caiva uromaṇḍalakau tathā..11..
3.6.d:
ऊर्ध्वमण्डलजौ चैव पार्श्वमंडलाजावपि ॥
पार्श्वार्धमण्डलौ चैव उरोमण्डलकौ तथा॥11॥
3.6.m: and both ūrdhvamaṇḍala, and both pārśvamaṇḍala; / both pārśvārdhamaṇḍala, and both uromaṇḍalaka;

3.6.s:
iṣṭasvastikakāvanyau tathā vai padmakauśikau ..
allipallavasaṃjñau ca tathā colvanasaṃjñitau .. 12 ..
3.6.d:
इष्टस्वस्तिककावन्यौ तथा वै पद्मकौशिकौ ॥
अल्लिपल्लवसंज्ञौ च तथा चोल्वनसंज्ञितौ ॥ 12 ॥
3.6.m: two others, iṣṭasvastika, and padmakośa; / both named allipallava, and both designated ulbaṇa;

3.6.s:
lalitau valitau caiva jñeyā nṛtyakarāḥ sadā ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi karāṇāṃ karmalakṣaṇam .. 13 ..
3.6.d:
ललितौ वलितौ चैव ज्ञेया नृत्यकराः सदा ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि कराणां कर्मलक्षणम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.6.m: lalita and valita are always to be known as dance-hands. / Hereafter I shall declare the characteristics and functions of the hands.

3.6.s:
prasāritāgrā sahitā yasyāṅgulyo bhavanti hi ..
kuñcitaśca tathāṅguṣṭhaḥ sa patāka iti smṛtaḥ .. 14 ..
3.6.d:
प्रसारिताग्रा सहिता यस्याङ्गुल्यो भवन्ति हि ॥
कुञ्चितश्च तथाङ्गुष्ठः स पताक इति स्मृतः ॥ 14 ॥
3.6.m: That [hand] whose fingers are extended at the tips and joined together, / and the thumb is contracted, is remembered as patāka (flag).

3.6.s:
eṣa prahāragrahaṇe rodhane syātpratāpane ..
calitāṅgulirapyeṣa vāyuvṛṣṭinirūpaṇe .. 15 ..
3.6.d:
एष प्रहारग्रहणे रोधने स्यात्प्रतापने ॥
चलिताङ्गुलिरप्येष वायुवृष्टिनिरूपणे ॥ 15 ॥
3.6.m: This may be used in taking a blow, checking, and scorching; / with fingers moving, it [serves] in depicting wind and rain;

3.6.s:
ūrdhvagaśca tathotsāhe chatrādiṣvapyadhomukhaḥ ..
puṣkaraprahitastāle samaḥ pracalitāṅguliḥ .. 16 ..
3.6.d:
ऊर्ध्वगश्च तथोत्साहे छत्रादिष्वप्यधोमुखः ॥
पुष्करप्रहितस्ताले समः प्रचलिताङ्गुलिः ॥ 16 ॥
3.6.m: turned upward in enthusiasm, turned downward in parasols and the like; / placed on a drum in rhythm, level with trembling fingers,

3.6.s:
pakṣmotkṣepe recitaka utkṣiptaścaiva dhāraṇe ..
asyaikānāmikā vakrā tripatākā tathā bhavet .. 17 ..
3.6.d:
पक्ष्मोत्क्षेपे रेचितक उत्क्षिप्तश्चैव धारणे ॥
अस्यैकानामिका वक्रा त्रिपताका तथा भवेत् ॥ 17 ॥
3.6.m: in recitaka of eyebrow-raising, and raised up in supporting. / When the ring finger of this is bent, it becomes tripatāka (three-fingered flag).

3.6.s:
āvāhane prayuñjīta mukuṭābhinaye'pyuta ...
acalāṅgulirapyeṣa laghupakṣinirūpaṇe 118 ..
3.6.d:
आवाहने प्रयुञ्जीत मुकुटाभिनयेऽप्युत ॥।
अचलाङ्गुलिरप्येष लघुपक्षिनिरूपणे 118 ॥
3.6.m: One should employ it in invocation and in acting out a crown, / and with motionless fingers in indicating a small bird.

3.6.s:
tayānāsikayā kāryaṃ tathaivāśrupramārjanam ..
maṅgalasparśanaṃ kāryaṃ śirasaśca niveśanam .. 19 ..
3.6.d:
तयानासिकया कार्यं तथैवाश्रुप्रमार्जनम् ॥
मङ्गलस्पर्शनं कार्यं शिरसश्च निवेशनम् ॥ 19 ॥
3.6.m: With that [hand] at the nose, touching auspicious objects / and wiping away tears are to be performed, as well as placing [the hand] on the head.

3.6.s:
śrotrasaṃvaraṇaṃ caiva kāryaṃ bhūmimukhena tu ..
bhujaṅgānāmābhinayaṃ bhramarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 3.26.20 ..
3.6.d:
श्रोत्रसंवरणं चैव कार्यं भूमिमुखेन तु ॥
भुजङ्गानामाभिनयं भ्रमराणां तथैव च ॥ 3.26.20 ॥
3.6.m: Covering the ears should be performed with [the hand] facing the earth, / and likewise the depiction of serpents and bees.

3.6.s:
tripatākā yadā haste bhavetpṛṣṭhāvalokinī ..
tarjanī tu tadā jñeyaḥ kartarīmukhasaṃjñakaḥ..21..
3.6.d:
त्रिपताका यदा हस्ते भवेत्पृष्ठावलोकिनी ॥
तर्जनी तु तदा ज्ञेयः कर्तरीमुखसंज्ञकः॥21॥
3.6.m: When the tripatākā hand has the forefinger looking backward, / it is then known by the name kartarīmukha.

3.6.s:
kāryo'yaṃ parivāreṣu bhinnaśca pataneṣu ca..
anāmikā tu sāṅguṣṭhā ardhacandre kare bhavet..22..
3.6.d:
कार्योऽयं परिवारेषु भिन्नश्च पतनेषु च॥
अनामिका तु साङ्गुष्ठा अर्धचन्द्रे करे भवेत्॥22॥
3.6.m: This is to be used for retinues, separations, and fallings. / When the ring finger is joined with the thumb, it is the ardhacandra hand.

3.6.s:
bālacandrābhinayane bālasyāttaravastathā..
mekhalāṃ jaghanaṃ caiva kuryāccānena kuṇḍalam..23..
3.6.d:
बालचन्द्राभिनयने बालस्यात्तरवस्तथा॥
मेखलां जघनं चैव कुर्याच्चानेन कुण्डलम्॥23॥
3.6.m: In representing the crescent moon, and similarly the limbs of a child, / one should portray a girdle, the hips, and an earring with this.

3.6.s:
khaṇḍapradeśinī kāryā aṅgulyaḥ kuṃcitāstathā..
śeṣā bhinnordhvavalitā mrarāleṅgulayaḥ kare .. 24 ..
3.6.d:
खण्डप्रदेशिनी कार्या अङ्गुल्यः कुंचितास्तथा॥
शेषा भिन्नोर्ध्ववलिता म्ररालेङ्गुलयः करे ॥ 24 ॥
3.6.m: The forefinger should be bent and the [other] fingers curled; / when the remaining fingers are separated and bent upward, the fingers are in the arāla hand.

3.6.s:
gāmbhīryasattvaśauṃḍīryakeśasaṃgrahaṇādiṣu ..
svedasya cāpanayane śeṣe caiṣa karo bhavet .. . .. 25 ..
3.6.d:
गाम्भीर्यसत्त्वशौंडीर्यकेशसंग्रहणादिषु ॥
स्वेदस्य चापनयने शेषे चैष करो भवेत् ॥ ॥। 25 ॥
3.6.m: In [representing] depth, courage, valor, grasping hair, and the like, / and in wiping away sweat, this hand is used for the rest.

3.6.s:
mrarālaḥ śukatuṇḍaśca vakritānāmikāṅguliḥ ..
nāhantvamityathaitena nityaṃ cābhinayedbudhaḥ .. 26 ..
3.6.d:
म्ररालः शुकतुण्डश्च वक्रितानामिकाङ्गुलिः ॥
नाहन्त्वमित्यथैतेन नित्यं चाभिनयेद्बुधः ॥ 26 ॥
3.6.m: The arāla with the ring finger bent becomes śukatuṇḍa. / With this, the wise actor should always represent 'not I' or 'not you'.

3.6.s:
aṅgulyo yasya hastasya talamadhye'grasaṃsthitāḥ ..
tāsāmuparitāṅguṣṭhaḥ sa muṣṭiriti saṃjñitaḥ .. 27 ..
3.6.d:
अङ्गुल्यो यस्य हस्तस्य तलमध्येऽग्रसंस्थिताः ॥
तासामुपरिताङ्गुष्ठः स मुष्टिरिति संज्ञितः ॥ 27 ॥
3.6.m: The hand whose fingertips are positioned in the middle of the palm, / with the thumb over them, is designated muṣṭi.

3.6.s:
eṣa prahāre vyāyāme nirdayastanapīḍane .. .
sandhāraṇe'siyaṣṭyośca grahaṇe kuntadaṇḍayoḥ .. 28 ..
3.6.d:
एष प्रहारे व्यायामे निर्दयस्तनपीडने ॥ ।
सन्धारणेऽसियष्ट्योश्च ग्रहणे कुन्तदण्डयोः ॥ 28 ॥
3.6.m: This is used in striking, wrestling, merciless squeezing of the breasts, / holding a sword or a staff, and grasping a spear or a rod.

3.6.s:
ūrdhvāṅguṣṭho'yameva syātkaraḥ śikharasaṃjñitaḥ ..
eṣa raśmigrahe kāryaścāpāṅkuśadhanurgrahe ..29.. .
3.6.d:
ऊर्ध्वाङ्गुष्ठोऽयमेव स्यात्करः शिखरसंज्ञितः ॥
एष रश्मिग्रहे कार्यश्चापाङ्कुशधनुर्ग्रहे ॥29॥ ।
3.6.m: This very [hand] with the thumb raised is the hand named śikhara; / this is to be used in holding the reins, a bow, a goad, or a weapon.

3.6.s:
muṣṭimadhyagatoṅguṣṭhaḥ kapittha iti kīrtitaḥ ..
anenābhinayaḥ kāryo madhye cakre śare tathā .. 3.26.30 ..
3.6.d:
मुष्टिमध्यगतोङ्गुष्ठः कपित्थ इति कीर्तितः ॥
अनेनाभिनयः कार्यो मध्ये चक्रे शरे तथा ॥ 3.26.30 ॥
3.6.m: When the thumb enters the middle of the muṣṭi, it is called kapittha; / with this, dramatic depiction should be made of the middle, a discus, and an arrow.

3.6.s:
utkṣiptavakrā tu yadānāmikā sakanīyasī ...
asyaiva tu kapitthasya tataḥ syātkhaṭakāmukhaḥ ..31..
3.6.d:
उत्क्षिप्तवक्रा तु यदानामिका सकनीयसी ॥।
अस्यैव तु कपित्थस्य ततः स्यात्खटकामुखः ॥31॥
3.6.m: When the ring finger and the little finger of this very kapittha / are raised and bent, it becomes khaṭakāmukha.

3.6.s:
hotre chatragraha caiva karṣaṇe vyajane tathā ..
sragdāmadhāraṇe kāryo hyasaṅkocosya saṃgrahaḥ ..32...
3.6.d:
होत्रे छत्रग्रह चैव कर्षणे व्यजने तथा ॥
स्रग्दामधारणे कार्यो ह्यसङ्कोचोस्य संग्रहः ॥32॥।
3.6.m: It should be used in offering oblations, holding an umbrella, pulling, fanning, / and holding a garland; its grasp should be uncompressed.

3.6.s:
prasṛtā tarjanī cātra yadā sūcīmukhastadā ..
niṣpādane cābhinayennetraśakramaheśayoḥ .. 33 ..
3.6.d:
प्रसृता तर्जनी चात्र यदा सूचीमुखस्तदा ॥
निष्पादने चाभिनयेन्नेत्रशक्रमहेशयोः ॥ 33 ॥
3.6.m: And when the forefinger here is extended, it is then sūcīmukha; / it should represent manifestation, the eye, Śakra, and Maheśvara.

3.6.s:
asyāṅgulyastu vipulāḥ sahāṃṅguṣṭhena kuñcitāḥ ...
ūrdhvāhaṃsanakhasyaiva sa bhavetpadmakośakaḥ .. 34 ..
3.6.d:
अस्याङ्गुल्यस्तु विपुलाः सहांङ्गुष्ठेन कुञ्चिताः ॥।
ऊर्ध्वाहंसनखस्यैव स भवेत्पद्मकोशकः ॥ 34 ॥
3.6.m: When the fingers of this [hand] are spread and bent along with the thumb, / with the nails pointing upward like a goose, it is padmakośa.

3.6.s:
śliṣṭoṅguṣṭho nimnamadhyaḥ patākohiśiro bhavet ..
salilasya pradāne tu kāryā tena ca sūcanam .. .. 35 ..
3.6.d:
श्लिष्टोङ्गुष्ठो निम्नमध्यः पताकोहिशिरो भवेत् ॥
सलिलस्य प्रदाने तु कार्या तेन च सूचनम् ॥ ॥ 35 ॥
3.6.m: When the thumb is joined and the center is hollowed, the patāka becomes ahiśiras; / it is to be used in offering water and in making a gesture of indication.

3.6.s:
adhomukhīnāṃ sarvāsāmaṅgulīnāṃ yadā bhavet ..
kaniṣṭhāṅguṣṭhakā cordhvā tadā syānmṛgaśīrṣakaḥ .. 36 ..
3.6.d:
अधोमुखीनां सर्वासामङ्गुलीनां यदा भवेत् ॥
कनिष्ठाङ्गुष्ठका चोर्ध्वा तदा स्यान्मृगशीर्षकः ॥ 36 ॥
3.6.m: When all the fingers are turned face down, / and the little finger and the thumb are raised, it is mṛgaśīrṣa.

3.6.s:
sūcite cchedite kāryaṃ śakyā svoccālane tathā ..
tretāgnisaṃsthitā madhyā tarjanyaṅguṣṭhayoryadā .. 37 ..
3.6.d:
सूचिते च्छेदिते कार्यं शक्या स्वोच्चालने तथा ॥
त्रेताग्निसंस्थिता मध्या तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठयोर्यदा ॥ 37 ॥
3.6.m: It should be used in pointing, cutting, capacity, and raising oneself. / When the middle finger, forefinger, and thumb are arranged like the three sacrificial fires,

3.6.s:
kāṅgule nāmikā vakrā tathā cordhvā kanīyasī ..
anena khalu kartavyaṃ phalānāṃ tu nirūpaṇam .. 38 ..
3.6.d:
काङ्गुले नामिका वक्रा तथा चोर्ध्वा कनीयसी ॥
अनेन खलु कर्तव्यं फलानां तु निरूपणम् ॥ 38 ॥
3.6.m: the ring finger bent, and the little finger likewise raised, / it is kāṅgula; with this, indeed, the depiction of fruits should be made.

3.6.s:
āvartyante karatale yasyāṅgulyaḥ karasya vai ..
pārśvāgatavikīrṇāśca kolapadma iti smṛtaḥ .. 39 ..
3.6.d:
आवर्त्यन्ते करतले यस्याङ्गुल्यः करस्य वै ॥
पार्श्वागतविकीर्णाश्च कोलपद्म इति स्मृतः ॥ 39 ॥
3.6.m: The hand whose fingers are curled inward in the palm / and spread out from the side is known as alapadma.

3.6.s:
pratiṣedha kṛte yojyo nāsti śūnyeṣu cāpyatha ..
tisraḥ prasāritāṅgulyastathā cordhvā kanīyasī .. 3.26.40 ..
3.6.d:
प्रतिषेध कृते योज्यो नास्ति शून्येषु चाप्यथ ॥
तिस्रः प्रसारिताङ्गुल्यस्तथा चोर्ध्वा कनीयसी ॥ 3.26.40 ॥
3.6.m: It is to be employed in making a denial, and in [representing] 'it is not' or emptiness. / When three fingers are extended and the little finger is raised,

3.6.s:
tasyā madhyāśritoṅguṣṭhaḥ karaḥ sa caturaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
vacasāṃ viniyoge ca mādhye caiva prayojayet..41..
3.6.d:
तस्या मध्याश्रितोङ्गुष्ठः करः स चतुरः स्मृतः ॥
वचसां विनियोगे च माध्ये चैव प्रयोजयेत्॥41॥
3.6.m: and the thumb rests on the middle finger, that hand is called catura; / one should employ it in the application of words and in sweetness.

3.6.s:
anenaiva tathā kāryaṃ varṇānāṃ tu nirūpaṇam ..
ūrdhvasthe ca nave cśvetaṃ rakte syādardhamaṇḍalam ..42..
3.6.d:
अनेनैव तथा कार्यं वर्णानां तु निरूपणम् ॥
ऊर्ध्वस्थे च नवे च्श्वेतं रक्ते स्यादर्धमण्डलम् ॥42॥
3.6.m: With this very [hand], the depiction of colors is to be made: / held upward and fresh, it indicates white; in red, it forms a semicircle;

3.6.s:
maṇḍalaṃ na bhavetpītaṃ nīlaṃ ca mṛditaṃ bhavet ..
svabhāvasthena kṛtsnaṃ ca śeṣā varṇāstathaiva ca .. 43 ..
3.6.d:
मण्डलं न भवेत्पीतं नीलं च मृदितं भवेत् ॥
स्वभावस्थेन कृत्स्नं च शेषा वर्णास्तथैव च ॥ 43 ॥
3.6.m: a circle is yellow; rubbed, it is dark blue; / in its natural state, it indicates everything, and likewise the remaining colors.

3.6.s:
madhyamāṅguṣṭhasandeśo vakrā caiva pradeśinī ..
ūrdhvamanyāḥ prakīrṇāśca bhramaraśca tadā bhavet .. 44 ..
3.6.d:
मध्यमाङ्गुष्ठसन्देशो वक्रा चैव प्रदेशिनी ॥
ऊर्ध्वमन्याः प्रकीर्णाश्च भ्रमरश्च तदा भवेत् ॥ 44 ॥
3.6.m: When the middle finger and thumb form a pincer, the forefinger is bent, / and the other fingers are raised and separated, it is then bhramara.

3.6.s:
padmādigrahaṇe kāryaṃ karṇapūre tathāpyayam ..
tarjanīmadhyamāṅguṣṭhā tretāgnisthā nirantaram .. .. 45 ..
3.6.d:
पद्मादिग्रहणे कार्यं कर्णपूरे तथाप्ययम् ॥
तर्जनीमध्यमाङ्गुष्ठा त्रेताग्निस्था निरन्तरम् ॥ ॥ 45 ॥
3.6.m: It should be used in holding a lotus or the like, and also for an ear ornament. / When the forefinger, middle finger, and thumb continuously stand like the three fires,

3.6.s:
bhaveyurhaṃsavaktrasya śeṣā hyanyāḥ prasāritāḥ ..
ślakṣṇalāghavaniḥsāramārdaveṣu prayojayet .. 46 ..
3.6.d:
भवेयुर्हंसवक्त्रस्य शेषा ह्यन्याः प्रसारिताः ॥
श्लक्ष्णलाघवनिःसारमार्दवेषु प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 46 ॥
3.6.m: they form the haṃsavaktra hand, while the other fingers are extended; / one should employ it in smoothness, lightness, insubstantiality, and softness.

3.6.s:
tiryak piṇḍīkṛtā yasminunnatā ca kaniṣṭhikā ..
aṅguṣṭhaḥ kuñcitastvevaṃ haṃsapakṣa iti smṛtaḥ .. 47 ..
3.6.d:
तिर्यक् पिण्डीकृता यस्मिनुन्नता च कनिष्ठिका ॥
अङ्गुष्ठः कुञ्चितस्त्वेवं हंसपक्ष इति स्मृतः ॥ 47 ॥
3.6.m: The hand in which [the fingers] are pressed together obliquely, the little finger is raised, / and the thumb is bent, is known as haṃsapakṣa.

3.6.s:
gaṇḍasaṃśrayametena bhojanaḥ saparigrahaḥ ..
sparśe caivānulāpārthe kārye saṃvāhane tathā .. 48 ..
3.6.d:
गण्डसंश्रयमेतेन भोजनः सपरिग्रहः ॥
स्पर्शे चैवानुलापार्थे कार्ये संवाहने तथा ॥ 48 ॥
3.6.m: Resting on the cheek is done with this, as well as eating with acceptance, / touching, conversation, and massage.

3.6.s:
tarjanyaṅguṣṭhasaṃdaṃśastvarālasya yadā bhavet ..
nirbhugnatalamadhyaśca sasandaṃśa iti smṛtaḥ .. 49 ..
3.6.d:
तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठसंदंशस्त्वरालस्य यदा भवेत् ॥
निर्भुग्नतलमध्यश्च ससन्दंश इति स्मृतः ॥ 49 ॥
3.6.m: When there is a pinching together of the forefinger and thumb of the arāla, / and the center of the palm is bent, it is known as sandaṃśa.

3.6.s:
saṃdaṃśastrividho jñeyastvagraho mukhajastathā ..
tathā pārśvakṛtaścaiva tasya karmāṇi me śṛṇu .. 3.26.50 ..
3.6.d:
संदंशस्त्रिविधो ज्ञेयस्त्वग्रहो मुखजस्तथा ॥
तथा पार्श्वकृतश्चैव तस्य कर्माणि मे शृणु ॥ 3.26.50 ॥
3.6.m: Sandaṃśa should be known as threefold: situated at the tip, at the mouth, / and held at the side; hear from me its functions:

3.6.s:
sandaṃśagrahaṇe kāryaḥ śalyoddhāre tathāgrajaḥ ..
ālekhārañjane caiva tarjanīpīḍane tathā .. 51 ..
3.6.d:
सन्दंशग्रहणे कार्यः शल्योद्धारे तथाग्रजः ॥
आलेखारञ्जने चैव तर्जनीपीडने तथा ॥ 51 ॥
3.6.m: The one at the tip is to be used in grasping with pincers, extracting splinters, / painting and coloring, and pressing with the forefinger.

3.6.s:
yajñopavītī pārśvasthaḥ śiraḥsaṃdarśane tathā ..
samāgatāgrāṅguliko muktalaḥ padmakośakaḥ .. 52 ..
3.6.d:
यज्ञोपवीती पार्श्वस्थः शिरःसंदर्शने तथा ॥
समागताग्राङ्गुलिको मुक्तलः पद्मकोशकः ॥ 52 ॥
3.6.m: Held at the side, it represents the sacred thread and touching the head. / When the fingertips are brought together, it is mukula or padmakośa.

3.6.s:
devārcākaraṇe kāryo balo padmanirūpaṇe ..
asaṃyutāḥ karā hyete yathāvatkīrtitā mayā .. 53 ..
3.6.d:
देवार्चाकरणे कार्यो बलो पद्मनिरूपणे ॥
असंयुताः करा ह्येते यथावत्कीर्तिता मया ॥ 53 ॥
3.6.m: It should be used in worshipping deities, offering oblations, and representing a lotus. / These single hands have thus been properly described by me.

3.6.s:
patākābhyāṃ tu hastābhyāṃ sasphuṭoñjalirucyate ..
devatānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ ceṣyate punaḥ .. 54 ..
3.6.d:
पताकाभ्यां तु हस्ताभ्यां सस्फुटोञ्जलिरुच्यते ॥
देवतानां गुरूणां च पितॄणां चेष्यते पुनः ॥ 54 ॥
3.6.m: Two patāka hands joined closely together are called añjali; / it is desired in honoring deities, elders, and the ancestors.

3.6.s:
anyonyapārśvasaktābhyāṃ karābhyāṃ syātkapotakaḥ ..
śīte bhaye ca kāryo'yaṃ viniyogagame tathā .. 55 ..
3.6.d:
अन्योन्यपार्श्वसक्ताभ्यां कराभ्यां स्यात्कपोतकः ॥
शीते भये च कार्योऽयं विनियोगगमे तथा ॥ 55 ॥
3.6.m: When two hands are joined side by side, it is kapota; / this is to be used in cold, fear, and in expressing agreement.

3.6.s:
aṅgulyo yasya hastasya aḍulyantaraniḥsṛtāḥ ..
sa karkaṭa iti jñeyaḥ kartavyastu vijṛmbhite .. 56 ..
3.6.d:
अङ्गुल्यो यस्य हस्तस्य अडुल्यन्तरनिःसृताः ॥
स कर्कट इति ज्ञेयः कर्तव्यस्तु विजृम्भिते ॥ 56 ॥
3.6.m: The hand whose fingers are interlocked between the fingers [of the other] / is to be known as karkaṭa, and it should be used in yawning.

3.6.s:
maṇibandhana vinyastāvarālau vardhamānakaḥ ..
uttānau natapārśvasthau svastikaḥ parikīrtitaḥ .. 57 ..
3.6.d:
मणिबन्धन विन्यस्तावरालौ वर्धमानकः ॥
उत्तानौ नतपार्श्वस्थौ स्वस्तिकः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 57 ॥
3.6.m: Two arāla hands placed at the wrists form vardhamānaka; / turned palms upward and held on bent sides, it is called svastika.

3.6.s:
vistīrṇaṃ sarvametena ṛtavo gaganaṃ ghanam ..
samudraścābhineyaḥ syādbhūmiśca manujeśvara .. 58 ..
3.6.d:
विस्तीर्णं सर्वमेतेन ऋतवो गगनं घनम् ॥
समुद्रश्चाभिनेयः स्याद्भूमिश्च मनुजेश्वर ॥ 58 ॥
3.6.m: With this, everything vast—the seasons, the sky, clouds, / the ocean, and the earth—is to be depicted, O lord of men.

3.6.s:
khaṭakaḥ khaṭake nyasya khaṭakā vardhamānakaḥ ..
śṛṅgārārthe prayoktavyaḥ praṇāmakaraṇeṣu ca .. 59 ..
3.6.d:
खटकः खटके न्यस्य खटका वर्धमानकः ॥
शृङ्गारार्थे प्रयोक्तव्यः प्रणामकरणेषु च ॥ 59 ॥
3.6.m: Placing one khaṭaka upon another khaṭaka forms khaṭakāvardhamānaka; / it should be employed for erotic love and in making salutations.

3.6.s:
arālau tu viparyastāvuttānau vardhamānakau ..
utsaṅga iti vijñeyaḥ sparśasya grahaṇe paraḥ .. 3.26.60 ..
3.6.d:
अरालौ तु विपर्यस्तावुत्तानौ वर्धमानकौ ॥
उत्सङ्ग इति विज्ञेयः स्पर्शस्य ग्रहणे परः ॥ 3.26.60 ॥
3.6.m: Two reversed arāla hands turned upwards and forming vardhamāna / are to be known as utsaṅga; it is supreme in perceiving touch.

3.6.s:
muktalaṃ tu yadā hastaṃ kapitthaṃ pariveṣṭayet ..
sa vijñeyastadā hasto niṣadho nāma nāmataḥ .. 61..
3.6.d:
मुक्तलं तु यदा हस्तं कपित्थं परिवेष्टयेत् ॥
स विज्ञेयस्तदा हस्तो निषधो नाम नामतः ॥ 61॥
3.6.m: When a kapittha hand encloses a mukula hand, / that hand is then known by the name niṣadha.

3.6.s:
saṃkṣipte caiva nikṣipte tathā kāryaḥ prapīḍite ..
patākau lambitau hastau doleti parikīrtitāḥ .. .. 62 ..
3.6.d:
संक्षिप्ते चैव निक्षिप्ते तथा कार्यः प्रपीडिते ॥
पताकौ लम्बितौ हस्तौ दोलेति परिकीर्तिताः ॥ ॥ 62 ॥
3.6.m: It should be used in contracting, tossing down, and squeezing; / two patāka hands hanging down are celebrated as dolā.

3.6.s:
dhyānādidāne kartavyo bhakṣyādikaraṇeṣu ca ..
dvitīyapārśvasaṃśliṣṭaḥ pūrvaḥ puṣpapuṭaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 63 ..
3.6.d:
ध्यानादिदाने कर्तव्यो भक्ष्यादिकरणेषु च ॥
द्वितीयपार्श्वसंश्लिष्टः पूर्वः पुष्पपुटः स्मृतः ॥ 63 ॥
3.6.m: It should be performed in offering gifts in meditation and the like, and in preparing eatables and so on. / Joined at the second side, the former [patāka] is remembered as puṣpapuṭa.

3.6.s:
pūrvāṇi cābhineyāni karaṇāneva pārthiva ..
patākau tu yadā hastau mūrtahastāvadhomukhau .. 64 ..
3.6.d:
पूर्वाणि चाभिनेयानि करणानेव पार्थिव ॥
पताकौ तु यदा हस्तौ मूर्तहस्तावधोमुखौ ॥ 64 ॥
3.6.m: The previously described movements are indeed to be performed, O king. / When the two hands are patāka, turned downwards and held as bodies,

3.6.s:
uparyupari vinyastau tadā samakaraḥ karaḥ ..
siṃhavyāghramṛgādyānāṃ kartavyo'bhinayo bhavet ..65..
3.6.d:
उपर्युपरि विन्यस्तौ तदा समकरः करः ॥
सिंहव्याघ्रमृगाद्यानां कर्तव्योऽभिनयो भवेत् ॥65॥
3.6.m: placed one above the other, then the hand is samakara. / It should be used in enacting lions, tigers, deer, and the like.

3.6.s:
añcitau kūrparāsā tu yadā syātsarpaśīrṣake ..
gajadantastathā nāmnā kāryaḥ śailanibarhaṇe ..66..
3.6.d:
अञ्चितौ कूर्परासा तु यदा स्यात्सर्पशीर्षके ॥
गजदन्तस्तथा नाम्ना कार्यः शैलनिबर्हणे ॥66॥
3.6.m: When [the hands] are bent at the elbows and become sarpaśīrṣa, / it is called gajadanta by name, and should be used in breaking a mountain.

3.6.s:
śukatuṇḍau karau kṛtvā vakṣasyabhimukhāñcitau ..
śanairadhomukhau viddhāvavahittha iti smṛtaḥ..67..
3.6.d:
शुकतुण्डौ करौ कृत्वा वक्षस्यभिमुखाञ्चितौ ॥
शनैरधोमुखौ विद्धाववहित्थ इति स्मृतः॥67॥
3.6.m: Having made the hands śukatuṇḍa, bent facing the chest, / and slowly turned downwards and pierced, it is remembered as avahittha.

3.6.s:
daurbalyaśca site kāryo gātrāṇāṃ ca nidarśane..
jñeyo vai vardhamānastu haṃsapakṣau parāṅmukhau .. 68 ..
3.6.d:
दौर्बल्यश्च सिते कार्यो गात्राणां च निदर्शने॥
ज्ञेयो वै वर्धमानस्तु हंसपक्षौ पराङ्मुखौ ॥ 68 ॥
3.6.m: It is to be used in indicating weakness, cold, and the limbs. / When haṃsapakṣa hands are turned away, it is known as vardhamāna.

3.6.s:
jālavātāyanādīnāṃ prayogastena ceṣyate ..
saṃyutānāṃ karāṇāṃ tu lakṣaṇaṃ kathitaṃ mayā .. 69 ..
3.6.d:
जालवातायनादीनां प्रयोगस्तेन चेष्यते ॥
संयुतानां कराणां तु लक्षणं कथितं मया ॥ 69 ॥
3.6.m: Its application is desired in [depicting] latticed windows and the like. / Thus the characteristics of combined hands have been spoken by me.

3.6.s:
evaṃ jñeyāḥ karāḥ sarve nānārasasamudbhavāḥ ..
ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi nustuhastamapāśrayam .. 3.26.70 ..
3.6.d:
एवं ज्ञेयाः कराः सर्वे नानारससमुद्भवाः ॥
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि नुस्तुहस्तमपाश्रयम् ॥ 3.26.70 ॥
3.6.m: All these hands are to be known as originating from various aesthetic sentiments. / Hereafter I shall explain the dance hands according to tradition.

3.6.s:
vakṣaso'ṣṭāṃgulasthau tu prāṅmukhau khaṭakāmukhau ..
samānakūrparāsau tu caturasro prakīrtitau..71..
3.6.d:
वक्षसोऽष्टांगुलस्थौ तु प्राङ्मुखौ खटकामुखौ ॥
समानकूर्परासौ तु चतुरस्रो प्रकीर्तितौ॥71॥
3.6.m: Held eight aṅgulas from the chest, facing forward as khaṭakāmukha, / with elbows and shoulders level, they are declared to be caturasra.

3.6.s:
haṃsapakṣau smṛtau hastau vyāvṛttau tālavṛntavat ..
udvṛttāviti vijñeyāvatha va. tālavṛntakau .. 72 ..
3.6.d:
हंसपक्षौ स्मृतौ हस्तौ व्यावृत्तौ तालवृन्तवत् ॥
उद्वृत्ताविति विज्ञेयावथ व। तालवृन्तकौ ॥ 72 ॥
3.6.m: When the hands are remembered as haṃsapakṣa, rotated like palm-leaf fans, / they are known as udvṛtta, or as tālavṛntaka.

3.6.s:
caturasrīkṛtau hastau haṃsapakṣīkṛtau tathā ..
tiryaṅamukhāvūrdhvatalau jñeyau laghumukhāviti .. 73 ..
3.6.d:
चतुरस्रीकृतौ हस्तौ हंसपक्षीकृतौ तथा ॥
तिर्यङमुखावूर्ध्वतलौ ज्ञेयौ लघुमुखाविति ॥ 73 ॥
3.6.m: Hands made caturasra and likewise made haṃsapakṣa, / facing obliquely with upturned palms, are to be known as laghumukha.

3.6.s:
tāveva maṇidhanvāṃtāvarālakacitau karau ..
jñeyāvabhinaye tvetau hyarālakhaṭakāmukhau .. 74 ..
3.6.d:
तावेव मणिधन्वांतावरालकचितौ करौ ॥
ज्ञेयावभिनये त्वेतौ ह्यरालखटकामुखौ ॥ 74 ॥
3.6.m: Those same hands, with tips extending to the wrists and curved in arāla, / should be known in dramatic performance as arālakhaṭakāmukha.

3.6.s:
bhujau sakūrparāgrau tu kuṭilāvartitau karau ..
adhomukhatalāviddhāvāviddhāviti kīrtitau .. 75 ..
3.6.d:
भुजौ सकूर्पराग्रौ तु कुटिलावर्तितौ करौ ॥
अधोमुखतलाविद्धावाविद्धाविति कीर्तितौ ॥ 75 ॥
3.6.m: The arms with elbows forward, the hands curved and rotated, / their palms turned downwards and pierced, are declared to be āviddha.

3.6.s:
sarpaśīrṣau yadā hastau bhavatāṃ svastika sthitau ..
tiryakprasāritāsyau ca jñeyau sūcīmukhāviti .. 76 ..
3.6.d:
सर्पशीर्षौ यदा हस्तौ भवतां स्वस्तिक स्थितौ ॥
तिर्यक्प्रसारितास्यौ च ज्ञेयौ सूचीमुखाविति ॥ 76 ॥
3.6.m: When the hands are sarpaśīrṣa and placed in a svastika, / with their faces extended obliquely, they are known as sūcīmukha.

3.6.s:
recitau cāpi vijñeyau haṃsapakṣādbhutabhramau ..
prasāritottānatalau racitāveva saṃ jñitau .. 77 ..
3.6.d:
रेचितौ चापि विज्ञेयौ हंसपक्षाद्भुतभ्रमौ ॥
प्रसारितोत्तानतलौ रचितावेव सं ज्ञितौ ॥ 77 ॥
3.6.m: They are to be known as recita when moving with wonderful rotation from haṃsapakṣa; / extended with palms turned upwards, they are designated as recita.

3.6.s:
caturasro bhavedvāmaḥ savyahastaśca recitaḥ ..
vijñeyo nāṭyatattvajñairevaṃ recitasaṃjñitaḥ .. 78 ..
3.6.d:
चतुरस्रो भवेद्वामः सव्यहस्तश्च रेचितः ॥
विज्ञेयो नाट्यतत्त्वज्ञैरेवं रेचितसंज्ञितः ॥ 78 ॥
3.6.m: The left hand is caturasra, and the right hand is recita; / this is known by knowers of the truth of drama as designated recita.

3.6.s:
añcitau kūrparābhyāṃ tu tri patākau yadā karau ..
kiṃcittiryaggatāvetāvāvahittha prakīrtitaḥ .. 79 ..
3.6.d:
अञ्चितौ कूर्पराभ्यां तु त्रि पताकौ यदा करौ ॥
किंचित्तिर्यग्गतावेतावावहित्थ प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 79 ॥
3.6.m: When the hands are tripatāka, bent from the elbows, / and move slightly obliquely, this is declared as avahittha.

3.6.s:
maṇibandhananirmuktau śithilau pallavau smṛtau ..
bāhu śīviniṣkrāntau nitambau parikīrtitau .. 3.26.80 ..
3.6.d:
मणिबन्धननिर्मुक्तौ शिथिलौ पल्लवौ स्मृतौ ॥
बाहु शीविनिष्क्रान्तौ नितम्बौ परिकीर्तितौ ॥ 3.26.80 ॥
3.6.m: Released from the wrists and loose, they are remembered as pallava. / Brought out from the head and shoulders, they are declared as nitamba.

3.6.s:
aṃsadeśe pravṛttau tu paripārśvotthitau tathā ..
vijñeyau keśabaṃdhākhyau karāvācāryasammatau .. 81 ..
3.6.d:
अंसदेशे प्रवृत्तौ तु परिपार्श्वोत्थितौ तथा ॥
विज्ञेयौ केशबंधाख्यौ करावाचार्यसम्मतौ ॥ 81 ॥
3.6.m: Proceeding from the region of the shoulders and raised at the sides, / the hands are known as keśabandha, accepted by the teachers.

3.6.s:
tiryakprasāritāveva pārśvasaṃsthau tathaiva ca ..
latākhyau tu karau jñeyau nṛttābhinayanaṃ prati .. 82 ..
3.6.d:
तिर्यक्प्रसारितावेव पार्श्वसंस्थौ तथैव च ॥
लताख्यौ तु करौ ज्ञेयौ नृत्ताभिनयनं प्रति ॥ 82 ॥
3.6.m: Extended obliquely and positioned at the sides, / the hands are known as latā in the dramatic enactment of dance.

3.6.s:
samunnatā latāhastaḥ pārśvātpārśvaviloḍitaḥ ..
dvitīyaḥ khaṭakākhyaśca karihastaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 83 ..
3.6.d:
समुन्नता लताहस्तः पार्श्वात्पार्श्वविलोडितः ॥
द्वितीयः खटकाख्यश्च करिहस्तः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 83 ॥
3.6.m: One hand is latā, raised high and swaying from side to side, / and the second is khaṭakā; it is declared as karihasta.

3.6.s:
kaṭiśīrṣaniviṣṭāgrau tripatākau yadā karau ..
pakṣāvañcitakau vāme tadā jñeyau prayoktṛbhiḥ .. 84 ..
3.6.d:
कटिशीर्षनिविष्टाग्रौ त्रिपताकौ यदा करौ ॥
पक्षावञ्चितकौ वामे तदा ज्ञेयौ प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥ 84 ॥
3.6.m: When the hands are tripatāka with tips placed at the waist and head, / they are known by practitioners as pakṣāvañcita on the left.

3.6.s:
tāveva tu parāvṛttau pakṣāghātau karāviti ..
adhomukhatalāviddhau jñeyau garuḍapakṣakau .. 85 ..
3.6.d:
तावेव तु परावृत्तौ पक्षाघातौ कराविति ॥
अधोमुखतलाविद्धौ ज्ञेयौ गरुडपक्षकौ ॥ 85 ॥
3.6.m: Those same hands reversed are the pakṣāghāta hands; / with palms turned downwards and pierced, they are to be known as garuḍapakṣaka.

3.6.s:
tathā prasāritabhujau daṇḍapakṣāviti smṛtau ..
tau cordhvamaṇḍalau jñeyau gurudeśavivartanāt .. 86 ..
3.6.d:
तथा प्रसारितभुजौ दण्डपक्षाविति स्मृतौ ॥
तौ चोर्ध्वमण्डलौ ज्ञेयौ गुरुदेशविवर्तनात् ॥ 86 ॥
3.6.m: Likewise, with arms extended, they are remembered as daṇḍapakṣa; / and those two are known as ūrdhvamaṇḍala from rotating in the upper region.

3.6.s:
tāveva pārśvavinyastau vijñeyau pārśvamaṇḍalau ..
veṣṭitāveṣṭitau hastau tayormaṇḍalakau smṛtau .. 87 ..
3.6.d:
तावेव पार्श्वविन्यस्तौ विज्ञेयौ पार्श्वमण्डलौ ॥
वेष्टितावेष्टितौ हस्तौ तयोर्मण्डलकौ स्मृतौ ॥ 87 ॥
3.6.m: Those same hands placed at the sides are to be known as pārśvamaṇḍala. / The two hands, winding and unwinding, are remembered as their maṇḍalaka.

3.6.s:
tāveva maṇibandhāntau svastikākṛtisaṃjñitau ..
svastikāviti vikhyātau vikhyātau ca prakī rṇakau .. 88 ..
3.6.d:
तावेव मणिबन्धान्तौ स्वस्तिकाकृतिसंज्ञितौ ॥
स्वस्तिकाविति विख्यातौ विख्यातौ च प्रकी र्णकौ ॥ 88 ॥
3.6.m: Those same hands at the ends of the wrists, designated as having the form of a svastika, / are celebrated as svastika, and also celebrated as prakīrṇaka.

3.6.s:
dvāveva padmakośābhau padmakośāviti smṛtau ..
karāvuddhe jitāgrau tu vijñeyāvalipallavau .. 89 ..
3.6.d:
द्वावेव पद्मकोशाभौ पद्मकोशाविति स्मृतौ ॥
करावुद्धे जिताग्रौ तु विज्ञेयावलिपल्लवौ ॥ 89 ॥
3.6.m: Both resembling padmakośa are remembered as padmakośa; / the hands with agitated and turned tips are to be known as alipallava.

3.6.s:
ūrdhvaprasāritau viddhau vijñeyāvulvaṇāviti ..
pallavau tu śirodeśe samprāptau lalitāviti .. 3.26.90 ..
3.6.d:
ऊर्ध्वप्रसारितौ विद्धौ विज्ञेयावुल्वणाविति ॥
पल्लवौ तु शिरोदेशे सम्प्राप्तौ ललिताविति ॥ 3.26.90 ॥
3.6.m: Extended upwards and pierced, they are known as ulvaṇa; / but when the two pallava hands reach the region of the head, they are lalita.

3.6.s:
kūrparasvastikanyastau lalitāvalitau smṛtau ..
saṃyutā viyutāścaiva nṛttahastāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .. 91 ..
3.6.d:
कूर्परस्वस्तिकन्यस्तौ ललितावलितौ स्मृतौ ॥
संयुता वियुताश्चैव नृत्तहस्ताः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 91 ॥
3.6.m: Placed in a svastika at the elbows, they are remembered as lalitāvalita. / Thus the dance hands, both combined and single, are declared.

3.6.s:
nānārtharasasaṃyuktaṃ prayogakālasaṃśrayam ..
vijñeyaṃ nṛttahastānāṃ tena nābhihitaṃ mayā .. 92..
3.6.d:
नानार्थरससंयुक्तं प्रयोगकालसंश्रयम् ॥
विज्ञेयं नृत्तहस्तानां तेन नाभिहितं मया ॥ 92॥
3.6.m: Endowed with various meanings and sentiments, and dependent on the time of performance, / is what is to be understood of the dance hands; therefore it has not been fully stated by me.

3.6.s:
ādhigraste jagante ca niyamasthe jagardite ..
matte pramatte cintāyāṃ nābhineyaḥ karo bhavet .. 93 ..
3.6.d:
आधिग्रस्ते जगन्ते च नियमस्थे जगर्दिते ॥
मत्ते प्रमत्ते चिन्तायां नाभिनेयः करो भवेत् ॥ 93 ॥
3.6.m: In one seized by anguish, in one dead, in one practicing self-restraint, in one afflicted by illness, / in an intoxicated person, in a negligent one, or in sorrow, no hand gesture is to be performed.

3.6.s:
udveṣṭaṃ samaveṣṭaṃ ca viceṣṭitavivartite ..
karmedaṃ nṛttahastānāṃ vijñeyaṃ ca caturvidham .. 94 ..
3.6.d:
उद्वेष्टं समवेष्टं च विचेष्टितविवर्तिते ॥
कर्मेदं नृत्तहस्तानां विज्ञेयं च चतुर्विधम् ॥ 94 ॥
3.6.m: Outward winding, inward winding, gesturing, and rotating— / this fourfold movement of the dance hands is to be known.

3.6.s:
kāryā lalitasaṃcārā nṛttahastāparā budhaiḥ..
lālityameva vijñeyaṃ vṛttasya pratibodhanam ..95..
3.6.d:
कार्या ललितसंचारा नृत्तहस्तापरा बुधैः॥
लालित्यमेव विज्ञेयं वृत्तस्य प्रतिबोधनम् ॥95॥
3.6.m: Other dance hands should be executed by the wise with graceful movement; / grace alone is to be known as the awakening of the dance.

3.6.s:
deśaṃ kālaṃ prayogaṃ ca hyarthayuktimavekṣya ca ..
hastā ete prayoktavyā strīṇāṃ nṝṇāṃ ca nartake .. 96 ..
3.6.d:
देशं कालं प्रयोगं च ह्यर्थयुक्तिमवेक्ष्य च ॥
हस्ता एते प्रयोक्तव्या स्त्रीणां नॄणां च नर्तके ॥ 96 ॥
3.6.m: Considering the place, time, dramatic application, and fitness of meaning, / these hand gestures should be employed for women and men in dance.

mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..

catuṣprakāro'bhinayaḥ kīrtito nāṭyakovidaiḥ .. .. 1 ..

हस्ता मयैते कथिता नृवीर सर्वं करायत्तमिदं हि नृत्तम् ॥
यत्नश्च कार्यस्तु करेषु तस्माच्चातुर्यलास्याभिनयोपपन्नम् ॥97 ॥
3.27
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
वाचिकश्च तथा हार्यस्त्वाङ्गिकस्सात्त्विकस्तथा ॥
चतुष्प्रकारोऽभिनयः कीर्तितो नाट्यकोविदैः ॥ ॥ 1 ॥
वाचिको वचसा प्रोक्तः शृणु हार्यं नराधिप ॥
चतुर्विधं तु विज्ञेयं प्रस्तोलङ्कार एव च ॥ 2 ॥
तथाङ्गरचना चैव ज्ञेया सज्जीवमेव च ॥
मृदा वा दारुणा वापि वस्त्रेणाप्यथ चर्मणा ॥ 3 ॥
लोहैरनुकृतिर्वापि प्रस्त इत्यभिधीयते ॥
देवदानवयक्षाणां गजाश्वमृगपक्षिणाम् ॥ 4 ॥
कार्याणि प्रतिशीर्षाणि नाट्यज्ञैः प्रस्तकर्मणा ॥
अलङ्कारस्तु विज्ञेयो माल्याभरणवाससाम् ॥ 5 ॥
नानाविधः समायोगे ह्यङ्गोपाङ्गविनिर्गतः ॥
तच्च कार्यो नयो बुद्ध्वा नियोगं जातिमेव च ॥ 6 ॥
3.6.m:
These hand gestures have been spoken by me, O hero among men; for this entire dance depends on the hands. / Therefore, effort should be made regarding the hands, endowed with skill, graceful dance, and dramatic expression.
3.27 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Verbal, and likewise costume and make-up, physical, and emotional: / fourfold is dramatic representation declared by experts in drama.
The verbal is said to be by speech; hear of costume and make-up, O lord of men. / It is to be known as fourfold: model-work, ornament,
and painting of the body, as well as living beings. / Whether with clay, with wood, with cloth, or with leather,
or an imitation made with metals, it is designated as model-work. / For gods, dānavas, and yakṣas, and for elephants, horses, beasts, and birds,
masks should be made by experts in drama through model-work. / Ornament, moreover, is to be known as consisting of garlands, jewellery, and garments,
diverse in combination, applied to the limbs and secondary limbs. / An intelligent person should execute that after comprehending the role and class,

ādhipatyaṃ tathā sthānaṃ deśe ca nṛpasattama ..
atoṅgaracanā tubhyaṃ vakṣyāmi nṛpa varṇajām .. 7 ..

3.6.d:
आधिपत्यं तथा स्थानं देशे च नृपसत्तम ॥
अतोङ्गरचना तुभ्यं वक्ष्यामि नृप वर्णजाम् ॥ 7 ॥
श्वेतो रक्तस्तथा पीतः कृष्णो हरितमेव च ॥
मूलवर्णाः समाख्याताः पञ्च पार्थिवसत्तम॥ 8 ॥
एकद्वित्रिसमायोगाद्भावकल्पनया तथा ॥
सङ्ख्यैवांतरवर्णानां लोके कर्तुं न शक्यते ॥ 9 ॥
अत्यर्थसमयोगित्वाल्लोकेऽहं नृपपुंगव ॥
विभागं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि वर्णयोः श्यामगौरयोः ॥ 3.27.10 ॥
द्विप्रकारा छविर्यस्मात्सर्वस्येह प्रकीर्तिता ॥
गौरी पञ्चविधा तत्र श्यामा द्वादशधा भवेत् ॥ ॥ 11 ॥
रुक्मगौरी दन्तगौरी स्फुटचन्दनगौर्यपि ॥
शरद्घनचन्द्रकवद्गौरी पञ्चविधा स्मृता ॥12॥
रक्तश्याम्या भवेत्पूर्वं मुद्गश्यामा निरन्तरम्॥
ततो दूर्वांकुरश्यामा पाण्डुश्यामा च पार्थिव ॥13 ॥
3.6.m:
as well as the sovereignty and status in the region, O best of kings. / Next I shall declare to you the painting of the body produced from colours, O king.
White, red, yellow, black, and green: / these are celebrated as the five primary colours, O best of kings.
By the combination of one, two, or three, and through the imagination of states, / it is impossible to count the intermediate colours in the world.
Because of their extreme relevance in the world, O bull among kings, / I shall explain the division of the two colours: dark and fair.
Since complexion is proclaimed to be of two kinds for everyone here: / among them, the fair is fivefold, and the dark should be of twelve kinds.
Gold-fair, ivory-fair, and also blooming-sandalwood-fair, / fair like an autumn cloud, and like the moon—the fair is remembered as fivefold.
First is reddish-dark; contiguous to it is mung-bean-dark; / then dūrvā-sprout-dark, and pale-dark, O king;

3.6.d:
ततश्च हरितश्यामा पीतश्यामा ततो भवेत् ॥
ततः प्रियङ्गुकश्यामा कपिश्यामा च पार्थिव ॥ ॥14.
ततो नीलोत्पलश्यामा चाषश्यामा ततः परम्॥
ततो रक्तोत्पलश्यामा घनश्यामा तथा परा॥15॥
द्रव्यानुरूपवर्णैस्तु तासां व्यक्तिरुदाहृता ॥
रङ्गव्यतिकरैः शोभामधिकृत्य महीयते ॥16॥
वक्ष्यामि वर्णान्देवानां मत्वापतु विनिश्चयम् ॥
तत्र येषां न वक्ष्यामि ते कार्या गौरवर्णकाः ॥17॥
श्यामस्तु वासुकिः कार्यो नागा गौरास्तु द्वापरे।
दैत्याश्च दानवाश्चैव राक्षसा गुह्यकानुगाः ॥18 ॥
पिशाचा जलसङ्काशा सम्मितानि तु वर्णतः॥
षट्सु द्वीपेषु पुरुषाः कर्तव्याः कनकप्रभाः ॥ ॥ 19 ॥
जम्बूद्वीपस्य वर्षेषु मुक्त्वैकं भारतं नृप ॥
भारतेषु तथा कार्या नानादेशभवास्तथा ॥ ॥ 3.27.20 ॥
पुलिन्दा दाक्षिणात्याश्च प्रायशो वर्णतोऽसिताः ॥
शकाश्च यवनाश्चैव पह्लवा वाह्लिकाश्च ये ॥ 21 ॥
3.6.m:
and then green-dark; then should be yellow-dark; / then priyaṅgu-dark, and monkey-dark, O king;
then blue-lotus-dark; after that roller-bird-dark; / then red-lotus-dark, and cloud-dark is another.
The manifestation of these is declared by means of colours corresponding to their substances; / through the mixtures of colours, taking beauty into account, it is enhanced.
Considering properly the ascertainment, I will declare the colours of the gods; / there, those of whom I do not speak are to be made of fair colour.
Vāsuki should be made dark, but the serpents are fair in the Dvāpara age; / daityas and dānavas, rākṣasas, followers of the guhyakas,
and piśācas resemble water; but measured by colour, / the men in the six continents should be made gold-lustred,
in the regions of Jambūdvīpa, with the exception of Bhārata alone, O king. / In Bhārata, they should be made native to diverse lands:
Pulindas and southerners are mostly dark in colour; / the Śakas and the Yavanas, the Pahlavas and the Vāhlikas,

3.6.d:
प्रायेण गौराः कर्तव्याः उत्तरापथसम्भवाः ॥
पाञ्चालाः शूरसेनाश्च तथा ये चात्र मागधाः ॥ 22 ॥
अङ्गा वङ्गाः कलिङ्गाश्च प्रायशो वर्णतोऽसिताः ॥
चन्द्रवर्णा द्विजाः कार्या राजन्याः पद्मसन्निभाः ॥ 23 ॥
आपाण्डुरास्तथा वैश्याः श्यामा शूद्राश्च वर्णतः ॥
नानावर्णाः स्मृता भूता गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तथा ॥ 24 ॥।
राजानः पद्मवर्णाभा ये चापि सुखिनो जनाः ॥
कुकर्माणो ग्रहग्रस्ता व्याधितास्तप आश्रिताः ॥ 25 ॥
आयस्तकर्मणश्चैव असिताः कुलजालयः ॥
वर्णः प्रत्यक्षदृष्टस्य कर्तव्यः सदृशस्तथा ॥ 26 ॥
देवगन्धर्वसिद्धानां कुमाराणां च पार्थिव ॥
श्मश्रु तेषां न कर्तव्यं ये च दीक्षां समाश्रिताः ॥ 27 ॥
दिव्या ये पुरुषाश्चैव तथा विद्याधराश्च ये ॥
शृङ्गारिणो नरेन्द्राश्च चित्रश्मश्रुधरास्तथा ॥ 28 ॥
3.6.m:
born in the northern region, should mostly be made fair. / The Pāñcālas, the Śūrasenas, and those who are Māgadhas here,
the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, and Kaliṅgas are mostly dark in colour. / Twice-borns should be made moon-coloured, and kṣatriyas lotus-like;
vaiśyas slightly pale, and śūdras dark in colour. / Bhūtas, gandharvas, and apsarases are remembered as of various colours.
Kings have the colour and lustre of a lotus, as do people who are happy. / Evil-doers, those possessed by planetary spirits, the diseased, those devoted to asceticism,
and those fatigued by labour are dark, [even if] born of noble family. / The colour of what is seen with one's own eyes should be made similar [to reality].
For gods, gandharvas, and siddhas, and for youths, O king, / no beard should be made, nor for those who have undertaken initiation.
Heavenly men and also vidyādharas, / amorous men and kings are wearers of trimmed beards.

3.6.m:
A clean-shaven [face] should be made for ascetics, ministers, and household priests, / for impartial men, and for those who have undertaken an initiation.
For those whose vows are unfulfilled, the sorrowful, ascetics, / and sages bound for a long time, a long beard is proclaimed.
The dress of a śūdra follows the pursuit of dharma, O lord of men; / of merchants, chamberlains, and likewise of brahmins,
the dress of kings should be variegated, and of courtesans, O Yādava. / The dress of others should conform to their status according to ordinary life.
Three kinds of crowns are to be known, belonging to gods and kings; / crest-diadems should be made for gods and kings:
with seven peaks for gods, with five for kings, / and with three peaks they should be made for the chief queen and the crown prince.
One with a single peak should be made for the commander of the army, O king; / for daityas, dānavas, yakṣas, and serpents along with rakṣases,

broad crowns of a single band, auspicious, should be made. / For vidyādharas, siddhas, and likewise for monkeys,
crowns with knots should be made by the directors. / Gods, dānavas, and gandharvas are proclaimed to have dark wings.
Daityas, dānavas, yakṣas, piśācas, nāgas, and rākṣasas / should be made with tawny beards and hair, and tawny-eyed, O king.
Chamberlains should be made with white hair on their heads; / for ministers, chamberlains, and excellent household priests,
one should make headdresses bound with turbans and fillets. / For piśācas, madmen, and spirits, and likewise for ascetics,
and for those who have not fulfilled their vow, the head should have hanging hair. / For boys, an ornament of hair-tufts should also be made;
for sages, it should be made endowed with a mass of matted hair, O king; / for servants, three tufts of hair should also be made.
For the jester, there should be baldness and a crow's-foot [tuft]; / for the rest, in the manner stated, in accordance with the remaining castes.

सज्जीव इति यत्प्रोक्तं तस्य वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम्॥
प्रवेशस्तु तिरश्चां वै सज्जीव इति संज्ञितः॥44॥
तेषां प्रस्तेन कर्तव्या प्रकृतिः पुरुषांतरा॥
तथैवायुधहस्तानां कर्तव्या हेतयः शुभाः ॥45॥
एवं लोकोपचारेण स्वबुद्ध्या विभवेन च ॥
नाट्योपकरणानीह यथावत्परिकल्पयेत् ॥ 46 ॥
हेतिप्रमोक्षो न तु रङ्गमध्ये कार्यो भवेत्पार्थिववंशमुख्य ॥

तस्मिन्कार्यः प्रयत्नस्तु नाट्यान्तरप्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 1 ॥

3.6.m:
That which is called sajjīva, I will state its characteristic: / the entrance of animals is designated as sajjīva.
Their nature should be made by means of models containing men within; / likewise, for those with weapons in hand, beautiful weapons should be made.
Thus, according to worldly convention, by one's own intellect and resources, / one should properly arrange the theatrical accessories here.
The discharge of weapons should not be done on the stage, O foremost of royal scions. / This extrinsic representation has been explained in brief; henceforth I will declare to you the bodily representation.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, named Extrinsic Representation, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the third book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara.
3.28 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall explain to you general representation; / in that, effort should be made, established within the theatrical art.
Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell— / the wise actor should represent the sense organs and sense objects through emotional expression.

कृत्वा साचीकृतां दृष्टिं शिरः किंचिन्नतं भवेत् ॥
तर्जनीकर्णदेशे तु शब्दन्त्वभिनयेद्बुधः ॥ 3 ॥
किञ्चिदाकुञ्चिते नेत्रे कृत्वोत्फुल्ला त्वनामिकाम् ॥
एकश्वासो भवेच्चापि गन्धमेवं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥4॥
इन्द्रियार्थास्तु पञ्चैते त्रिविधाः परिकीर्त्तिताः ॥
इष्टास्तथा ह्यनिष्टाश्च मध्यस्था नृपसत्तम ॥ 5 ॥
गात्रप्रह्लादनेनेह तथा पुलकितेन च ॥
नितान्तास्रक्रियाभिश्च सर्वमिष्टं निरूपयेत् ॥ 6 ॥
परावृत्तेन शिरसा तथा चानेन चक्षुषा ॥
नेत्रनासाञ्चितत्वेन ह्यनिष्टमिति निर्दिशेत् ॥ 7 ॥
मध्यस्थेनैव भावेन मध्यस्थकरणं भवेत् ॥।
आत्मानुभावी योऽर्थः स्यादात्मस्थ इति संज्ञितः ॥ 8 ॥
परार्थवर्णनं यच्च परस्थेति च कीर्तितम् ॥
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा स्वस्तिकौ पार्श्वसंस्थितौ ॥ 9 ॥
3.6.m:
Making the gaze slanted, with the head slightly bent, / and the forefinger at the ear, the wise man should represent sound.
Having the eyes slightly contracted, with the ring-finger expanded, / and with a single breath, one should indicate smell.
These five sense objects are declared to be threefold: / agreeable, disagreeable, and neutral, O best of kings.
By the delight of the limbs, by horripilation, / and by actions of abundant tears, one should depict everything agreeable.
With an averted head, with averted eyes, / and with the contraction of the eyes and nose, one should indicate what is disagreeable.
With an indifferent disposition occurs the depiction of the neutral. / An object experienced by oneself is called 'relating to oneself'.
And the depiction of another's affairs is proclaimed as 'relating to another'. / Making the two hands supine and in the svastika gesture, placed at the sides,

सुखस्पृश्यानि सर्वाणि रोमांचं न तु दर्शयेत् ॥ 16 ॥
3.6.m:
with an uplifted head and looking upward: / dawn, the sky, night, twilight, and day,
the seasons, clouds, the earth, expansive reservoirs of water, / the quarters, planets, constellations, and whatever else belongs to the sky, O king,
their dramatic representation should be performed accompanied by various glances, / repeatedly with these very hands, with the breasts, and with the head.
Then, by looking downward, one should represent things situated on the ground. / The wise one should enact the moon, moonlight, the face, and the wind through touch.
The sun, dust, smoke, and fires [should be enacted] by veiling oneself with cloth; / and one should represent the heat of the ground and warmth by sighs and longing speech.
With an upward squinting glance [one should show] the midday sun, / and when rising and setting, one should display it in the sense of wonder.
One should show the moon with an astonished glance, and likewise the stars. / For all things pleasant to touch, one should not show goosebumps;

3.6.m:
and [one should show] pains and agitation by contortions of the face. / Objects associated with the profound and the exalted, endowed with gracefulness,
one should indicate with the hand placed in the region of the sacred thread. / In shedding necklaces, in offerings, and in showing a garland,
with the bhramara hand, with the forefinger, and with the following of the glance, / [or] by the pressure of the alapadma hand, the grasping of all objects occurs.
What is audible through the application of hearing, and what is visible through the observing of the gaze, / one should indicate as relating to oneself, relating to another, or neutral.
Lightning, meteors, the roar of clouds, sparks, poison, / the goad, and the winking of the eye: these must be enacted by the performers.
Veiling of the face should be done to ward off bees and the like. / Having formed two padmakośa hands turned downward in the svastika position,
one should perform the depiction of lions, bears, monkeys, and the like. / Two tripatāka hands in svastika [are used] in saluting the feet of elders,

3.6.d:
खटकास्वस्तिकौ चापि प्रतोदग्रहणे भवेत् ॥
एकाद्यानां दशान्तानां संख्या त्वंगुलिभिर्भवेत् ॥ 24 ॥
दशाख्या च शताख्या च स्थानसंख्या ततः परम् ॥
पताकाभ्यां तु हस्ताभ्यां वाचा चाभिनयो भवेत् ॥ 25 ॥
छत्रध्वजपताकाश्च विज्ञेया दण्डधारणात् ॥
नाना प्रहरणं चैव विज्ञेयमिह वारणैः ॥ 26 ॥
एकचित्तो ह्यधोदृष्टिः शिरः किञ्चिन्नतं भवेत् ॥
सव्यहस्तश्च संदंशस्मिते व्याने वितङ्किते ॥ 27 ॥
उद्वाहितं शिरः कृत्वा हंसपक्षं प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
अपत्यरूपणे कार्यमुश्वायं च प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥ 28 ॥
अरालं च शिरः स्थाने समुद्वाह्या च वामतः ॥
गते निवृत्ते ध्वस्ते च श्रान्तं वाक्यं नियोजयेत् ॥ 29 ॥
जितेन्द्रियतया युक्तं प्रसन्नवदनं तथा ॥
विचित्रकुसुमालोकां शरदं तु निरूपयेत् ॥ ॥। 3.28.30 ॥
3.6.m:
and the khaṭakāsvastika hands [are used] in holding a goad. / Numbers from one up to ten are made with the fingers;
the count of tens, the count of hundreds, and the positional numbers beyond that / should be enacted with the two patāka hands and with speech.
Umbrellas, standards, and flags are to be understood by the holding of a staff, / and various weapons are to be understood here by warding off.
With a single-pointed mind, with downward glance, the head slightly bowed, / and the right hand in saṃdaṃśa: in smiling, in breathing, [or] in deep thought.
Having raised the head, moving the haṃsapakṣa hand clockwise, / performers should represent a child and sighing.
Placing the arāla hand at the position of the head, raised on the left side, / for what is gone, turned back, or destroyed, one should employ wearied speech.
Accompanied by self-control, with a serene face, / one should depict autumn filled with the sight of diverse blossoms.

3.6.d:
गात्रस्य कम्पनात्तज्ज्ञैस्तथा चान्याभिलाषितः ॥
हेमन्तस्त्वभिधेयः स्यात्पुरुषैर्मध्यमाधमैः ॥31॥
शिरोदन्तौष्ठकम्पेन गात्रसंकोचकेन ।च ॥
कूजितैश्च ससीत्कारैः शीतस्याभिनयो भवेत् ॥ 32 ॥
प्रसादजननारम्भैरुपभोगैः ससम्भ्रमैः ॥
वसन्तस्त्वभिनेतव्यो नानापुष्पप्रदर्शनात्॥ ॥। 33 ॥
स्वेदापमार्जनाच्चापि भूमिपातोपजीविनः ॥
उष्णस्य वायोः स्पर्शश्च ग्रीष्मस्याभिनयो भवेत् ॥ 34 ॥
गम्भीरनादश्रवणात्प्रावृष्यभि नयो भवेत ॥
वचसाभिनयः कार्यो ऋतूनां सुखदुःखयोः ॥ 35 ॥
स्वभावाभिनये स्थानं पुंभिः कार्यं तु वैष्णवम् ॥
आयुतं चावहित्यं च स्त्रीभिः कार्यं स्वभावतः ॥ 36 ॥
धैर्यशीलाङ्गसम्पन्नं पुरुषाणां विचेष्टितम् ॥
मृतशीलाङ्गहारैस्तु स्त्रीणां कार्यं विचेष्टितम् ॥ 37 ॥
3.6.m:
By the trembling of the limbs and as desiring another, by those who know it, / winter should be expressed by middling and low characters.
By the trembling of the head, teeth, and lips, by the contraction of the limbs, / by low groans, and with hissing sounds, the representation of cold takes place.
With undertakings generating delight and with eager enjoyments, / spring should be enacted through the display of various flowers.
By wiping off sweat, by seeking the shade on the ground, / and through the touch of hot wind, the depiction of summer occurs.
From hearing a deep roar, the rainy season should be enacted. / The enactment of the seasons, in pleasure and in pain, should be made with speech.
In natural acting, the vaiṣṇava stance should be assumed by men; / the āyuta and the avahittha [stances] should be assumed naturally by women.
The movement of men is endowed with fortitude, good conduct, and proper limbs; / the movement of women should be performed with gentle movements and gestures.

3.6.d:
आलिङ्गन तु कर्तव्यं स्मितरोमाञ्चसंयुतम् ॥
रोमाञ्चेन तु हर्षः स्यात्क्रोधमुद्वृत्तचक्षुषा ॥ 38 ॥
ईर्ष्या क्रोधस्तु कर्तव्यो माल्याभरणवर्जितम् ॥
शिरसा कम्पनं चैव मर्मभंगैस्तथैव च ॥ 39 ॥
अधोमुखः सनिःश्वासो दुःखं सन्दर्शयेन्नरः ॥
भूमिहस्ताभिघातेन स्त्रीणां स्याद्रुदितेन तत् ॥। 3.28.40 ॥
आनन्देतिसमुद्भूतं रुदितं द्विविधं स्मृतम् ॥
हृष्टेन चाप्यहृष्टेन तं मुखेन निरूपयेत् ॥ 41 ॥
सम्भ्रमावेगचेष्टाभिः पुरुषाणां भयं भवेत् ॥
त्रातुरन्वेषणादेव उच्चैराक्रन्दितेन च ॥ 42 ॥
नरालिङ्गनतश्चैवं भयं कार्यं भवेत्स्त्रियः ॥
त्रिपताकांगुलीभ्यां तु चलिताभ्यां प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 43 ॥
शुकश्च शारिका चैव सूक्ष्मा ये चैव पक्षिणः ॥
शिखिसारसहंसाद्याः स्थला ये च स्वभावतः ॥ 44 ॥
3.6.m:
An embrace should be performed accompanied by a smile and horripilation. / Joy is [shown] by horripilation, and anger by rolling eyes.
Jealous anger should be enacted devoid of garlands and ornaments, / with a shaking of the head, and likewise with breakdowns of composure.
With face cast down and sighing, a man should display sorrow; / for women, that is [shown] by striking the ground with the hands and by weeping.
Weeping is remembered as twofold: arising from joy [or from grief]. / One should depict it with a joyous or unjoyous face.
Fear of men occurs through gestures of agitation and alarm, / through seeking a protector, and by crying out loudly;
and by embracing a man, fear of women should be performed. / With two trembling tripatāka fingers one should represent
the parrot, the myna, and whatever small birds there are; / peafowl, cranes, swans, and the like, and whatever birds dwell naturally on the ground,

पक्षाङ्गहारैर्द्विविधैस्तैषामभिनयो भवेत्॥
भूताः पिशाचा यक्षाश्च दानवा राक्षसास्तथा ॥ 45 ॥
अङ्गहारैर्विनिर्देश्याः प्रत्यक्षा न भवन्ति ये ॥
प्रत्यक्षा अभिनेयाः स्युस्तथोद्वेगैः सविस्मयैः ॥ 46 ॥
देवान्प्रणामकरणैः प्रत्यक्षे तु नराधिप ॥
परोक्षे विविधैश्चिह्नैस्तथानुकरणैः शुभैः ॥ 47 ॥
सव्योत्थितेन हस्तेन त्वरालेन शिरः स्पृशेत् ॥
नरेभिवादनं ह्येतत्कपोलेन तथा स्त्रियाः ॥ 48 ॥
महाजनं सखिवरं विटधूर्तजनं तथा ॥
परिमण्डलसंज्ञेन हस्तेनाभिनयेद्बुधः ॥ 49 ॥
प्रवृत्तान्प्रांशुयोगेन वृक्षांश्चैव समुत्थितान् ॥
प्रसारिताभ्यां बाहुभ्यामुत्क्षिप्ताभ्यां प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ 3.28.50॥
3.6.m:
their enactment should be made through twofold wing-gestures. / Spirits, piśācas, yakṣas, dānavas, and rākṣasas,
those that are not visible are to be indicated by body-gestures; / those that are visible should be enacted with agitation and wonder.
The gods [are enacted] by making obeisances when they are present, O lord of men; / when absent, by various emblems and auspicious imitations.
With the right hand raised in the arāla gesture one should touch the head; / this is greeting for a man, and on the cheek for a woman.
The wise [actor] should represent a crowd of people, an excellent friend, as well as a gallant or a rogue, / with the hand called parimaṇḍala.
He should display [trees] growing tall / and trees that have sprung up, with both arms stretched out and raised.

( समूहं सुमहत्सेनां बहुविस्तीर्णमेव च ॥
पताकाभ्यां तु हस्ताभ्यां चोत्क्षिप्ताभ्यां प्रदर्शयेत् ॥)
शौर्यं च धैर्यदर्पं च गर्वमौदार्यमुच्छ्रयम् ॥
ललाटस्थानसंस्थेन त्वरालेन प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ 51 ॥
प्रज्ञो देहामदाविद्धौ करौ तु मृगशीर्षकौ ॥
विस्तीर्णप्रद्रुतोत्क्षेपौ योज्यौ यत्स्यादुपावृतम्॥ ॥ 52 ॥
अधोमुखोत्तानतलं हस्तं किंचित्प्रसारितम् ॥
कृत्वा चाभिनयो द्वे च बिलग्राहं गृहं गृहम् ॥ 53 ॥

तेषामभिनयः कार्य उच्छ्वासैः कम्पनैस्तथा ॥54॥
प्रत्यक्षाभिनयः कार्यो दोलायाः परिदोलने ॥
आकाशरचनानीह वक्ष्याम्यात्मगतानि च ॥ 55 ॥
अपवारितकं चैव जनान्तिकमथापि च ॥

अन्यैरश्रवणीयं तु जनान्ति कमिहोच्यते॥
अपवारितकं कर्णे पुनरुक्तं प्रचक्षते॥57॥
3.6.m:
He should display a gathering, a very large army, and something widely spread out / with both hands [in] patāka raised up. / He should display heroism, the arrogance of fortitude, pride, generosity, and high station / with the arāla [hand] placed at the forehead.
The wise [actor] should employ the two mṛgaśīrṣaka hands, drawn back toward the body, / extended, rapid, and tossed upwards, for whatever is open.
Making the hand slightly stretched out with the palm turned downward and upward, / the representation of two [things is made]: catching a creature in a hole, and house by house.
For those afflicted by desire, those with fever, and those whose minds are struck by a curse, / their representation should be done with sighs and with trembling.
A direct representation should be made for swinging on a swing. / Now I shall explain speech addressed to the air and [speeches] kept to oneself.
Aside to one person, speaking into the wing, and also / conversation with another—that is considered speech to the air.
What is inaudible to others is called janāntika here; / apavāritaka is spoken of as repeated in the ear.

3.6.m:
Covering [the mouth] with the hand [held in] tripatāka, actors / should perform janāntika, and likewise apavāritaka.
In the representation of dreaming, it should be with a faltering voice. / For the old, one should employ cunning with faltering, stumbling syllables.
For children, [the voice] has unfinished syllables and sweet tones; / for the sick, one should employ [a voice] accompanied by long sighs and languid.
With a long sigh one should act out the moment of death; / the representation of one who is dead should be by the condition of motionless limbs. / O king, I shall [now] explain sattva-based representation in the sentiments and emotional states.
Only this much in representation can be spoken by me to you, foremost of kings; / for drama is an imitation of the whole universe, so it cannot be spoken in its entirety, O lord.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall explain to you the characteristics of gaits. / In an elevated gait by nature, [the lifting of the foot] should be equal [in height] to the knee and waist.

युद्धचारी प्रचारेषु जानुस्तनसमं न्यसेत् ॥
ज्वरान्ते च क्षुधान्ते च तपःश्रान्ते रुजान्विते ॥ 2 ॥
विकृते चावहित्थे च तथौत्सुक्यसमन्विते ॥
शृङ्गारे चैव शोके च स्वच्छन्द गमने तथा ॥ 3 ॥
एतेष्वेव तु सर्वत्र स्थिरा कार्या गतिर्बुधैः ॥
अस्वस्थे कम्पिते नैव भये वित्रासिते तथा ॥ 4 ॥
आवेगे चैव हर्षे च कार्यं यच्च त्वरान्वितम् ॥
अनिष्टश्रवणे चैव क्षेपे चाद्भुतदर्शने ॥ 5॥
अपि चात्ययिके कार्ये तथा चैवारिमार्गणे ॥
अपराधानुसारेण श्वापदानुगतौ तथा ॥ 6 ॥
एवंविधेषु कार्येषु गतिं शीघ्रां प्रयोजयेत् ॥
गतिः शृङ्गारिणी कार्या स्वस्थकामितसम्भवे ॥ 7 ॥
दूतीदर्शितमार्गस्तु हृद्यवेशपरिक्रमे ॥
ससौष्ठवसमायुक्तैर्लयतालवशोनुगैः ॥ 8 ॥
पादयोरनुगौ चापि हस्तौ कार्यौ प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥
प्रच्छन्नकामिते गच्छन्न चात्यर्थं विभूषितः ॥ 9 ॥
3.6.m:
In the movements of martial steps, one should place the knee level with the chest. / At the end of fever, at the end of hunger, exhausted by asceticism, afflicted with pain,
in transformation, in concealment, and likewise when filled with longing, / in the erotic, in sorrow, and in moving at will—
in all these alone, a steady gait should be executed by the wise. / In uneasiness, in trembling, in fear, in terror,
in agitation, and in joy, and whatever action is hurried, / on hearing what is disagreeable, in tossing about, and on seeing a marvel,
also in urgent business, and likewise in pursuing an enemy, / in following an offense, and in pursuing wild beasts—
in actions of this kind, one should employ a swift gait. / An erotic gait should be used when a composed lover is present.
When the path is shown by a female messenger, in pacing toward a charming house, / endowed with grace, following the rhythm and tempo,
the two hands should also be made by actors to follow the feet. / When going [as] a secret lover, not overly adorned,

विघूर्णितशरीरा च स्तब्धा च शिथिला गतिः ॥ 16 ॥
3.6.m:
wearing dark clothes, with slow steps, constantly fearful of sound, / with body trembling, suspicious, stumbling repeatedly.
The furious is considered threefold: by bodily form, by nature, and by costume. / With his body wet with blood, holding intestines like lotuses as ornaments,
bearing many weapons, he is proclaimed [furious] by the furious costume. / Harsh, speaking with threats, and pitiless by nature—
the gait of the various [types of] furious [character] has an interval of four spans. / Where the ground is unpleasant, crowded with cremation grounds and battle,
near and drawn back, there is the odious gait. / And in the heroic [sentiment], a gait should be performed accompanied by sweeping strides of the feet.
In wonder and in joy, the stride of the feet is cast out; / the gait is declared to have steady steps in the pathetic sentiment.
There no bodily grace is to be shown, nor such measure; / the gait has a swaying body, rigid, and slack.

3.6.m:
For one heavily struck, a gait should be performed with a huddled body. / A swift [gait] should be used in the terrible [sentiment], and a rigid one according to circumstances.
When a deformed creature is seen, the gait has wide-open eyes. / For ascetics, the gait should be slow, with the gaze cast a yoke's length ahead.
In darkness, the gait should also be slow from touching with the hands. / For one standing in a chariot, the gait should be performed with slow steps.
Assuming the samapāda posture of the wise, he should adopt the movement of a chariot, / holding a bow with one hand, and likewise the chariot pole with the other.
And his charioteer should have the appearance of holding a whip. / For one seated in an aerial chariot, the gait should be joyous.
Ascents and descents [are indicated] by movements with upward and downward glances; / moving in the sky should be performed with circular turns.
Falling from the sky should be done with feet coming straight and raised; / climbing high should be performed with step-by-step strides,

अश्वयाने गतिः कार्या वैशाखस्थानकेन ह ॥

कंचुकीयस्य कर्तव्या कम्पिता स्खलिता गतिः ॥28॥
विष्टम्भनगतिप्राणा कृशस्यापि गतिर्भवेत् ॥
व्याधिग्रस्तस्य च तथा तपःश्रान्तस्य चैव हि ॥ 29 ॥
दीर्घाध्वनि गतस्यापि शनैर्मन्दपरिक्रमा ॥
मत्तस्य तु गतिः कार्या स्खलिता पार्श्वयोर्द्वयोः ॥ 3.29.30 ॥
3.6.m:
and descent should be performed with [feet] close together as if apprehensive. / Movement in water should have raised footsteps.
In climbing a tree, there should be movement with raised hands, / with feet crossed, stepped aside, and turned sideways.
By holding a goad, [he indicates] an elephant; by holding a bridle, a horse; / by holding reins, he should represent the gait of others.
In riding a horse, the gait should be executed in the vaiśākha posture; / the gait of serpents should be performed with crossed feet.
For a gallant, the gait should be executed with graceful strides; / for a chamberlain, a trembling and stumbling gait should be performed.
The gait of an emaciated person should be characterized by staggering and halting breaths, / and likewise for one afflicted by disease, and indeed one fatigued from ascetic penance.
And for one who has traversed a long road, [the gait should consist] of walking slowly and sluggishly. / But for an intoxicated person, the gait is to be made staggering to both sides.

श्वापदानां पशूनां च गतिः कार्या नराधिप ॥
शेषाणामर्थयोगेन स्थानकानि प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 35 ॥
धैर्योपपन्ना गतिरुत्तमानां मध्या गतिर्मध्यमसंमितानाम् ॥
द्रुता गतिश्च प्रचुराधमानां लयत्रयं सत्त्ववशेन योज्यम् ॥ 36 ॥
रंगे विकृत्ता तु नृपप्रधान गतागतैः पादगतिप्रचारः ॥
कार्या वशादेव गृहस्य नित्यं समीक्ष्य रङ्गं तु यथानुरूपम् ॥ 37 ॥
3.6.m:
For an insane person as well, the gait is to be made according to theatrical representation; / he should be raving incoherently, dirty, and hairy.
The gait of disabled people should be made according to the requirements of the action; / for a corpulent body, a gait that drags the body is to be performed.
For the vidūṣaka, a gait giving rise to laughter is likewise to be performed, / having placed a natural crook in his left hand.
In walking, servants should take pleasure, and their gaze should be wandering about the noble ones; / [the gaits] of men born in various regions arise from their natural character.
The gait of wild beasts and cattle should be performed [accordingly], O king; / for the rest, one should employ the postures in accordance with the thematic context.
The gait of superior characters is endowed with firmness; the gait of middling characters is moderate; / the gait of common inferior characters is rapid; the three tempos are to be applied according to character.
The movement of footsteps, varying on stage with comings and goings, O foremost of kings, / is always to be done under the control of the stage-space, having properly examined the stage appropriately.

3.6.d:
स्त्रीणां गतिः स्याल्ललितप्रचारा धीरा नराणां च तथोद्धता स्यात् ॥
गति प्रचारोऽर्थवशेन योज्यश्चैतावदुक्तं तव राजसिंह॥38॥
वयोनुरूपः प्रथमस्तु वेशो वेशानुरूपश्च गतिप्रचारः ॥
गतिप्रचारानुगतं च नाट्यं नाट्यानु रूपोऽभिनयश्च कार्यः ॥ 39 ॥
3.30
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
हास्यशृंगारकरुणारौद्रघोरभयानकाः ॥
बीभत्साद्भुतशान्ताख्या नव नाट्ये रसाः स्मृताः ॥ 1 ॥
शान्तो रसः स्वतन्त्रोत्र पृथगेव व्यवस्थितः ॥
शृङ्गाराद्धि भवेद्धास्यो रौद्राच्च करुणोदयः ॥2॥
वीराच्चैवाद्भुतोत्पत्तिर्बीभत्साच्च भयानकः ॥
एतेषामङ्गवर्णाश्च सात्त्विकोभि नयः स्मृतः ॥ 3 ॥
शान्तस्वभाववर्णस्तु रसः प्रोक्तो नराधिप ॥
शृङ्गारस्तु भवेच्छ्यामो रक्तो रौद्रः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 4 ॥
सितो हास्यश्च विज्ञेयः कृष्णश्चैव भयानकः ॥
गौरो वीरस्तु विज्ञेयः पीतश्चैवाद्भुतः स्मृतः ॥ 5 ॥
3.6.m:
The gait of women should have a graceful movement; that of men should be steady and bold; / the movement of gait should be applied according to the context—this much has been told to you, O lion among kings.
First, the costume corresponds to age; and the movement of gait corresponds to the costume; / drama follows the movement of gait; and dramatic representation must be made corresponding to drama.
3.30 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The comic, erotic, pathetic, furious, terrifying, / odious, marvelous, and peaceful: nine rasas are remembered in dramatic art.
The peaceful rasa is autonomous here, established quite distinct; / for from the erotic arises the comic, and from the furious arises the pathetic.
And from the heroic arises the marvelous, and from the odious the terrifying; / their body colors and their dramatic representation are remembered as internal.
The color of the peaceful rasa is declared to be natural, O king; / the erotic is dark blue, and the furious is proclaimed to be red.
The comic is to be known as white, and the terrifying as black; / the heroic is to be known as fair, and the marvelous is recorded as yellow.

3.6.d:
कापोतः करुणश्चैव नीलो बीभत्समेव च ॥
हास्यः प्रमथदेवस्तु शृङ्गारो विष्णुदैवतः ॥ 6 ॥
रौद्रो रौद्राधिदेवश्च करुणो यमदैवतः ॥
बीभत्सस्य महाकालः कालदेवो भयानकः ॥ 7 ॥
वीरो महेन्द्रदेवः स्यादद्भुतो ब्रह्मदैवतः॥ शा
न्तस्य देवो विज्ञेयः परः पुरुष एव तु॥8॥
शान्तस्य तु समुत्पत्तिर्नृप वैराग्यतः स्मृता॥
स चाभिनेयो भवति लिङ्गग्रहणतस्तथा॥9॥
सर्वभूतदयाध्यानमोक्षमार्गप्रर्तनैः॥
नास्ति यत्र सुखं दुःखं न द्वेषो नापि मत्सरः॥3.30.10॥
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु स शान्तः प्रथितो रसः॥
हास्यस्य तु समुत्पत्तिरसम्बद्धप्रलापतः ॥ 11 ॥
असम्बद्धात्तथा वेशाद्भवतीति विनिश्चयः ॥
आत्मस्थश्च परस्थश्च द्विविधः स च कीर्तितः ॥ 12 ॥
आत्मस्थश्च स्वयं हासात्परस्थः परहासनात् ॥
उत्तमाधममुख्यानां त्रिविधः स भवेत्तदा ॥ 13 ॥
3.6.m:
The pathetic is dove-colored, and the odious is blue; / the comic has the pramathas as deity, while the erotic has Viṣṇu as presiding deity.
The furious has Rudra as its presiding deity, and the pathetic has Yama as presiding deity; / Mahākāla is the deity of the odious, and the god of death is the deity of the terrifying.
The heroic has Mahendra as deity, and the marvelous has Brahmā as presiding deity; / the deity of the peaceful is to be known as the Supreme Cosmic Person alone.
The arising of the peaceful, O king, is remembered to be from dispassion; / and it is to be represented through the assumption of ascetic garb,
and through compassion for all beings, meditation, and embarking on the path of liberation; / where there is neither pleasure nor pain, neither hatred nor envy,
and equanimity toward all beings, that celebrated rasa is the peaceful. / The arising of the comic, however, is from incoherent talk,
and it is determined that it arises from improper dress; / and it is proclaimed as twofold: situated in oneself and situated in another.
Situated in oneself is from one's own laughing; situated in another is from making another laugh; / it is then threefold for superior, inferior, and middling characters.

3.6.d:
ईषद्विकम्पितैर्गण्डैः कटाक्षैस्सौष्ठवान्वितैः ॥
अलक्षितद्विजं चैव उत्तमानां स्मितं भवेत् ॥ 14 ॥
तथा दर्शितदन्तन्तु मध्यमानां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
सास्रं तदधमानां स्यात्सस्वनं च महीभुजाम् ॥ 15 ॥
शृङ्गारो द्विविधः प्रोक्तः सम्भोगाद्विरहात्तथा ॥
विप्रलम्भकृतस्यात्र निर्वेदोऽभिनयक्रियः ॥ 16 ॥
विप्रलम्भे तु निर्दिष्टाः कामावस्थास्तथा दश ॥
चक्षुःप्रीतिर्विनिर्दिष्टा प्रथमायां नराधिप ॥ 17 ॥
मनसश्च तथा सङ्गो द्वितीयायां प्रकीर्तितः ॥
स्मरणं च तथा प्रोक्तं तृतीयायां निरन्तरम् ॥ 18 ॥
निद्राभेदश्चतुर्थ्यां तु पंचम्यां तनुता तथा ॥
व्यावृत्तिविषयेभ्यस्तु षष्ठ्यां प्रोक्ता नराधिप ॥ 19 ॥
लज्जाप्रणाशः सप्तम्यामुन्मादस्तदनन्तरम् ॥
नवम्यां तु तथा मूर्च्छा दशम्यां मरणं भवेत् ॥3.30.20॥
3.6.m:
With slightly trembling cheeks, with glances endowed with grace, / and with teeth unseen, is the smile of superior persons.
Showing the teeth is described for middling persons; / for inferior persons, it is with tears and with sound, O king.
The erotic is declared to be twofold: from union and from separation; / in the case of that caused by separation in love, world-weariness is the mode of representation.
In separation in love, ten stages of passion are designated; / pleasure of the eyes is designated as the first, O king,
and attachment of the mind is declared in the second; / and continuous recollecting is declared in the third.
Disruption of sleep is in the fourth, and emaciation in the fifth; / turning away from sense objects is stated in the sixth, O king;
loss of shame is in the seventh; madness immediately after that; / fainting in the ninth; and death would be in the tenth.

3.6.d:
द्वयोरुज्ज्वलयोस्तत्र सम्भोगाभिनयो भवेत ॥
सुखप्रायेष्टसंपन्नो यत्र माल्यानुलेपकः ॥ 21॥
पुरुषप्रमदायुग्मं शृंगार इति संज्ञितः ॥
शोकाद्भवति राजेन्द्र तथैव करुणो रसः ॥ 22 ॥
त्रस्तगात्राद्विनिःश्वासपरिदेवितरोदनैः ॥
मुखवैवर्ण्य शोषैश्च तस्येहाभिनयो भवेत् ॥ 23 ॥
क्रोधाद्भवति रौद्रस्य रसस्य तु समुद्भवः ॥
रक्तत्वनेत्रभ्रुकुटिक्रोधामर्षैः ससाहसैः ॥ 24 ॥
पीडनैः शस्त्रसङ्घातैस्तस्येहाभिनयो भवेत ॥
जुगुप्सया भवति बीभत्सस्य समुद्भवः ॥ 25 ॥
नासाविघूर्णनात्तस्य चोद्वेगेन तथैव च ॥
आश्चर्येण समुत्पत्तिरद्भुतं तत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 26 ॥
प्रस्फुरिताक्षिरोमाञ्चैरङ्गुलीभ्रमणादिभिः ॥
स्वेदेन चाभिनेयः स्यादद्भुतस्तु तथा रसः ॥ 27 ॥
3.6.m:
There, the representation of union is between two radiant lovers, / where there are garlands and unguents, abounding in pleasure and endowed with desired objects.
The union of a man and a woman is called the erotic; / from grief, O king of kings, the pathetic rasa likewise arises.
Its dramatic representation here is by trembling limbs, sighs, lamentations, weeping, / loss of facial color, and drying up [of the mouth].
The arising of the furious rasa takes place from anger; / by red eyes, knit brows, rage, intolerance, along with reckless deeds,
by oppression, and by clashing of weapons, its representation is done here; / the arising of the odious takes place from disgust.
Its [representation is] by turning away the nose and likewise by agitation; / the marvelous is proclaimed as having its origin from astonishment.
With wide-open eyes, horripilation, rotating of the fingers and so forth, / and with perspiration, the marvelous rasa is likewise to be represented.

3.6.s:
nāṭyasya mūlaṃ tu rasaḥ pradiṣṭo rasena hīnaṃ na hi vṛttamasti ..
tasmātprayatnena rasāśrayasya vṛttasya yatnaṃ puruṣeṇa kāryam .. 28 ..
3.6.d:
नाट्यस्य मूलं तु रसः प्रदिष्टो रसेन हीनं न हि वृत्तमस्ति ॥
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन रसाश्रयस्य वृत्तस्य यत्नं पुरुषेण कार्यम् ॥ 28 ॥
3.6.m: Rasa is declared to be the root of dramatic art, for no dramatic plot exists devoid of rasa; / therefore, an effort must be made by a person with great care concerning a plot that has rasa as its foundation.
